> `( identifier constant_bit_select dot &( identifier constant_bit_select dot ) )*`.
> `ral.arr[0].g()` with `ral` a subroutine formal went **REJECT `pos=750` → ACCEPT** — and so did
> `top.u1[0].t;`, an IEEE **1364-2005** §12.4 / A.9.3 indexed hierarchical task enable that had been
> rejecting in PLAIN VERILOG, on all three profiles, with nothing pointing at it.
>
> ⭐⭐⭐ **THE GUARD COULD NEVER PASS, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DEFECT.** The loop's negative lookahead
> `!callable_method_call_body` was meant to stop the receiver before the method name. But IEEE 1800
> A.8.2 writes `array_manipulation_call ::= array_method_name { attribute_instance }
> [ ( list_of_arguments ) ] [ with ( expression ) ]` — **the parens are OPTIONAL** — so a bare member
> name `arr` already IS a `callable_method_call_body`, and the lookahead fired on *every* identifier.
> ⇒ the loop ran **zero iterations for its entire life**, and the rule degenerated to
> `qual? identifier constant_bit_select` — a ONE-component receiver. Multi-component receivers
> survived only through `method_call`'s `( dot method_call_body )*` chain, which carries no
> bit-select. That is exactly why `a.b.g()` parsed and `a.b[0].g()` did not: the chain could carry
> the extra `.member` but not the `[0]`.
>
> ⛔⛔ **A DEAD GUARD AND AN UNNEEDED LOOP ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM OUTSIDE.** Nothing in the
> repository could see this: the rule parsed, its tests passed, `--lint-grammar` had no complaint,
> and the branch was SELECTED on every method call — it simply never took the one path it existed
> to take. The instrument that names it did not exist and now does (below).
>
> ⚠️ **THE INHERITED DIAGNOSIS WAS RE-DERIVED AND IT NAMED THE WRONG RULE.** This leaf was opened
> with the mechanism *"`method_call_receiver_sv_2017` branch 2/14 reaches the un-fact-gated
> `hierarchical_sequence_identifier` arm, which consumes `ral.arr[0].g` including the method name"*.
> On HEAD `hierarchical_sequence_identifier` is **not on the path at all** — it appears in the trace
> only inside the `[0]` index expression, and the receiver that wins is
> `split_direct_callable_method_call`'s. ⇒ **a mechanism note ages like a hypothesis**; the seven
> days between opening and fixing included the LR-elimination rule split that renamed the path.
> Re-derive from the trace, never from the leaf.

**THE LRM ADJUDICATION — THREE AUTHORITIES, all in-repo, read rather than inferred.**
`split_hierarchical_callable_receiver` carries **no `@profiles` gate**, and neither does anything
above it on the path (`subroutine_call`, `method_call`, `method_call_initial`, `call_primary`), so
this is a three-profile change by construction — the `.13c.2h`/`-0226` rule, applied before the fix
this time rather than after.

| authority | production | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| IEEE 1800-2017 A.8.2 / A.8.4 (`docs/systemverilog/2017/md`) | `method_call_root ::= primary \| implicit_class_handle`, `primary ::= … \| [ class_qualifier \| package_scope ] hierarchical_identifier select \| …` | the receiver is a full `primary`; `ral.arr[0]` is `hierarchical_identifier` + `select` |
| IEEE 1800-2023 A.8.2 / A.8.4 (`docs/systemverilog/2023/md/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax.md:2942,3083`) | identical, production for production | same |
| IEEE 1364-2005 A.9.3 / A.6.9 / A.8.2 (`docs/verilog/2005/md/section-Annex_A-…:1260,776,1036`) | `hierarchical_identifier ::= { identifier [ [ constant_expression ] ] . } identifier`; `task_enable ::= hierarchical_task_identifier [ ( … ) ] ;`; `function_call ::= hierarchical_function_identifier { attribute_instance } ( … )` | `top.u1[0].t;` is legal PLAIN VERILOG — §12.4 hierarchical names over an instance array |

⇒ every authority admits an indexed component in the middle of a hierarchical name in a call
position. The rejection was under-acceptance on all three, and the v2005 leg had **no owning leaf
and no reproducer** until this slice — it was found by asking the third authority a question the
SV-shaped reproducers could not ask.

**THE SWEEP — the class, not the instance** (`docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/dead_negative_lookahead/`).
The `.13c.2e` lesson is explicit: `SV-0049` fixed one brace mis-transcription and did not sweep its
class, which is the only reason `.13c.2e` existed three days later. So this leaf ships the sweep as
an instrument rather than as a resolution. `sweep_dead_guards.py` asks, of every negative lookahead
in the SV grammar, whether its subject accepts a **bare simple identifier** — the shape that kills a
guard standing where an identifier is legal — and it decides by PARSING (TOOLBOX 1.5b
`--interpret-entry-rule`), not by reading:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `!R` guard subjects probed | 8 | 7 |
| inline `!( … )` group guards, reported not probed | 5 | 5 |
| ⛔ **DEAD-RISK** — subject accepts a bare identifier | **1** (`callable_method_call_body`, line 3312) | **0** |

⇒ **`callable_method_call_body` was the only one.** The class is closed, and the sweep is
re-runnable rather than a paragraph. ⛔ Four controls run before any verdict prints (`identifier`
must accept `x`; `lparen` must reject it; every named subject must resolve to a rule head; the
grammar must yield at least one `!` site), and it was **proven able to fail**: pointed at the
pre-fix grammar with `--grammar` it exits 1 with `dead_risk=1 -> callable_method_call_body`, naming
the exact line the trace had independently named. Honest bound, printed rather than hidden: it
decides ONE shape, and the inline `!( … )` group forms have no rule name to enter, so they are
listed in full instead of probed.

⛔ **A SECOND LRM DIVERGENCE WAS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED — because the measurement refuted
my own first hypothesis.** `method_call_receiver_sv_2017`/`_sv_2023` is a hand-copied cut of
`primary_sv_2017`/`_sv_2023` that dropped **two** things: `select` (present in A.8.4) and the
`class_scope` branch of `primary_hier_scope_prefix` (added by `SV-EXH-PROOF.3.3.4.b.6.2.37.3`).
Restoring `select` was this slice's FIRST candidate fix, and it is LRM-faithful — but measured on
an 18-row probe suite it changed **nothing**, in either direction, because `hierarchical_identifier`'s
own greedy `( identifier constant_bit_select dot )*` had already swallowed `ral.arr[0].g` before
`select` was ever reached. ⇒ **an LRM-faithful change with no measured effect is still a widening
with a risk profile** (`.13c.2f`'s "no demonstrated defect ⇒ do not write it" rule), so the
divergence is ROUTED as `.13c.2j` with its measurement attached rather than bundled here.

**ROUTING EVIDENCE** (`ROUTING-EVIDENCE` doctrine — measured OUTSIDE the family before routing):
this leaf sends one finding out of `SV-CORPUS-GRAD` to `LANG-CAPABILITY-AUDIT.10.18` — *PGEN's `*`,
`+` and `?` are possessive; a quantifier never gives back*. (⛔ This paragraph first said `*` and
`+`; `?` was measured under director challenge on 2026-08-18 and behaves identically — see that
leaf's correction block.) **Does it reproduce outside
SystemVerilog? Yes, and with no SystemVerilog in it at all.** On the five-line synthetic
`s := ( a )* a b` (`docs/tasks/artifacts/lang_capability_audit/possessive_quantifier/`), input `ab`
→ `accepted=false furthest_position=1` and `aab` → `accepted=false furthest_position=2`; both are in
the language the grammar declares, and a backtracking `*` accepts each. ⇒ the subject is the ENGINE's
quantifier contract, which binds all 11 shipped families, not an SV grammar defect. What stays here
is the SV consequence: the four hand-written lookaheads `grammars/systemverilog.ebnf` carries to work
around it, one of which (`!callable_method_call_body`) was written wrong and is what this leaf fixes.
The two findings routed to `.13c.2j` / `.13c.2k` stay INSIDE this tree — both are SV grammar defects
with SV reproducers — so they are intra-tree bookkeeping, not routing. ⛔ The SV-side count this
leaf published — *"four hand-written lookaheads"* — was **counted from the sites this leaf walked
past, not enumerated**, and is corrected to **six inside a repetition / eight including optionals**
in `LANG-CAPABILITY-AUDIT.10.18`'s census table. The error was in the direction that made the
routed finding look smaller.

- **MEASURED, on the shipped parser, BEFORE and AFTER `.13c.2c`** (so it is pre-existing and the
  `.13c.2c` fix neither caused nor cured it):
  `tmp` repro `class inner; function int g(); return 0; endfunction endclass / class rb; inner arr[2]; endclass /
  class w; function int f(rb ral); return ral.module[0].g(); endfunction endclass` → **ACCEPT** on
  `sv_2017` and `sv_2023`, both parser states.
- **WHY IT IS A DEFECT.** IEEE 1800-2017 §B (Keywords) reserves `module`; A.9.3 gives
  `identifier ::= simple_identifier | escaped_identifier` and §5.6.2 forbids a reserved word as a
  simple identifier. There is no derivation of `ral.module[0]` — accepting it is **over-acceptance**,
  the failure mode the strict-LRM default exists to prevent.
- ⚠️ **The suspect is the `identifier` vs `non_keyword_identifier` split**: `hierarchical_identifier`
  guards only its FINAL component (`non_keyword_identifier`), while every component inside its
  `( identifier constant_bit_select dot )*` loop — and inside
  `split_hierarchical_callable_receiver`'s loop — is the unguarded `identifier`. ⛔ That is a
  HYPOTHESIS, not a diagnosis: it has not been run through the toolbox, and this leaf may not be
  fixed until it has been (TOOLBOX-FIRST).
- ⛔⛔ **AND THE ORACLE CANNOT HOLD THIS ROW UNTIL IT IS FIXED — a gap in the ratchet itself, found
  by trying to pin it.** `stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/MANIFEST.tsv` has four classes: `defect`
  (valid SV, currently rejected), `invalid` (illegal text, correctly rejected), `control`, `fixed`.
  There is **no class for illegal text that is currently ACCEPTED**. Filing this as `invalid`
  expects REJECT and so goes RED on the commit that files it; filing it as anything else lies. ⇒ a
  known over-acceptance can be written in prose here and nowhere the runner can see it, which is the
  exact asymmetry that lets an accepts-invalid defect age quietly while every rejects-valid defect
  is ratcheted. The missing class (`accepts_invalid`, expect ACCEPT, failing loudly the day it
  starts REJECTing — the mirror of `defect`) is part of what this leaf owes.
- [x] ⭐⭐ **DIAGNOSIS — the leaf's hypothesis was RIGHT, and the position matrix says exactly how far
  it reaches.** Measured on the shipped parser, `sv_2017` and `sv_2023`, every row a separate file
  pinned in `MANIFEST.tsv`:

  | where `module` sits | verdict | why |
  |---|---|---|
  | non-final component, indexed — `ral.module[0].g()` | **ACCEPT** ⛔ | the loop spells raw `identifier` |
  | non-final component, plain — `ral.module.g()` | **ACCEPT** ⛔ | the bit-select is not what admits it |
  | FIRST component — `module.g()` | **ACCEPT** ⛔ | not a member-position special case |
  | method name — `ral.arr[0].module()` | REJECT ✅ | `callable_identifier := non_keyword_identifier` |
  | final component — `ral.arr[0].module` | REJECT ✅ | `hierarchical_identifier`'s tail is guarded |
  | declared name — `int module;` | REJECT ✅ | `declaration_identifier := non_keyword_identifier` |
  | control — `ral.modxx[0].g()` | ACCEPT ✅ | legal SV; one identifier changed |

  parser previously accepted one does not end a parse — it sends the PEG engine back to try further
  alternatives, each of which re-enters `identifier`/`non_keyword_identifier` at new positions.
  **Rejection is not free: it buys more speculation.** The price instrument asked *"where does the
  lookahead execute"* and answered it correctly; it could not ask *"what does the parser do
  differently when that lookahead says no"* — and that second question is where the cost lives.
  ⇒ [[a-strictness-fix-redirects-the-search-not-just-the-predicate]].

#### ✅✅ `.13c.2m` — **`done`** 2026-09-23 (opened 2026-08-18 by `.13c.2j`; `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0413`, release `1.0.244`, ledger `SV-0129`, contract `1.0.244`, **AST schema 33 → 34**; GRAMMAR tier, ZERO Rust / codegen / engine bytes; `1738 → 1735` rules) — **THE LRM-EXTRACTION PSEUDO-KEYWORDS ARE DELETED: `class_qualifier` (an Annex A NONTERMINAL welded into a keyword by one lost colon) AND THE FOOTNOTE SUPERSCRIPTS `43` / `48` LEAVE THE GRAMMAR; THE LRM's `local ::` BEFORE A TYPE NAME IS RENDERED.** The record below this heading is the leaf's own history — how the weld was found, measured with one-identifier controls, proved by the edition difference and reproduced by running the extractor. This release lands (d) the fix, (b) and (c) its two owed measurements, and the six pinned rows flip.
- **HISTORY (the record as opened 2026-08-18 by `.13c.2j`, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0229`; the discharges and the routing note below are that record's own):**

- **HOW IT WAS FOUND.** `.13c.2j` had to read the canonical rendering of A.8.4's
  `[ class_qualifier | package_scope ]` to know what the copies were missing, and the first branch of
  every rendering is `kw_class_qualifier_fa08937d` — which resolves to
  `grammars/systemverilog.ebnf:6518`: `kw_class_qualifier_fa08937d := trivia /class_qualifier\b/`.
  A literal keyword. IEEE 1800 has no such keyword; `class_qualifier` is a NONTERMINAL with its own
  production. Confirmed against the in-repo LRMs, not from memory:
  `docs/systemverilog/2017/txt/section-41-data-read-api.txt:1967` and
  `docs/systemverilog/2023/txt/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax.txt:1987`.
- ⛔⛔ **MEASURED ON THE SHIPPED PARSER, WITH ONE-IDENTIFIER CONTROLS** (three profiles; every row is now a PINNED reproducer in
  `stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/` — `.13c.2k` built the `accepts_invalid` class that can hold them,
  so these verdicts are re-run by the oracle rather than quoted from this table):

  | input | `sv_2017` | `sv_2023` | `verilog_2005` |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `y = class_qualifier m;` | **ACCEPT** | **ACCEPT** | REJECT |
  | `y = foo_qualifier m;` (control — one identifier changed) | REJECT | REJECT | REJECT |
  | `y = null class_qualifier:=;` | **ACCEPT** | **ACCEPT** | REJECT |
  | `y = null foo_qualifier:=;` (control) | REJECT | REJECT | REJECT |
  | `y = null class_qualifier:=local::43;` | **ACCEPT** | REJECT | REJECT |
  | `y = null class_qualifier:=local::48;` | REJECT | **ACCEPT** | REJECT |

  None of these six is derivable from Annex A. Every ACCEPT is an over-acceptance, and the controls
  isolate each one to the literal spelling `class_qualifier`.
- ⭐⭐⭐ **THE LAST TWO ROWS ARE THE ROOT CAUSE, PROVED BY THE EDITION DIFFERENCE.** The LRM text runs:

  ```text
  | this41
  | $42
  | null
  class_qualifier := [ local ::43 ] [ implicit_class_handle . | class_scope ]
  ```

  The extractor did not see a production boundary — the text dump renders `::=` as `:=` — so it
  welded the ENTIRE `class_qualifier` definition line onto `primary`'s final `| null` alternative,
  and turned the footnote superscript `43` into a token. That is exactly what the grammar carries
  today, at four sites (`:3361`, `:3378`, `:4509`, `:4572`):

  ```text
  kw_null_2be88ca4 kw_class_qualifier_fa08937d colon assign
      ( kw_local_939bb46a scope_resolution kw_n_43_0286dd55 )? ( instance_or_class_scope )?
  ```

  with `kw_n_43_0286dd55 := trivia /43\b/` (`:6814`). ⛔ **1800-2023 renumbers that footnote to 48**,
  and PGEN's sv_2023 variants carry `kw_n_48_64e095fe := trivia /48\b/` (`:6829`) — which is why the
  `43` form parses only under `sv_2017` and the `48` form only under `sv_2023`. Two editions, two
  footnote numbers, two literal tokens: the mangle is not a hypothesis, it is reproduced twice with
  the discriminator the LRM itself supplies.
- **WHAT THIS COSTS, in both directions.**
  1. **Over-acceptance** — the six rows above, on the strict-LRM-by-default profiles.
  2. **A production that was never rendered** — `class_qualifier`'s real body,
     `[ local :: ] [ implicit_class_handle . | class_scope ]`, has no rule. The canonical
     `primary_hier_scope_prefix` carries the corpse (`kw_class_qualifier_fa08937d`) plus a
     `class_scope` branch bolted on later by `SV-EXH-PROOF.3.3.4.b.6.2.37.3`; the `local ::`
     qualifier of §18.7.1 is not rendered at all in that position. ⚠️ Whether that is an
     over-REJECTION is NOT yet measured and this leaf may not claim it — `local::x` inside
     `randomize() with { … }` needs its own probe.
  3. `.13c.2j`'s rendering-drift sweep asserts the four renderings AGREE; one member of what they
     agree on is this defect, which the sweep's README states rather than implies.

  re-reading it turned up a THIRD marker, `29`, in a completely different production — and unlike the

  | `covergroup extends base;29` — the same text with the FOOTNOTE NUMBER typed in | REJECT ✅ | **ACCEPT** ⛔ |
  | `covergroup base; endgroup` (control — plain covergroup, same carrier) | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |

  production derives. **This is a REJECTS-VALID defect** — the axis the Nexsim release bar is

  1800-2023's Annex A and **nowhere** in the 1800-2017 source (`grep` over both, 1 hit vs 0).

  kw_n_29_7719a1c7 coverage_spec_or_option* kw_endgroup …`.

  (`covergroup cg extends base;`) the branch fails at `❌ Regex 'extends\b' no match at position 52
  (next: 'cg extends')`, which is the LRM being right — the derived covergroup carries no new name —
  and is why the first attempt to reproduce this used the wrong input and had to be bisected.

  orphaned token definition removed, so the fix leaves no unreachable rule behind); positional refs

#### ⚠️ `.13c.2p` NEW `todo` — the footnote-marker census is a HAND count, and a hand count of a class is the shape that rots (opened 2026-08-18 session #246 by `.13c.2o`, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0232`)

- ⭐ **Re-measured 2026-10-09 by `.51` — STILL OPEN, and now COUNTED.** No tracked census derives the `kw_n_<digits>_<hash>` adjudication (`ls docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad | grep -i 'foot\|marker'` → nothing); the 5-legitimate / 3-marker reading above is still the hand count this leaf exists to replace; no commit names the leaf. A `####` leaf the `#####`-only census never read.
- **WHAT IT IS.** `.13c.2o` decided, by reading, which of the grammar's `kw_n_<digits>_<hash>` tokens
  are legitimate LRM literals and which are footnote markers the extractor mistook for syntax. The
  answer today is **5 legitimate** — `0`/`1`/`2` (`finish_number`, `level_symbol`, `assert #0`) and
  `01`/`10` (`edge_descriptor`, A.7.4) — and **3 markers**: `43` (1800-2017), `48` (1800-2023), `29`
  (the covergroup one, now fixed).
- ⛔ **WHY IT IS A LEAF AND NOT A PARAGRAPH.** `.13c.2m` published *"every `kw_n_<digits>_<hash>` rule
  … is a footnote marker by construction"* and that was **wrong for five of eight**. The corrected
  census is better but has the same defect in waiting: it is a judgement made once, written in prose,
  and re-checked by nobody. The `.13c.2e` rule applies — one instance is never the class — and so
  does the `-0228`/`-0231` rule: a hand count is a claim.
- ⭐ **AND IT IS MECHANISABLE, which is why it is worth doing rather than re-reading.** Both LRM
  sources are TRACKED in this repository. For a token `kw_n_<D>_<hash>`, the question *"is `<D>` a
  footnote marker or a grammar literal?"* is answerable from those sources: a marker appears
  **immediately after a token with no separating space** in an Annex A production line (`;29`,
  `::43`, `this41`, `$42`) and its digits appear again at the start of a footnote line (`29) The
  extends specification …`). A literal appears as a standalone alternative (`| 0`, `| 01`). ⇒ the
  instrument reads the production line and the footnote block rather than the analyst's memory.
- **WHAT THIS LEAF OWES**: (a) that instrument, with controls that make it able to go RED (a
  legitimate literal reclassified as a marker must fail; a known marker must be found); (b) a run
  over the CURRENT grammar with the verdict for all 8 tokens; (c) the same question asked of the
  `kw_<name>_<hash>` family — is `<name>` an Annex A NONTERMINAL rather than an Annex B keyword? —
  which is `.13c.2m`'s outstanding sweep half and shares this machinery exactly.
- ⚠️ **BOUND.** This decides *which tokens came from footnotes*. It does not decide whether a marker
  is HARMFUL: `43`/`48` sit in optional groups and only over-accept, while `29` was mandatory and
  rejected a legal construct. The instrument should report the position class alongside the verdict,
  because that is what ranks the fixes.

#### ✅ `.13c.2q` `done` — EIGHT gate/switch keywords lost their trailing DIGIT in extraction, so `bufif0`, `bufif1`, `notif0`, `notif1`, `tranif0`, `tranif1`, `rtranif0`, `rtranif1` cannot be parsed as gates at all (opened 2026-08-18 session #247 by `.13c.2k`'s sweep, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0233`)

- ⛔⛔ **HOW IT WAS FOUND — by a fix REGRESSING the corpus, not by looking for it.** `.13c.2k`'s
  candidate grammar (the reserved-word exclusion moved into `identifier`) was A/B'd against the
  baseline over 245 currently-PASSING corpus files on the interpreter. Two moved to REJECT. One,
  `ispras-sv-tests/ieee-1364-2005/test_07_01_06_2.v`, stops at `bufif0 ar[3:0](out, in, en);` —
  IEEE 1364-2005 §7.1.6's own worked example. ⇒ that file was only ever parsing because a RESERVED
  KEYWORD could stand in for a UDP type name, and closing that hole exposed a **rejects-valid**
  defect underneath it. *An over-acceptance was load-bearing for a construct the parser could not
  otherwise reach.*
- **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE) — read off the grammar and confirmed against all THREE tracked LRMs.**

  ```text
  $ grep -n "enable_gatetype\|pass_en_switchtype" grammars/systemverilog.ebnf
  2410:enable_gatetype := kw_bufif_8c9c7ee6 -> {kind: "bufif"}
  2411:                | kw_notif_8743f903 -> {kind: "notif"}
  4470:pass_en_switchtype := kw_tranif_02d116e0 -> {kind: "tranif"}
  4471:                   | kw_rtranif_75c812fc -> {kind: "rtranif"}
  6585:kw_bufif_8c9c7ee6 := trivia /bufif\b/
  6898:kw_notif_8743f903 := trivia /notif\b/
  7143:kw_tranif_02d116e0 := trivia /tranif\b/
  ```

  The standards write **four** alternatives each, and every one carries a trailing digit:

  | LRM source (tracked, in repo) | production |
  |---|---|
  | `docs/verilog/2005/txt/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax-definition.txt:382` | `enable_gatetype ::= bufif0 \| bufif1 \| notif0 \| notif1` |
  | `docs/systemverilog/2017/txt/section-28-gate-level-and-switch-level-modeling.txt:86` | same |
  | `docs/systemverilog/2023/txt/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax.txt:1150` | same |
  | `docs/verilog/2005/txt/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax-definition.txt:386` | `pass_en_switchtype ::= tranif0 \| tranif1 \| rtranif1 \| rtranif0` |

  The extraction collapsed each pair/quad to its common ALPHABETIC STEM and dropped the digits, so
  the grammar holds `bufif` / `notif` / `tranif` / `rtranif` — **four tokens where the LRM has
  eight, and not one of the four can ever match**: `/bufif\b/` requires a word boundary after
  `bufif`, and in `bufif0` the next character is `0`, which is a word character. ⇒ the token is
  unmatchable by construction, and so are `enable_gatetype`, `pass_en_switchtype` and both
  `gate_instantiation_sv_*` alternatives that reference them.
  ⭐ Note the contrast that makes this a *targeted* extraction failure rather than a general one:
  `n_input_gatetype` (`and|nand|or|nor|xor|xnor`), `mos_switchtype` (`nmos|pmos|rnmos|rpmos`),
  `cmos_switchtype` and `pass_switchtype` are all COMPLETE and all work. The collapse happened
  exactly where the alternatives differ ONLY by a trailing digit.
- ⛔ **MEASURED, on the interpreter, both arms, correct ARITY per A.3.1** — the first cut of this
  matrix used the wrong arity for six gates and reported ten defects where there are eight, which is
  the `.13c.2d` false-positive shape and is why the arities are spelled out here:

  | gate | probe | baseline verdict | baseline ARM |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `and` (n_input, 3 terminals) | `and g1(o, i, e);` | ACCEPT | `gate_instantiation` ✅ |
  | `bufif0` (enable, 3) | `bufif0 g1(o, i, e);` | ACCEPT | **`udp_instantiation`** ⛔ |
  | `nmos` (mos, 3) | `nmos g1(o, i, e);` | ACCEPT | `gate_instantiation` ✅ |
  | `cmos` (cmos, 4) | `cmos g1(o, i, e, c);` | ACCEPT | `gate_instantiation` ✅ |
  | `tran` (pass, 2) | `tran g1(o, i);` | ACCEPT | `gate_instantiation` ✅ |
  | `tranif0` (pass_en, 3) | `tranif0 g1(o, i, e);` | ACCEPT | **`udp_instantiation`** ⛔ |
  | `pullup` (pull, 1) | `pullup g1(o);` | ACCEPT | `gate_instantiation` ✅ |

  ⇒ every affected form parses today as a **UDP instantiation whose type name is a reserved
  keyword**. The verdict is ACCEPT either way, so no verdict-only oracle in this repository could
  see it — the `arm` column (`.13c.2a.2`) is the only instrument that can, and this is its second
  independent justification.
- **THE FIX** — restore the LRM's own alternatives: `bufif0`/`bufif1`, `notif0`/`notif1`,
  `tranif0`/`tranif1`, `rtranif0`/`rtranif1`, each as its own token, in all three profiles
  (the productions are identical in 1364-2005 and both 1800 editions, so no `@profiles` gate).
- ⛔ **SEQUENCING — THIS BLOCKS `.13c.2k`.** `.13c.2k` cannot land until the gate route can reach
  these forms, because otherwise its (correct) narrowing converts eight masked defects into corpus
  regressions. `.13c.2r` blocks it for the same reason.

#### ✅ `.13c.2r` `done` — a GREEDY `( X )*` immediately before a MANDATORY `X`-shaped tail is unmatchable, and it makes `buf` and `not` gate instantiations unreachable (opened 2026-08-18 session #247 by `.13c.2k`'s sweep, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0233`)

- **HOW IT WAS FOUND.** The same A/B as `.13c.2q`. Once the eight digit-suffixed keywords were
  explained, `buf` and `not` still moved — and their tokens (`/buf\b/`, `/not\b/`) are correct and
  their `n_output_gatetype` rule is complete. So the defect is not in the keyword.
- **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — `grammars/systemverilog.ebnf:3762`:

  ```text
  n_output_gate_instance := ( name_of_instance )? lparen output_terminal ( comma output_terminal )* comma input_terminal rparen
  ```

  The `( comma output_terminal )*` is greedy and `output_terminal` and `input_terminal` match the
  same texts, so the star consumes the **mandatory** trailing `comma input_terminal` and the
  sequence then fails with no input left to satisfy it. The engine does not backtrack into a
  committed `*`, so the rule cannot match ANY input.
  ⭐ Its sibling `n_input_gate_instance:3752` has the star **at the end**
  (`… output_terminal comma input_terminal ( comma input_terminal )* rparen`) and works — which is
  exactly why `and`/`nand`/`or`/`nor`/`xor`/`xnor` were unaffected.
- ⛔ **THE MECHANISM IS ISOLATED ON AN 8-LINE SCRATCH GRAMMAR, not argued from PEG folklore**
  (`docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/gate_route_unmasking/star_starve.ebnf` and its `_tail`
  twin, driven by TOOLBOX 1.5b `--interpret-parse`):

  | grammar shape | `(o, i)` | `(o, p, i)` |
  |---|---|---|
  | `out ( comma out )* comma inp` — the `n_output` shape | **REJECT** | **REJECT** |
  | `out comma inp ( comma inp )*` — the `n_input` shape | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |

  Two inputs, two grammars, one difference: where the star sits. Nothing about SystemVerilog is
  involved, which is what makes it a CLASS rather than an instance.
- **THE FIX** — respell the sequence so the star cannot starve the tail. IEEE 1364-2005 A.3.1 writes
  `n_output_gate_instance ::= [ name_of_instance ] ( output_terminal { , output_terminal } ,
  input_terminal )`, i.e. "one or more outputs then exactly one input"; the derivation-equivalent
  PEG spelling puts the repetition where it cannot swallow the tail.
- ⭐ **AND THE CLASS IS SWEPT, because one instance is never the class here (`.13c.2e`).** This leaf
  owes a re-runnable census of every `( … )*` in the grammar whose repeated body can also match the
  MANDATORY element that follows it — the shape that is unmatchable by construction — and a verdict
  for each hit. `--lint-grammar` reports `nullable_repetition` but has no check for this, so the
  census is the durable half and the `buf`/`not` fix is the acute one.

  ```text
  system_tf_call := …
                  | system_tf_identifier lparen expression ( comma ( expression )? )* ( comma ( clocking_event )? )? rparen
  ```

  IEEE 1800-2017 A.8.2 writes

  `( comma ( expression )? )*` consumes the comma before `@(posedge clk)`; its inner `( expression )?`

  separator, and `( comma ( clocking_event )? )?` — which now needs a comma and sees `@` — takes zero
  iterations. `rparen` is then required against `@` and the alternative fails.

  the rule was unmatchable for every input; here it is OPTIONAL, so the rule still matches — it just
  can never reach the clocking-event form. A verdict-only oracle sees a REJECT here and saw nothing
  at all there.

  unchanged, because the starved follower is optional and the star's own body is nullable; decide
  the spelling against the LRM's derivation and prove it on the pinned pair; (b) a check that the
  other two `system_tf_call` alternatives still route the inputs they route today (the `arm` column);

  naming the next thing owed: the working-tree digest not matching any register row, then the
  contract declaring a different digest from the register's newest row, then passing only once
  release `1.0.191`, the register row and ledger rows `SV-0063`/`SV-0064` all existed.
  ⛔ **The gap: tier A was keyed on the COMMIT SHA, and the row for the commit being made cannot
  carry that commit's own sha.** Tier D forced the row to exist; tier A would then have rejected it
  on the NEXT commit and demanded a fixup. Tier A is now keyed on the **DIGEST**, which is known
  before the commit is and is the identity the contract actually describes; `commit` became
  documentation, and the `(pending)` placeholder that digest-keying makes necessary is itself GATED —
  once its commit exists the doctrine demands the back-fill, because a reminder has already lost
  1 592 times in this repository. *A gate is not finished until it has been driven through a real
  change.*
- ⭐⭐ **AND THE RE-KEYING SILENTLY DISARMED ONE OF THE PROBE'S OWN ARMS, WHICH IS WHY THE PROBE IS
  RE-RUN RATHER THAN TRUSTED.** Tier A's adversarial arm deleted `e28cc856`'s register row and
  expected a breach. Under digest-keying that row is a comment-only revision whose digest its
  predecessor still records, so the tier correctly stayed green — the arm went from RED-on-demand to
  vacuous **without the doctrine weakening at all**, and nothing but re-running it would have said
  so. The arm now deletes a row with a UNIQUE digest, a second arm covers the `(pending)` back-fill,
  and the probe reports **8/8**. ⇒ *a control can stop controlling without ever going red.*

  Annex A faithfully; the gap is in Annex A, and `.13c.2f` slice 4 is the standing precedent for
  which side wins (`-0221` made IEEE 1800-2023 §30.7.1's own `PATHPULSE$` example parse).

The reasoning is from the tracked LRMs, read rather than recalled:

  | source | what it says | status |
  |---|---|---|
  | `docs/systemverilog/2017/txt/section-Annex_A…:—` / `2023/…:1480` | `assignment_pattern_key ::= simple_type \| default` | normative, BOTH editions identical |
  | `docs/systemverilog/2017/md/section-10-assignment-statements.md` §10.9.2 | *"The `'{member:value}` or **`'{data_type: default_value}`** syntax can also be used"* | normative body text |
  | same, §10.9.2 worked example | `initial s2 = '{int:1, default:0, string:""};` | normative example |
  | same, §10.9.2 | *"The type:value specifies an explicit value for each field whose type matches the type (see 6.22.1)"* | 6.22.1 ranges over `data_type` |

  ⇒ **two normative clauses of the same standard disagree**, and they disagree the same way in 2017
  and 2023, so this is a standing LRM defect and not an edition difference.
- ⛔ **WHY THE UNION IS THE ONLY COMPLIANT READING.** `simple_type` and `data_type` are NOT nested:
  `simple_type ::= integer_type | non_integer_type | ps_type_identifier | ps_parameter_identifier`
  (`2023/…:598`), and `ps_parameter_identifier` (`:2187`) appears NOWHERE in `data_type` (`:545`),
  while `data_type` alone carries `string`, `chandle`, `event`, `class_type`,
  `ps_covergroup_identifier`, `type_reference` and the `virtual interface` form. So:
  * keeping only `simple_type` **rejects the standard's own §10.9.2 example** — a rejects-valid
    non-conformance, the axis the release bar is about;
  * replacing it with `data_type` **drops `ps_parameter_identifier`** — a silent narrowing, and
    exactly the "fix one instance, break the class" move `.13c.2e` warns against.

  The union is the only spelling under which every derivation either normative clause licenses is
  derivable, and it admits nothing the standard forbids: §10.9.2 says the key names a *type*, and
  `data_type` is the LRM's own name for the set of types. ⭐ `simple_type` stays FIRST so the AST
  arm for every construct that parses today is unchanged.

  a key-like operand. The drafters knew `simple_type` was short of `string`; they fixed it at

  rather than a deliberate restriction.

- **THE CLASS.** IEEE 1800's Annex A is normative *and so is the clause text*, and where they
  disagree PGEN currently mirrors Annex A — because that is what the grammar was extracted from. So
  every disagreement is a latent **rejects-valid** defect, and the LRM's own worked examples are the
  place they surface. `.13c.2t` is the confirmed instance: `assignment_pattern_key ::= simple_type |
  default` against §10.9.2's *"the `'{data_type: default_value}` syntax can also be used"* and its
  example `'{int:1, default:0, string:""}`.
- ⭐ **AND THE STANDARD PATCHES ITSELF IN PLACES, which is what makes this mechanisable.** Annex A's
  `casting_type ::= simple_type | constant_primary | signing | string | const` carries an explicit
  `| string` beside `simple_type` — the drafters fixed the same shortfall at one site and not at the
  other. A production that names a nonterminal AND separately names one of the things that
  nonterminal should already cover is a signal that the nonterminal is short.
- **WHY IT IS A LEAF AND NOT A NOTE.** Two prior slices found LRM-text defects one at a time
  (`.13c.2m`'s lost colon, `.13c.2o`'s mandatory footnote marker) and `.13c.2p` is already
  mechanising one family of them. This is a different family with a different signal, and the
  release bar is *"100 % LRM-compliant"* — which is a claim about the union of Annex A and the
  clause text, not about Annex A alone.
- **WHAT THIS LEAF OWES**: (a) the signal — for each Annex A production, whether the clause text that
  defines the same construct names a BROADER nonterminal (both LRM editions are tracked in
  `docs/systemverilog/{2017,2023}/{md,txt}/`, so the question is answerable from the repository);
  (b) the self-patch signal above as a second, independent detector; (c) a verdict per hit, since
  most disagreements will be editorial rather than substantive; (d) route each substantive one.

  alternatives is `randomize_call`**. IEEE 1800-2017 A.8.4 spells that alternative
  `function_subroutine_call`, and A.8.2 expands it to `subroutine_call ::= tf_call | system_tf_call
  | method_call | [ std :: ] randomize_call` — read from the in-repo LRM, not inferred. PGEN's own

  but it is referenced only from `for_step_assignment`, `module_path_primary` and
  `void_cast_statement_sv_only` — from no expression path. ⇒ the `with constraint_block` tail was
  unreachable from every expression.
  ⭐ **The asymmetry is what makes the diagnosis certain rather than plausible**: the STATEMENT path
  (`subroutine_call`, `@branch_policy: priority_first`) and the CONSTANT path
  (`constant_primary_sv_2017` → `constant_function_call`) both list the qualified `randomize_call`
  explicitly — measured, the same text parses as a statement (`initial randomize(a, b) with { a < b; };`)
  and fails as an expression.
  ⛔ **And the first hypothesis was WRONG, which is why it was traced rather than reasoned.** The
  obvious reading — *"`tf_call` matches `randomize(a,b)` first and masks `randomize_call` under
  `priority_first`"* — is refuted by `PGEN_TRACE_VERBOSITY=debug --trace-rules subroutine_call`,
  whose caller stacks show `randomize_call > constraint_block > constraint_block_item` being entered
  and the constraint block parsing, on a path seeded through `casting_type_lr_seed_constant_function_call`.
  `--parse-dump-ast` then named the accepted control's route exactly: `randomize(a, b)` produces
  `kind: "plain_tf"` and never `randomize`, because IEEE 1800 Annex B does **not** reserve
  `randomize` (it lists `rand`, `randc`, `randcase`, `randsequence` and stops).

  one new rule plus two references, tracked verbatim as a patch at

  ```text
  @profiles: ["sv_2017", "sv_2023"]
  scope_randomize_sv_only := ( kw_std_55ec981f scope_resolution )? randomize_call
                          -> {kind: "scope_randomize", std_scope: $1, body: $2}
  ```

  referenced as a bare pass-through from `primary_sv_2017` and `primary_sv_2023`, as each rule's
  **LAST** alternative.
  ⛔⛔ **AND "LAST" IS PART OF THE FIX — THE FIRST SPELLING PUT IT THIRD AND SILENTLY BROKE A
  LEGITIMATE IDENTIFIER.** Every part of `randomize_call` is optional (`randomize
  { attribute_instance } [ ( … ) ] [ with … ]`), so the rule matches a **bare `randomize`**. Placed
  after `call_primary` but before `hierarchical_identifier select`, it captured `randomize` used as
  an ordinary user identifier — which IEEE 1800 Annex B permits, since it reserves `rand`, `randc`,
  `randcase` and `randsequence` and not `randomize`. **The verdict never moved**: the control file
  parsed before and after. Only the AST did — `sweep_arms.py` reported `shape=2`, and the typed-AST
  diff named it exactly: `hierarchical` **4 → 3**, `bit_select` **4 → 3**, `scope_randomize`
  **0 → 1**. Moving the alternative to LAST returns `scope_randomize` nodes in that control to
  **0** while all three defect rows parse. ⭐ It is also the cheaper spelling — a last alternative
  is reached only when every other has failed. ⭐⭐ **The control that caught this was written in
  the same slice, deliberately, to guard the one direction the fix could break** — and it is the
  only thing that saw it. `run_adjudication_repros.py` verdicts, `--lint-grammar` (`1611 rules`,
  every counter identical) and all three defect reproducers were GREEN on the broken spelling.
  ⛔ **WHY NOT THE LRM-FAITHFUL SPELLING.** Replacing `call_primary` with `function_subroutine_call`
  in `primary` is what A.8.4 literally says and was measured as `armA`: it fixes the defect and
  wraps **every** existing call-primary AST in an extra `{kind: "call_primary", body: …}` level —
  a replaced shape for every function call in every expression, i.e. a schema bump across the whole
  consumer surface to buy one construct. Refused on cost, and the refusal is recorded rather than
  implied.
  ⭐ **WHY THE `kind` IS `scope_randomize` AND NOT `randomize`.** Four existing rules already emit
  `kind: "randomize"` (`built_in_method_call`, `constant_function_call`, `function_subroutine_call`,
  `subroutine_call`). An `arm` claim on a kind four other rules emit **cannot discriminate**, which
  is the exact failure `.13c.2a.2` recorded when it built that column. `grep -c 'kind:
  "scope_randomize"'` returns **1**.

     | **stale** | green | the baseline was stale and still correct ⇒ **AUTO RE-STAMP**, reported |
     | **stale** | **red** | AMBIGUOUS ⇒ refuse: *"stale AND diverging — re-derive deliberately"* |

#### ✅✅✅ `.13c.2y` **`done`** 2026-08-20 (`PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0261`; release `1.0.193`, ledger `SV-0066`, schema `25` → `26`) — **the LRM keyword is restored, the two non-productions are gone, and the fix took SV's union `UNKNOWN` from 53 to ONE.** Previously: **an IEEE 1800 KEYWORD IS BOUND TO AN OPERATOR TOKEN OF THE SAME NAME: `a implies b` is REJECTED and two constructs no IEEE 1800 production reaches are ACCEPTED** (⛔ `-0259` published THREE; `a -> b` is legal as an EXPRESSION per §11.3.2 and is a CONTROL, corrected in `-0261`) (opened 2026-08-20 session #252 by `.13c.2x`(a), `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0259`)

- ⛔ **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE), tool-pinned.** `grammars/systemverilog.ebnf:6666` defines

  ```ebnf
  implies := trivia "->"                        -> {kind: "implies"}
  ```

  — a **token rule named after an IEEE 1800 keyword**. `prop_primary_sv_2017` (`:4928`) and its
  `sv_2023` twin (`:5019`) each carry three branches built on it — two binding `implies` itself
  (`:4938`, `:4954`; the twin at `:5029`, `:5045`) and one binding its `|=` sibling `or_assign` —
  whose LRM counterparts spell something else entirely:

  | grammar | line (sv_2017) | what it compiles to | IEEE 1800-2017 A.2.10 |
  |---|---:|---|---|
  | `\| implies property_expr` | `:4938` | `-> property_expr` | **no such production** — the mangled remnant of `\|-> property_expr`, named as such in `SV-0039`'s own root cause and left in place by that fix |
  | `\| sequence_expr or_assign property_expr` | `:4941` | `sequence_expr \|= property_expr` (`or_assign := trivia "\|="`, `:7411`) | **no such production** — the mangled remnant of `\|=> property_expr`, likewise |
  | `\| property_expr implies property_expr` | `:4954` | `property_expr -> property_expr` | `property_expr **implies** property_expr` — the KEYWORD, mis-resolved to the arrow token |

  ⇒ the SVA keyword `implies` **is not in the grammar at all**. Every other A.2.10 property operator
  got a minted `kw_<name>_<hash>` token (`kw_nexttime_b0f658f8`, `kw_not_557f2555`,
  `kw_iff_ee1c009e`, …); `implies` collided with the pre-existing arrow rule and silently resolved to
  it. There is no `kw_implies_*` anywhere in `grammars/systemverilog.ebnf`.
- ⛔ **THE TOOL NAMED IT, IT WAS NOT READ OFF THE GRAMMAR** (TOOLBOX 2.1, scoped):

  ```bash
  PGEN_TRACE_VERBOSITY=debug ./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog \
      docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/cert_union_adjudication/sva_probes/implies.sv \
      --profile sv_2017 --trace-rules implies
  #   Attempting to match terminal '->' at position 60 (end: 62)
  #   Terminal '->' failed at position 60 - found 'im'
  ```

  Byte 60 is the first byte of the keyword `implies`.
- **MEASURED, both profiles, 23 probes** (21 at diagnosis, +2 precedence probes added by the fix slice) (`…/cert_union_adjudication/probe_matrix.tsv`; the measuring
  binary's embedded SV parser digest was verified equal to `generated/systemverilog_parser.rs`
  before use, `--parser-fingerprint` → `bfaca030…`):

  | probe | A.2.10 | `sv_2017` | `sv_2023` | class |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `a implies b` (named property) | legal | **REJECT** | **REJECT** | over-REJECTION |
  | `a implies b` (no clocking event) | legal | **REJECT** | **REJECT** | over-REJECTION |
  | `assert property (@(posedge clk) a implies b)` | legal | **REJECT** | **REJECT** | over-REJECTION |
  | `-> b` in property position | **no production reaches it** (`->` is binary only) | **ACCEPT** | **ACCEPT** | over-ACCEPTANCE |
  | `a \|= b` in property position | **no production reaches it** (`\|=` is an assignment op) | **ACCEPT** | **ACCEPT** | over-ACCEPTANCE |
  | `a -> b` in property position | ⛔ **LEGAL as an EXPRESSION** (§11.3.2 implication `->`), so this row is a CONTROL, not a defect — `.13c.2x`(a) first published it as over-acceptance and `-0261` corrected that | **ACCEPT** | **ACCEPT** | control |
  | the other 15 A.2.10 rows (`until`, `s_until_with`, `iff`, `and`, `or`, `\|->`, `nexttime`, `s_nexttime`, `eventually`, `s_eventually`, `s_always`, `accept_on`, `reject_on`, `sync_accept_on`, `sync_reject_on`, named instance — `and`/`or` share one probe) | legal | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | ok — **the control** |
  | `a implies b until c`, `a until b implies c`, `a iff b implies c` (added by the fix slice) | legal; Table 16-3 puts `implies` in ONE right-associative group with the `until` family, below `iff` | — | **ACCEPT** | precedence probes |

  ⭐ The 15 passing rows are what makes the six failing ones a finding rather than a broken probe
  harness: same file shape, same profiles, same binary, one token different.
- ⭐ **WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT — and it is a property of the instrument, not an oversight.**
  `--report-certificate-coverage` measures reach over the **declared** rule set, so a production the
  grammar never spells cannot be `UNKNOWN`; it can only be absent. The corpus rule-coverage TSV has
  the same blind spot for the same reason. `.13c.2x`(a) found this by using the nine unwitnessable
  `prop_primary` keywords as a POINTER and reading the rule they live in — a step no count performs.

  closed the missing `\|->`/`\|=>` operators and its own recorded root cause reads: *"the
  LRM-markdown→EBNF extractor split the `\|`-prefixed operators on `\|` (the EBNF alternation
  metachar), leaving the mangled `implies` (`->`) / `or_assign` (`\|=`) remnants in `prop_primary`"*.
  It **named both remnants and removed neither**, and it did not notice that the third site — the
  genuine A.2.10 `property_expr implies property_expr` — was mis-resolved to the same arrow. ⇒ the
  over-acceptance half has been tracked in prose since 2026-07-23 with no owning leaf, which is the
  `DOCTRINE-GAP-OWNERSHIP` thesis on an SV artifact.

  it, restoring `property_expr implies property_expr`; (b) DELETE the two mangled remnants

  IEEE 1800-2017 **Table 16-3** (§16.12, in-repo at
  `docs/systemverilog/2017/txt/section-15-interprocess-synchronization-and-communication.txt:3574`)

##### ⛔⛔⛔ `.13c.2y` — THE DELETION AUDIT, ON DIRECTOR CHALLENGE (2026-08-21, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0263`)

> **The challenge, verbatim**: *"Any reason why you had to delete 43 'dead' rules. Where did these
> rules come from? the IEEE 1800 LRMs contain an initial set of rules which we extracted
> automatically … I am surprised you had to delete up to 43 of those rules. on which basis did you
> decide it was legit to get rid of those rules? did you cross-check the IEEE 1800 LRMs first? … We
> have to audit what we did there."* — and *"We can't just delete 43 rules on a whim."*

- ⛔⛔ **THE PREMISE IS MINE, NOT THE DIRECTOR'S: NO RULE WAS DELETED. NOT ONE.** `-0261`'s own
  write-up said *"43 dead rules stopped existing"* and *"96 synthesised rules gone"*, which reads
  exactly as *"we deleted 43 rules"*. That phrasing is the defect. Measured, two ways:

  ```bash
  git show 958fcc24 -- grammars/systemverilog.ebnf | grep -E '^-[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*[ ]*:='   # -> 0
  ```

  | | before (`211b46b5`) | after (`958fcc24`) |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | SOURCE rules the frontend parses from the `.ebnf` | **1484** | **1485** |
  | rules present before and ABSENT after | — | **0** |
  | rules ADDED | — | **1** (`kw_implies_470cec58`) |

  The whole diff removes **six lines**: three alternatives, each with its annotation line, in each of
  the two profile rules. **Rule definitions removed: zero.**
- ⛔ **AND THE 43 WERE NEVER IN A GRAMMAR FILE, AT ANY COMMIT.** They are `property_expr_lr_suffix_r0…r39`
  plus three siblings, minted at BUILD TIME by
  `rust/src/ast_pipeline/indirect_lr_elimination.rs:862` — `format!("{base_rule}_lr_suffix_r{index}")`
  — when the eliminator rewrites a left-recursive rule into `X := X_lr_base ( X_lr_suffix )*`:

  ```bash
  git log --all --oneline -S "property_expr_lr_" -- grammars/   # -> 0 commits, ever
  grep -c "property_expr_lr_" grammars/systemverilog.ebnf       # -> 0, before AND after
  ```

  ⇒ they are **compiler output**, the parser-generator's own temporaries, in the same sense as a
  compiler's spill slots. No LRM extraction produced them and no debugging session authored them.
  They stopped being emitted because the eliminator stopped having a left-recursion to eliminate.
- ⭐⭐ **THE REAL QUESTION IS THE THREE ALTERNATIVES, AND THAT AUDIT IS OWED WHATEVER THE RULE COUNT
  SAYS** — [[feedback_no_rule_deletion_without_lrm_proof]] binds on grammar content, not on rule
  definitions alone. Each, cross-checked against IEEE 1800-2017 Annex A.2.10:

  | removed alternative | what it COMPILED to | in A.2.10? | basis, and where the LRM content went |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `\| implies property_expr` | `-> property_expr` | ⛔ **no such production** | the **mangled remnant of `sequence_expr \|-> property_expr`** — the extractor split the `\|`-prefixed operator on `\|`, the EBNF alternation metachar, leaving `-> property_expr`. Named as a remnant in **`SV-0039`'s own recorded root cause** (2026-07-23). Its correct replacement, `\| sequence_expr overlapped_implication property_expr`, was added by that same fix and sits at `grammars/systemverilog.ebnf:4940` **today** |
  | `\| sequence_expr or_assign property_expr` | `sequence_expr \|= property_expr` | ⛔ **no such production** | the remnant of `sequence_expr \|=> property_expr`, split identically; also named by `SV-0039`. Replacement `\| sequence_expr non_overlapped_implication property_expr` at `:4942` |
  | `\| property_expr implies property_expr` | `property_expr -> property_expr` | ✅ **YES — this IS A.2.10** | ⭐ **NOT DELETED — RELOCATED AND REPAIRED.** It is in the grammar at `:4910` / `:4997` as `prop_iff_<profile> kw_implies_470cec58 prop_until_<profile>`, now consuming the KEYWORD instead of the arrow, at the Table 16-3 precedence level the LRM assigns it. Moving it is what made `a implies b` parse for the first time |

- ✅ **THE RULING: ZERO IEEE 1800 PRODUCTIONS LEFT THE ACCEPTED LANGUAGE.** Two extraction artifacts
  were removed, each superseded by its own correct replacement already shipping since `1.0.169`; one
  genuine A.2.10 production was moved to the right rule with the right terminal. The accept set
  changed in exactly the two directions the LRM demands — `implies` in, `-> property_expr` and
  `sequence_expr |= property_expr` out.
- ⭐ **AND IT IS CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY, NOT ONLY BY READING** (`-0263`): the full 16 335-file external
  corpus shows **0 pass→fail**, exactly **1** fail→pass, and — the sharper control — **6 541 of 6 541
  still-failing files keep a BYTE-IDENTICAL failure offset**. If either removed alternative had been
  carrying real SystemVerilog, a corpus of 16 335 files would have moved somewhere. It moved in one
  place, and that place is the `implies` assertion.
- ⚠️ **WHAT I OWE FROM THIS EXCHANGE, and it is a writing rule rather than a grammar one**: an
  engine-synthesised rule and an authored rule must never be counted in the same sentence without
  saying which is which. *"96 synthesised rules gone"* is true and unreadable; *"the eliminator stops
  emitting 96 temporaries because the left-recursion it was eliminating no longer exists"* is the
  same fact and cannot be misread as a deletion. ⛔ The director read my sentence exactly as written,
  and the alarm was the correct response to it.

  that mints operator tokens with human-readable names can bind an imported keyword to a same-named
  operator, and the resulting defect is invisible to every coverage instrument because the keyword
  never becomes a rule.

###### ✅ `.13c.2x.9`(c1) `done` — **THE REACH BFS PROVED AN UNGATED ESCAPE EXISTS INSIDE A MANDATORY SIBLING, AND THEN THREW THAT PROOF AWAY — SV's LAST UNION `UNKNOWN` IS CLOSED** (opened 2026-08-22 session #254 by `(c)`'s diagnosis; ENGINE-UNIVERSAL, `rust/src/ast_pipeline/stimuli_generator.rs`)

- **GOAL** — when a reach plan's path crosses a rule, the store gates of that rule's MANDATORY
  SIBLINGS must be satisfiable *by the branch the generator actually renders*, so the sample parses
  the way the plan assumes. Parser-agnostic; SV is where it was measured, not what it is about.
- ⭐⭐ **PRICED FIRST AGAINST THE EXISTING PASS, as `(c)` required — and the existing pass is RIGHT.**
  `reach_hops_pass(_, _, exclude_store_gated_edges = true)` calls `edge_is_store_gated` →
  `mandatory_reach_gate` → `mandatory_node_gated`, which is **Or-aware**: *"gated iff EVERY
  alternative is gated — any non-gated alternative is a clean escape."* For
  `ps_checker_identifier := scoped_checker_identifier | known_unscoped_checker_identifier` the second
  alternative is gated on `checker_name` and the first is **not gated at all** —
  `non_typedef_package_scope`'s only predicate is `lacks_fact_attribute_equals`, satisfied by an
  empty store, and `package_scope := package_identifier scope_resolution` needs no fact. **MEASURED**:
  `bind top zz::chk c1 (myprop);` — with **no package and no checker declared anywhere** — parses and
  commits `scoped_checker_identifier=2` and the target `known_unscoped_property_identifier=2`.
  ⇒ the BFS is correct to keep the edge, and there is nothing to fix in the gate analysis.
- ⛔⛔ **THE DEFECT IS THAT THE ESCAPE IS COMPUTED AND DISCARDED.** `mandatory_node_gated` returns a
  **bool**. It knows *which* alternative is the clean escape at the moment it finds one, and it
  throws that away. The renderer then reaches `ps_checker_identifier` with **no directive** — the
  plan only steers rules ON the path to the target, and this rule is a mandatory sibling of one —
  draws the gated alternative, and the parse re-routes. ⇒ *the analysis that admits the edge and the
  render that must honour it disagree about which branch makes the edge admissible.*
- **DESIGN — no new mechanism, no new annotation surface**
  ([[feedback_read_prior_art_before_designing]]: the prior art is in this same file and is reused
  rather than duplicated). A reach plan is already a list of `(rule, node_path)` pairs turned into
  `ReachDirective`s by `directives_along_path`, and `("ps_checker_identifier", "root/o0")` already
  means *force branch 0*. So the fix is to EMIT the escape the analysis found as one more pair:
  1. `mandatory_escape_sites` — a path-carrying twin of `mandatory_node_gated` that records, for each
     `Or` in a rule's mandatory subtree where **some** alternatives are gated and **some** are not,
     the path of the FIRST ungated alternative (deterministic, lowest index), then descends into that
     alternative only.
  2. `install_reach_plan_from_hops` computes, per hop, the facts available at that hop (accumulated
     `gen_emit_facts` kinds, mirroring the BFS's `emitted_available`) and **prepends** the escape
     directives to `chain`. Prepending is the precedence rule: `from_directives` builds a map where a
     later insert wins, so an on-path directive always overrides an escape at the same key, and
     `chain.last()` — which defines the plan's target — stays the target hop.
  3. Both the BFS plan and the carrier-DIVERSIFIED plan install through this one function, so they
     gain the behaviour together (that factoring is `STORE-AWARE-GEN.4b.12`'s stated purpose).
- ⛔ **INERTNESS ARGUMENT, stated before implementing**: escape sites can only be produced where an
  `Or` inside a mandatory subtree has a *mixed* gated/ungated split, which requires the grammar to
  carry fact-query `@predicate`s at all. `reach_gate_kinds` is EMPTY for every grammar without them
  ⇒ `json`, `ebnf`, `vhdl`, `rtl_*` and the annotation grammars must be **byte-identical**, and that
  is an acceptance criterion below rather than an assertion.
- ⚠️ **BLAST RADIUS**: `stimuli_generator.rs` is the STIMULI side. No grammar byte, no codegen byte,
  no `generated/*.rs` byte moves ⇒ `PARSE-COST-RATCHET` and `GENERATED-REPRODUCIBILITY` are NOT
  disturbed, and no parser regeneration is required.


###### `.13c.2x.9`(c1) — WHAT LANDED: **SYSTEMVERILOG'S LAST CERTIFICATE-UNION `UNKNOWN` IS CLOSED — BY A WITNESS, WITH ZERO GRAMMAR BYTES** (`PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0276`, 2026-08-22 session #254)

- ✅✅✅ **THE RESULT.** Canonical `sv_2017` certificate coverage goes
  **`1385/18/1366/1 fully_certified=false` → `1385/18/1367/0 fully_certified=true`**, deterministic at
  seeds **0 / 7 / 42**, and the tracked recognized-union lane goes
  **`total=1385 proof=7 witness=1377 UNKNOWN=1` → `total=1385 proof=7 witness=1378 UNKNOWN=0
  fully_certified=true`**. ⛔ **No grammar byte, no codegen byte, no `generated/*.rs` byte moved** —
  `generated/systemverilog_parser.rs` is still `cc874b60…`. The SV ACCEPT SET did not move, which is
  exactly what `(d)` forbade buying this number with.
- ⛔⛔ **THE FIX IS ONE LINE OF INSIGHT: the escape analysis already knew the answer and returned a
  `bool`.** `mandatory_node_gated` is Or-aware — *"gated iff EVERY alternative is gated — any
  non-gated alternative is a clean escape"* — so at the moment it admits an edge it knows WHICH
  alternative made it admissible, and discards that. The plan then steers only rules ON the path, the
  ordinary generator draws the gated alternative of a mandatory sibling, the parser rejects it, and
  the enclosing choice commits something else. Three additions, no new annotation surface and no new
  plan representation (the prior art is `ReachDirective` + `directives_along_path`, reused):

  | piece | what it does |
  |---|---|
  | `StoreGateScope::ParseRejects` | positive gates ONLY — `gen_name_gate` ∪ `gen_count_kinds` |
  | `hop_escape_sites` / `escape_walk` | per hop: FOLLOW the on-path descent; for every off-path `Or` with a mixed gated/ungated split, record the first ungated alternative's path |
  | `install_reach_plan_from_hops` | PREPENDS those directives, so an on-path directive always wins the map and `chain.last()` still defines the target |

- ⛔⛔⛔ **THE SCOPE CHOICE IS THE WHOLE DESIGN, AND THE FIRST CUT GOT IT WRONG IN THE ONE WAY THAT
  PRODUCES NO OUTPUT RATHER THAN WRONG OUTPUT.** Built on `StoreGateScope::AnyQuery` — the scope the
  reach BFS uses — it emitted **`sites=[]`** for the very target it was written for. `AnyQuery`
  counts `lacks_fact*`, and **an empty store SATISFIES a `lacks_fact*`**, so
  `scoped_checker_identifier` (whose only predicate is a `lacks_fact_attribute_equals` on
  `type_name`) read as gated, the two-alternative `Or` read as *"every alternative gated"*, and the
  analysis found no escape. `GenerationPruned` fails the other way — it excludes name gates because
  GENERATION never prunes on them, while the PARSER rejects on them and the parse is what has to be
  predicted. ⭐ **A wrong scope here is silent**: `sites=[]` is indistinguishable from *"no escape was
  needed"*, which is why `PGEN_REACH_ESCAPE_DUMP` shipped in the same slice rather than after it.
- ⭐ **NO-REGRESSION IS MEASURED TWO-SIDED, ONE BINARY PER ARM** (`git stash` the single source file,
  rebuild, re-run; restored copy verified byte-identical afterwards). Certificate tuples
  BEFORE → AFTER:

  | family | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | `json` | `9/0/9/0` | **identical** |
  | `regex` | `269/9/260/0` | **identical** (2 of 166 plans DO carry escape sites — installed and inert) |
  | `vhdl` | `225/0/225/0` | **identical** |
  | `systemverilog_preprocessor` | `74/0/74/0` | **identical** |
  | `rtl_frontend` | `169/1/168/0` | **identical** |
  | `rtl_const_expr` | `48/0/48/0` (= its contract exactly) | **identical** |
  | **`systemverilog` (canonical)** | `1385/18/1366/1` `false` | **`1385/18/1367/0` `true`** |

  ⇒ **exactly one number moved, in one family, in the intended direction.** ⚠️ `ebnf`,
  `return_annotation` and `semantic_annotation` cannot be measured this way at all — the cert refuses
  with *"no generated parser is registered for grammar 'X'"* — and that is a PRE-EXISTING fact about
  cert wiring, not an effect of this change (they install zero reach plans either way). It is also a
  finding in its own right; see below.
- ⭐ **COST: none.** The canonical cert run is **22.3 s** against a 25 s baseline — the escape walk is
  bounded by the same mandatory subtree the gate analysis already walks, and a target that witnesses
  first time costs fewer retry attempts than one that never does.
- ⛔⛔ **THE GATE WENT RED, AND IT WAS RIGHT TO — `.13c.2x.3`'s LESSON, SECOND OCCURRENCE: THE GATE
  IS RED BECAUSE THE TREE GOT BETTER.** `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate` reported
  `unmet_criteria_count: 15` — five quantities × three seeds — with `primary_unmet=seed=0 canonical
  witness=1367 (expected 1366)`. ⭐ It also **REFUSED to auto-re-stamp**, in the exact words the
  doctrine promises: *"AND THIS BASELINE IS STALE … the failure above is AMBIGUOUS … Adjudicate it;
  do NOT re-stamp to make it green, because a stamp asserts the numbers were RE-DERIVED and matched,
  which is precisely what just did not happen."* The auto-re-stamp fires only on stale+GREEN;
  stale+RED is the one case reserved for a person, and this was it.
- ✅✅ **THE ADJUDICATION — A TWO-SIDED SET CHECK, because a count could not tell an improvement from
  a swap.** The canonical `UNKNOWN` set after the change is **exactly the eleven entry-relative
  rules** — `include_statement`, `kw_file_path_spec_*`, `kw_incdir_*`, `kw_include_*`, `kw_library_*`,
  `library_declaration`, `library_description`, `library_text`, `parseable_source_item`,
  `sv_multi_entry_root`, `systemverilog_parseable_file` — **byte-identical at seeds 0/7/42**, and the
  union residual is `[]`. ⇒ BEFORE − AFTER = `{known_unscoped_property_identifier}` **exactly**;
  AFTER − BEFORE = **∅**, so no rule fell out of `witness` into `UNKNOWN` behind the falling count.
  Both accountings still close on unchanged `total` and `proof`: `7 + 1367 + 11 = 1385` and
  `7 + 1378 + 0 = 1385`. Only then was the contract rebaselined, with that adjudication written into
  its own `rebaseline_note`, and the gate re-run to GREEN so it re-stamped its identity block itself.
- ✅ **Verification**: `clippy_on_rust_change` PASS (strict source + generated stages, 68 pinned
  correctness lints intact); `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate` GREEN on the re-run;
  `scripts/check_doctrines.sh` ALL 25 PASS; `mdbook_docs_gate` PASS.
- ⛔⛔ **WHAT THIS DOES *NOT* MEAN, stated before anyone reads the number as licence.** The director's
  `SVPP-EXPANSION` activation gate is *"every existing parser cert-coverage WIRED + clean +
  `UNKNOWN`=0"*. SystemVerilog was the last family with `UNKNOWN > 0` and it is now `0` ⇒ **SV is no

  grammar names, so their certificate coverage cannot be measured at all. ⇒ the gate is **not open**,

> Ledger `SV-0049` (2026-08-09, three days earlier) fixed the IDENTICAL defect one clause away —
> `expression_or_dist ::= expression [ dist { dist_list } ]` rendered as `( kw_dist dist_list* )?`.
> It fixed the instance it was looking at. Had it swept the class, this leaf would not exist. The
> sweep now exists as an instrument rather than as a resolution
> (`docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/intersect_braces/lrm_brace_transcription_sweep.py`), and its
> before/after pair is what lets this leaf claim the class is closed rather than hope so.

**WHAT THE SWEEP MEASURED — the leaf's own *"do not assume this is the only place"* discharged.**
The discriminator is semantic and decidable: IEEE 1800 writes repetition `{ x }` and literal braces
`{ x }` with the same characters, but a `{ X_list }` whose inner nonterminal is itself a LIST can
only be literal — repeating a comma-separated list with no separator between repetitions is
something no clause means. Run over **both** the 2017 and 2023 extracted LRMs (867 / 880
productions) against all three grammar spellings of every rule:

| tier | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| **DEFECT** — literal `{ X_list }` rendered as `X_list*`, no braces | **2** (`select_condition`, once per LRM edition) | **0** |
| **CORRECT** — literal `{ X_list }` modelled `lbrace … rbrace` | 4 (`expression_or_dist`, `inside_expression`) | 6 (+ `select_condition`) |
| **REPEAT** — `{ X }`, X not a list ⇒ genuine repetition | 49 | 49 |

⇒ **`select_condition` was the only mis-transcription in either edition.** ⛔ **THE CLAIM IS THE
BRACE CLASS, NOT THE DELIMITER CLASS — and the difference is routed, not glossed.** `SV-0049`'s own
changelog asked for an *"exhaustive Annex-A **bracket/brace** sweep"*; this leaf delivers the brace
half. The bracket half has no discriminator yet: transferring the `_list` rule naively returns **83
rows / 45 productions**, visibly dominated by ordinary optionals (`[ lifetime ]`, `[ signing ]`,
`[ port_direction ]`, `[ name_of_instance ]` ×7 — two read against the LRM, both genuine), a ratio
that would teach waivers rather than close a class. Owned by **`LRM-GRAMMAR-FIDELITY.1a`** with that
sizing as its routing evidence. The instrument refuses
rather than guesses: four controls run before any verdict prints (both LRMs parse to a plausible
size; the grammar reader resolves `select_condition`; `expression_or_dist` **and**
`inside_expression` are in CORRECT; `specify_block` is in REPEAT), and it deliberately does **not**
pin `select_condition` to a tier — that is the cell the fix moves, so pinning it would have made the
control unfalsifiable. Honest bound, stated: the tier rule keys on the `_list` suffix, so a
literal-brace production whose inner nonterminal is named otherwise would land in REPEAT and be
missed — which is why REPEAT is printed in full rather than summarised.

- **IEEE 1800-2017 A.2.11:** `select_condition ::= binsof ( bins_expression ) [ intersect {
  covergroup_range_list } ]` — the `{` and `}` are **literal syntax**, and `covergroup_range_list` is
  the comma-separated list *inside* them.
- **`systemverilog.ebnf:5259` models neither:**
  `select_condition := kw_binsof_efb35b22 lparen bins_expression rparen ( kw_intersect_6c96caaf covergroup_range_list* )?`
  — no brace terminals, and the list is a `*` repetition instead.

  `x: cross ca, cb { ignore_bins ib = binsof(ca) intersect { 1 } && binsof(cb); }`: the select node is
  kind **`condition`** with **no `and` node at all**; its `intersect` payload holds a `concat` of `1`
  whose `operand_chain.rest` carries `logical_and` + `binsof(cb)`. ⇒ `{ 1 }` was parsed as a
  **concatenation expression**, and with no closing-brace terminal to stop it the `covergroup_range_list*`
  **swallowed `{ 1 } && binsof(cb)` as one expression**.

  `binsof(ca) intersect { 1 } && binsof(cb)` → `select_expression_lr_suffix` entries=1 **committed=0**,
  versus the parenthesized `( binsof(ca) intersect { 1 } ) && binsof(cb)` → entries=4 **committed=1**.
  The parens are doing the work the braces should be doing.

  where the LRM admits only a brace-delimited range list). Under the SV *"100 % LRM-compliant by
  default; over-acceptance is a defect"* bar this is a defect, not a preference.

##### ✅✅ ANSWERED 2026-08-23 (`PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0281`) — YES, and 147 rows were misclassified on a premise the corpus itself refutes

**Instrument:** `stimuli/sv/audit_no_sv_key.py` → `docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/no_sv_key_secondary_keys/`
(`report.txt` + `README.md`), byte-identical across runs, no wall-clock. ZERO grammar / Rust /
codegen / generated bytes; ZERO adjudicator bytes.

- ⭐⭐⭐ **THE SENTENCE WAS TRUE ABOUT THE DESCRIPTOR AND FALSE ABOUT THE QUESTION.** 147 rows (27 of
  them DARK) carry the adjudicator's basis *"vvp_tests descriptor(s) without an explicit generation
  flag — dialect unresolved (**the upstream default generation is not encoded in the descriptor**)"*.
  Every word is correct about the descriptor. It is simply the wrong artifact to interrogate: the
  default generation is compiled into `iverilog`, and **`iverilog` is vendored in this same corpus**:

  ```text
  stimuli/sv/subs/iverilog/compiler.h   enum generation_t { … GN_VER2005 = 4, … GN_DEFAULT = 4 }
  stimuli/sv/subs/iverilog/main.cc      generation_t generation_flag = GN_DEFAULT;
  ```

  ⇒ a run with no `-g` flag compiles as **plain IEEE 1364-2005 Verilog**. Those rows belong to the
  **`v2005_profile_lane`** (ROUTED — *answered in the v2005 manifest, not lost*), never to
  `no_sv_key` (NO VERDICT — answered nowhere). ⛔ **The information was in the repository the whole
  time, one directory below the descriptor the adjudicator was reading.**
- ⭐ **THE CONTRAST IS WHAT MAKES IT SAFE TO SAY, and it was measured rather than assumed.** The
  primary key `regress-sv.list` encodes the dialect **explicitly in 907 of its 922 entries**
  (`-g2005-sv` / `-g2009` / `-g2012` / `-g2017` / `-g2023`) — which is *why* it is the SV key. An
  unflagged descriptor is therefore not an SV entry missing its label; it is a different lane. Had
  that ratio come back near zero, the whole primary key would have been in question and this leaf
  would have reported that instead.
- ⛔⛔ **THE ONE MECHANISM THAT WOULD INVERT THE VERDICT IS CHECKED ON EVERY RUN, because it is a
  single upstream edit away.** `vvp_reg.py` defines `force_gen()`, which strips any generation and
  inserts `-g2023`. If it ran by default every unflagged descriptor would be SystemVerilog and this
  finding would be backwards. Three facts, all re-derived at run time: it is guarded by
  `cfg['force-sv']`; `--force-sv` is `action='store_true'` (default off); and the vendored
  `Makefile.in`'s own `check-installed-vvp-py` target invokes `python3 vvp_reg.py $(opts)` with no
  such flag. `run_ivl.py` injects no generation on the normal path either.
- ⛔ **THIS IS NOT THE RELABELLING `.13` FORBIDS, and the distinction is load-bearing.** That warning
  is against *"pinning the deferred rows to an expectation and calling them adjudicated"*. **Nothing
  here becomes adjudicated.** A row moves from one deferral to a **weaker and checkable** one, and it
  moves because the stated ground for its original class — *the dialect cannot be determined* — is
  refuted by measurement. ⭐ The check the move creates is real: a row claiming the v2005 lane must
  then actually be answered there, which `.13e.1` owes.
- **THE OTHER BASIS — ENUMERATED, NOT ARGUED.** 596 rows (52 DARK) carry *"no `regress-sv.list`
  entry"*. The vendored tree holds **11** `*.list` files and the adjudicator reads **2**:

  | lists naming the DARK row | rows |
  |---|---:|
  | `regress-ivl1.list` | 16 |
  | **(NONE — no ivtest list names it)** | **15** |
  | `regress-ivl1.list` + `regress-vlog95.list` | 4 |
  | `regress-synth.list` + `vhdl_regress.list` | 4 |
  | `vpi_regress.list` | 4 |
  | `blif.list` | 2 |
  | `regress-ivl1.list` + `vhdl_regress.list` | 2 |
  | `regress-synth.list` + `regress-vlog95.list` | 2 |
  | `regress-fsv.list` + `regress-ivl1.list` + `regress-vlog95.list` | 1 |
  | `regress-synth.list` | 1 |
  | `regress-fsv.list` + `regress-synth.list` | 1 |

  ⇒ **37 of 52 are named by another list; 15 by none.** ⭐ **The honest-permanent-deferral set this
  leaf owed is 15 rows, not 743** — which is the leaf's own ask (*"naming the 78 rather than the
  743"*) met two orders of magnitude tighter than it asked for.
- ⛔⛔ **AND THE AUDIT REFUSES TO READ A VERDICT OUT OF A SECONDARY LIST, which is the discipline
  that keeps 37 rows from becoming 37 false defects.** The lists are different **back ends** and they
  disagree about what a verdict means: `regress-fsv.list` is read **only** under `--force-sv`, so it
  testifies about *forced* SystemVerilog; `regress-vlog95.list` is a Verilog-95 **output** lane where
  a `CE` means the back end refused, **not** the parser (`always_comb_rfunc CE` sits in it, and
  `always_comb` is perfectly legal SystemVerilog); `vhdl_regress.list`, `blif.list` and
  `vpi_regress.list` are other back ends again. Reading a `CE` from any of those as `must_reject`
  would **manufacture a parser defect**. ⇒ *a key is not a verdict*, and the per-list adjudication is
  `.13e.1`'s work.
- ⭐⭐ **EVERY REFUSAL ARM WAS FIRED, in a throwaway mini-repo under `rust/target/` holding mutated

  |---|---|---|
  | A1 | `GN_DEFAULT` deleted from the enum | `REFUSE: GN_DEFAULT is not a member of enum generation_t` |

  | C1 | one row given an unbucketed basis | `REFUSE: … classify it rather than letting it fall into a total` |
  | C2 | the class emptied | `REFUSE: no deferred:no_sv_key rows … the class moved or the run is stale` |

  ⭐ A3/B1/B2/B3 exist because each is **one upstream edit** that would flip the verdict silently.
  The audit's value is not the number it prints today; it is that the number cannot outlive its
  premise.

note read the seven names and proposed *"a `partsel_outside_*` pair (indexed part-select bounds), a
`timing_check_*` pair, and two `br_gh*` regressions plus one UDP row"*. Measured, the real
population is **FIVE constructs**, and the part-select cluster **does not exist**: `arr[-'d1 +: 2]`
**PARSES** (control `control_v2005_partsel_negative_base.sv`), and both files stop on an unbased
unsized `'x` sitting in their *self-checking `if`* — a line that has nothing to do with what the
test is named for. ⇒ **naming a defect cluster from a filename is a guess, and the control is what
separates the two hypotheses.** Only the `timing_check_*` pair survived as a pair.

⭐⭐ **AND THE ROW THE LEAF SAID TO ADJUDICATE FIRST WAS RIGHT FOR A REASON THE LEAF DID NOT GIVE.**
`udp_empty_table_fail.v` was flagged because a `_fail` suffix hints at invalid text. It *is* invalid
text — but the same `type: "CE"` key sits on `br_gh1087b.v` and `br_gh552.v`, whose names carry no
such hint at all. **Three of the seven are keyed `CE` — the file is EXPECTED not to compile** — and
they reached a `must_accept` lane anyway. The naming hint found one of three; the descriptor found
all three. ⇒ read the KEY, not the filename.

**WHY THREE `CE` ROWS BECAME `must_accept`** — `_gold_has_syntax_error()` searches the golden for
the literal words *"syntax error"*, and iverilog says something else in all three
(*"is an Icarus Verilog extension"*, *"Empty UDP table."*, an elaboration error). That heuristic is
a claim about **which stage of iverilog refused**, which is a different question from **whether the
LRM derives the text** — and the corpus-expected-from-SPEC doctrine asks the second. Routed as
`.13e.3`, together with a second, sharper hole the same rows exposed.

⛔⛔ **AND THE OBVIOUS CLASSIFIER IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** *"Does the flag reach
`parse.y`?"* is the natural test and it fails twice over:

| flag | variable | consumed at | decides the language? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-gxtypes` / `-gno-xtypes` | `gn_cadence_types_flag` | **`pform.cc:3580`** — never `parse.y` | **YES** — *"Net data type requires SystemVerilog or -gxtypes."* |
| `-gicarus-misc` / `-gno-` | `gn_icarus_misc_flag` | `parse.y:4162/4174` | **YES** — the `K_NAND`/`K_NOR` alternatives |
| `-gverilog-ams` / `-gno-` | `gn_verilog_ams_flag` | `lexor.lex` | **YES** — a different language; already has its own lane |
| `-gspecify` / `-gno-specify` | `gn_specify_blocks_flag` | `parse.y` ×**21** | **no** — every site is an ACTION BODY of a rule that already reduced |
| `-gsupported-assertions` | `gn_supported_assertions_flag` | `parse.y` ×3 | **no** — same shape |
| `-ginterconnect` / `-gno-` | `gn_interconnect_flag` | `elaborate.cc` only | **no** |
| `-gno-strict-*declaration` | `gn_strict_*_declaration` | `symbol_search.cc` | **no** — name resolution |

⇒ a `parse.y` membership test would **admit** `-gspecify` and `-gsupported-assertions` and
**reject** `-gxtypes`, which is the only one of the three that actually gates a production.
**The classifier had to be derived from what each variable GUARDS, not from where its name
appears** ([[feedback_derive_classifiers_from_the_producer]]).

⭐⭐ **THE TWO THAT MATTER MOST ARE DEFAULT-ON, SO THEY APPEAR IN NO DESCRIPTOR AT ALL.**
`main.cc:109-110` sets `gn_icarus_misc_flag = true` and `gn_cadence_types_flag = true`. ⇒
`.13e.1` derived `GN_DEFAULT = GN_VER2005` correctly and stopped one question short: iverilog's
`-g2005` is *Verilog-2005 **plus** Cadence extended types **plus** the Icarus misc extensions*,
not plain 1364-2005. **Every** unflagged ivtest row inherits that posture, and the basis strings
of **100 v2005-lane rows and 147 SV-lane rows** said only *"the compiler's own default"*. They
now name the posture — the same correction `.13e.1` made one field over.

**HOW THE BLAST RADIUS WAS BOUNDED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** The 53 remaining v2005 rejects-valid
rows were scanned for the two default-on extensions' constructs and every candidate was put
through the parser: 11 candidates, and `furthest_position=` put **exactly one** of them on the
extension (`real_invalid_ops.v` L17:20, at `var1` `~&`). The other ten stop on unrelated
constructs — `tri1 scalared [63:0]`, `pulldown (a,b,c)`, a UDP edge entry, `j++`, a specify path
— i.e. the coarse text filter was 10/11 false positives and **only the parser could tell**.

**THE GUARD, AND ITS RED CONTROL.** A descriptor that switches a language-affecting extension ON
by hand can no longer key `must_accept` from compile testimony; it routes to
`out_of_scope_with_cause:vendor_extension_enabled`. ⛔ **It fires on ZERO tracked rows today**
(the one row that would trip it, `br_gh1087b.v`, is already pinned by clause cite, and pins run
first) — and a guard never observed firing is not known to work, so it ships with
`--self-test`: **16/16 arms**, including the guard FIRING on a synthetic extension-enabling
descriptor, DISCRIMINATING (the same row without the flag still keys `must_accept`), and two
REFUSALS proven to fire when the vendored `main.cc` stops recognising `-gxtypes` or stops
initialising `gn_icarus_misc_flag`.
