###### `.13e.3` (b) — **DONE: the golden vocabulary is enumerated AND SPLIT BY EDITION, and it moved the bar in BOTH directions — 2 phantoms removed, 3 REAL over-acceptances surfaced** (2026-08-23, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0286`; opens `.13e.5`)

- ⭐⭐⭐ **THE HOLE WAS HIDING DEFECTS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THE HIDDEN OVER-ACCEPTANCES
  OUTNUMBER THE PHANTOMS.** Measured over the **394** ivtest `CE` rows: **84** carry a usable
  golden and only **6** of those say the words *"syntax error"*. Enumerating what iverilog
  actually says moved five rows — `br_gh1117` and `pr2794144` out of the burn-down (phantom
  rejects-valid), and `br1027a` / `br1027c` / `br1027e` **into** it as
  `unexplained_accepts_invalid`. ⛔ **The v2005 arm's headline barely moved (66 → 67) and its
  COMPOSITION changed materially** — `rejects_valid 52 → 50`, `accepts_invalid 14 → 17`. A
  campaign watching only the headline would have called this noise.

⛔⛔ **A FILE-BASED CLASSIFIER LOOKED DECISIVE AND OVER-ADMITS BADLY.** Mapping every golden
message back to the source that emits it is the obvious producer-derived move, and the result is
a trap: **97** distinct messages resolve to a "parse-stage" file and **90 of them are
`'X' has already been declared in this scope.` out of `pform.cc`** — a duplicate declaration,
which every edition derives perfectly well. `pform.cc` is the parse-time **form builder** and
does semantic checking too. ⇒ only `parse.y` / `lexor.lex` are reliable signals, and even those
had to be read one message at a time.

⭐⭐⭐ **AND THE VOCABULARY HAD TO BE SPLIT BY EDITION — AN UNSPLIT LIST WAS MEASURED
MANUFACTURING FIVE FALSE DEFECTS.** `.3.24` could give verilator ONE flat list because every
entry there is a **lexical** fact true in all editions. Several ivtest parse refusals are
**dialect gates** instead: true under the generation iverilog was run with, false under the
edition the lane adjudicates.

| candidate entry | what it really says | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `requires SystemVerilog …` | *"you need a LATER generation than the one I was given"* | ⛔ **EXCLUDED** — would have flipped `br_gh1143e/f/g/h` (run at `-g2009`, whose null for-loop initialization **IEEE 1800-2017 A.6.8 makes optional**) and `br_gh1087a` (`Net data type requires SystemVerilog or -gxtypes` — and IEEE 1800 net declarations DO take a data type). **5 false `accepts_invalid` defects against PGEN, avoided by measurement** |
| `Missing task/function port direction.` | true under 1364-2005 A.2.7, **relaxed** by IEEE 1800 A.2.7 | ⚠️ **v2005 lane ONLY** |
| `operator is an Icarus Verilog extension` · `Empty UDP table.` · `Invalid table for UDP primitive` · `generate/endgenerate regions cannot nest.` · `is not a valid expression. Please use operator` | no IEEE edition derives them | ✅ **edition-invariant** |

**EVERY MOVER WAS ADJUDICATED BY CLAUSE BEFORE IT WAS ALLOWED TO MOVE** (the auditor's asymmetry:
a re-derivation that contradicts a standing number carries the heavier burden):

- `br1027a/c/e` — `task t(a, b);` / `task t(integer a, b);` / `task t(input integer a, integer b);`.
  A.2.7 `task_port_item` (`…Annex_A…txt:290`) is one of exactly three `tf_*_declaration`s and each
  (`:300`/`:303`/`:306`) **begins with its direction keyword**. ⭐ The distinction that makes the
  third file a separate row: `tf_input_declaration ::= input task_port_type
  list_of_port_identifiers` lets ONE `input` cover several names, so `task t(input integer a, b);`
  **is** legal — the defect is that a *new* `task_port_item` may start directionless.
  **PGEN accepts all three ⇒ three real over-acceptance defects**, owned by `.13e.5`.
- `br_gh1117` — nested `generate … endgenerate`. A.4.2 `generate_region ::= generate
  { module_or_generate_item } endgenerate`, and `module_or_generate_item` (`:65`) has **no**
  `generate_region` alternative — only `non_port_module_item` (`:88`) does. Not derivable; PGEN
  rejects; the `must_accept` was a phantom.
- `pr2794144` — `res = ~ |in;`. A.8.3 `expression ::= unary_operator { attribute_instance }
  primary` (`:882`) — the operand of a unary operator is a **primary**, and `|in` is an
  *expression*. Not derivable; PGEN rejects. ⭐ The file says so **itself**: its success path
  prints *"FAILED: These expressions should be a syntax error."*

- ⚠️ **BOUND**: this enumerates the goldens that EXIST. **310 of the 394 CE rows carry no usable
  golden at all** and are untouched — they remain the `.8b.3`/`.8c.2` stage-pin population, and
  no message vocabulary can reach them.

##### ✅✅✅ `.13e.4` — **DONE: `integer signed` / `time signed` no longer parse under `verilog_2005` (ledger `SV-0069`, release `1.0.196`) — and the leaf's own scoping was WRONG IN TWO PLACES, both found by measuring instead of reading** (`done` 2026-08-24, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0288`; opens `.13e.7`)

**THE DEFECT.** IEEE 1364-2005 A.2.1.3 is `integer_declaration ::= integer
list_of_variable_identifiers ;`
(`docs/verilog/2005/txt/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax-definition.txt:152`) — there is no
signing on it, and neither `signing` nor `integer_atom_type` appears **anywhere** in that Annex.
Signing on an integer ATOM is IEEE 1800 A.2.2.1 only. PGEN spelled `data_type`'s second alternative
the IEEE 1800 way — `integer_atom_type ( signing )?` — with **no `@profiles` gate**, so
`integer unsigned u;` parsed as plain Verilog on a strict-1364-2005 profile. Over-acceptance is a
defect ([[feedback_sv_strict_lrm_compliance_default]]).

⛔⛔ **THE LEAF'S OWN "OWED" LIST UNDERSTATED THE DEFECT TWICE, AND ONE COMMAND SAID SO EACH TIME.**
The routing evidence named `integer signed` / `integer unsigned` at one site. Measured:

1. **`time` is the same defect.** `integer_atom_type` admits exactly `integer` and `time` under
   `verilog_2005`, and A.2.1.3:174 is `time_declaration ::= time list_of_variable_identifiers ;` —
   no signing either. `time signed t;` accepted. A gate written for the `integer` spelling alone
   would have shipped with half the defect live.
2. **`block_data_type` carries the identical shape.** `grammars/systemverilog.ebnf:2077` is a
   second, independent `integer_atom_type ( signing )?`, reached from `block_item_declaration`, and
   A.2.8:314 is `{ attribute_instance } integer list_of_block_variable_identifiers ;` — no signing
   there either. `initial begin : b integer signed i; …` accepted, as did the function- and
   task-scope forms. ⇒ **grep the SHAPE, not the rule you were sent to.**

⭐⭐ **AND THE GATE GOES ON THE OPTIONAL, NOT ON THE ALTERNATIVE.** The invited fix — split
`data_type`'s alternative into `_sv_only` / `_v2005` variants, the `.13e.5` idiom — is wrong here
for a reason `.13e.5`'s own subject did not have: `integer_atom_type` **must stay reachable under
`verilog_2005`**, because that admission is exactly what makes plain `integer i;` parse. Only the
`( signing )?` beside it is IEEE-1800-only. Wrapping the OPTIONAL in a profile-gated alias — the
live `hierarchical_root_prefix_sv_only` idiom, already used by `hierarchical_identifier` — is a
one-rule change that adds **no** `data_type` alternative, so no branch index moves and
`signing: $2` keeps its slot and is simply always absent under `verilog_2005`.

```ebnf
@profiles: ["sv_2017", "sv_2023"]
integer_atom_signing_sv_only := signing
```

⭐ **THE INTERPRETER PAID FOR THE DESIGN BEFORE THE COMPILER DID.** `--interpret-parse` (TOOLBOX
§1.5b) gave the verdict against the raw `.ebnf` in **seconds, with no codegen and no `rustc`**, and
`--interpret-parse-ast-json` proved the sv_2017 typed AST **byte-identical across the edit on 11
inputs** — including the bare-annotation `block_data_type` path, where a pass-through rule was the
thing most likely to add a wrapper level. The ~40-minute regenerate + release-probe cycle was paid
**once**, for a grammar already known to be right in both directions.

**VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND BOTH EDITIONS** (interpreter first, then the regenerated parser):

| under `verilog_2005` | verdict |
|---|---|
| `integer signed i;` · `integer unsigned u;` · `time signed t;` · `time unsigned t;` — module scope | **REJECT** ✅ |
| the same four in a named block, in a `function` and in a `task` | **REJECT** ✅ |
| `integer i;` · `time t;` · `integer j = 1;` · `reg signed [7:0] r;` · `reg [7:0] r;` · `real r;` · `realtime r;` | **ACCEPT** ✅ |
| **under `sv_2017` / `sv_2023`: every one of the above** | **ACCEPT** ✅ (IEEE 1800 relaxation preserved) |

##### ✅✅✅ `.13e.5` — **DONE: the `verilog_2005` task/function port direction is MANDATORY again (ledger `SV-0068`, release `1.0.195`) — and the OBVIOUS fix was built, regenerated and MEASURED WRONG before it shipped** (`done` 2026-08-24, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0287`)

- **THE DEFECT.** IEEE 1364-2005 A.2.7 `task_port_item`
  (`docs/verilog/2005/txt/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax-definition.txt:290`) is one of
  exactly three `tf_*_declaration`s and each (`:300`/`:303`/`:306`) **begins with its direction
  keyword** — there is no directionless alternative. PGEN spelled the rule as IEEE 1800 does
  (`( tf_port_direction )?`, optional and inherited) with **no `@profiles` gate**, so
  `task t(a, b);` parsed as plain Verilog on a strict-1364-2005 profile. Over-acceptance is a defect
  ([[feedback_sv_strict_lrm_compliance_default]]).

⛔⛔ **THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG, AND ONLY MEASUREMENT SAID SO.** *"Every item must carry a
direction"* is the reading the defect invites, and it **rejects `task t(input integer a, b);`** —
which A.2.7 derives, because `tf_input_declaration ::= input task_port_type
list_of_port_identifiers` takes a **list** of names, so one `input` covers both. PGEN renders a port
list the IEEE 1800 way (one `tf_port_item` per comma), so a continuation name arrives as its own
directionless item and a per-item requirement forbids it. ⭐ **That version was written, the parser
was regenerated, and the grammar-AST interpreter reported the rejection — before any of it
shipped.** The refuting input is now the tracked control
`control_v2005_task_port_shared_direction.sv`, so the wrong shape cannot be re-derived from the same
reasoning.

**THE SHIPPED SHAPE**, which is what A.2.7 actually says: a directionless item is admitted **only
when it is a bare port identifier** (no data type, no `var` — i.e. a `list_of_port_identifiers`
continuation), and the **first** item of the list must carry a direction.

```ebnf
@profiles: ["verilog_2005"]
tf_port_list_v2005 := tf_port_item_v2005 ( comma tf_port_item_v2005_tail )*
tf_port_item_v2005_tail := tf_port_item_v2005 | tf_port_item_v2005_continuation
```

⭐⭐ **THE INTERPRETER IS WHAT MADE THE CORRECTION CHEAP.** `--interpret-parse` (TOOLBOX §1.5b) gives
a verdict against the raw `.ebnf` in **seconds, with no codegen and no `rustc`**, so the design was
iterated to correctness *before* paying the ~20-minute release-probe rebuild — which was paid once,
for the right grammar. Had the first shape been validated only through the generated parser, the
correction would have cost two full rebuild cycles instead of one.

**VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND BOTH EDITIONS** (interpreter first, then the regenerated parser):

| under `verilog_2005` | verdict |
|---|---|
| `t(a, b)` · `t(integer a, b)` · `t(input integer a, integer b)` · `f(a)` · the two pinned repros | **REJECT** ✅ |
| `t(input integer a, b)` · `t(input integer a, output integer b)` · `t()` · non-ANSI `task t; input a;` · `f(input integer a)` · `f(input integer a, b)` · non-ANSI `function` · `f([7:0] ranges)` | **ACCEPT** ✅ |
| **under `sv_2017`: every one of the above** | **ACCEPT** ✅ (IEEE 1800 relaxation preserved) |

**ROUTING EVIDENCE** (`ROUTING-EVIDENCE` doctrine):

  outcome file that hides a *fix* inflates the bar, so the campaign works on phantoms; a stale one
  that hides a *regression* deflates it, so the campaign ships. Both are silent, and nothing in the

  manifests and says so in its own header: *"it does not re-adjudicate the corpus."*
- **Reproduces beyond this row by construction, and the mechanism is sharper than "no identity
  block"** — `results.tsv` / `results_v2005.tsv` are **`.gitignore`d** (`.gitignore:424-427`,

  is defensible on size and the reasoning behind it is exactly one step short**: the DERIVED
  artifacts it points at (`characterization.md`, the adjudication manifests) are tracked and two of
  them carry identity blocks — but an identity block on a derivation cannot detect that its own
  INPUT was measured against yesterday's parser. Same shape as `SV-CORPUS-DENOMINATOR`'s own stated
  limit, one layer further down. ⇒ a **`CLAIM_VERIFICATION` leg-3 breach on the campaign's
  foundational input**, not a housekeeping note. They are the INPUT to every number this campaign
  publishes: the bar, the denominator tuple, and every burn-down delta quoted in the book.
- **Owed:** (a) the outcome files are `.gitignore`d, so an identity block cannot live IN them — put
  the producing run's identity (grammar digest + generated-parser sha + probe fingerprint + row
  count) into the TRACKED artifact they feed, and have the adjudicator REFUSE when the outcome file
  it reads does not match it; (b) decide whether a grammar-revision commit must
  re-run the lanes, or whether the identity check is enough to make the staleness LOUD — `.13i`'s
  finding is that only the gate-checked one never went stale; (c) size how often it has happened:
  the register now lists every grammar revision, so the population is derivable rather than
  guessed.

###### `.13e.6` (a) — **THE MECHANISM: the runner stamps the DUMPS it wrote into the tracked report, and the adjudicator REFUSES a dump that report does not describe** (2026-09-02, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0333`; PRODUCER + ADJUDICATOR tier, ZERO Rust / grammar / codegen / generated bytes)

**THE SHAPE (a) ASKED FOR, AND WHY IT IS A DIGEST AND NOT A RECONCILIATION.** The owed item is
*"put the producing run's identity … into the TRACKED artifact they feed, and have the adjudicator
REFUSE when the outcome file it reads does not match it"*. The obvious cheap form — hold the
report's per-sub-corpus verdict COUNTS equal to the dump — **looks equivalent and is not**: two
files swapping verdicts inside one sub-corpus **cancel**, which is exactly the multiset trap
`PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0160` paid for and re-keyed onto the PATH. A **sha256 of the dump
itself** has no such hole, costs one streamed read, and is the same primitive
`BASELINE-IDENTITY` already uses everywhere else in this repository.

**WHAT LANDED.**

- `stimuli/run_external_corpus.sh` writes **two more identity rows** — `results (output)` and
  `positions (output)` — digesting the dumps **this run just wrote**, and the block's own prose now
  separates the three INPUT rows (re-hash them to know the report still describes your tree) from
  the OUTPUT rows (re-hash them to know the DUMP is the one these numbers describe).
- `stimuli/sv/adjudicate_external_corpus.py` gains `verify_outcome_identity()`, called **once per
  lane** before either lane reads a row, with `--report` / `--report-v2005` seams so the arms can be
  driven against fixtures. A mismatch is `SystemExit` naming the exact re-run; an **absent output
  row** is `NOT EVALUATED`, printed loudly, so an older tree adjudicates exactly as it did before
  and says so.

⭐ **THE IDENTITY TRANSFERS THROUGH THE TRACKED FILE, WHICH IS THE POINT `.13e.6` MADE AND COULD NOT
ACT ON.** Its own words: *"an identity block on a derivation cannot detect that its own INPUT was
measured against yesterday's parser."* It cannot — but the report and the dump are **two outputs of
one run**, so digesting the dump INTO the report closes the loop from the other side: the report
says WHICH parser, and the digest says the dump on disk is that parser's.

**THE BANK — `docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/outcome_identity/probe.sh`, `OUTCOME-IDENTITY: 8/8
as declared`, ~5 s, nothing tracked mutated** (every fixture and all five adjudicator outputs are
redirected under `rust/target/`).

| arm | what it drives | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| A | a matching digest | OK, **and it says so** — a silent pass is not a reading |
| B | **RED**: the dump on disk is a different one | REFUSED, naming the re-run |
| C | a report with no output row | NOT EVALUATED, loudly, naming `.13e.6` |
| D | a recorded row for an ABSENT dump | OK — only a PRESENT dump can be the WRONG dump |
| E | an absent report | NOT EVALUATED, never a pass |
| F | a digest for a DIFFERENT dump | still NOT EVALUATED — it does not vouch for this one |
| G | **END-TO-END**: the real adjudicator, real corpus, mutated report fixture | rc≠0, `is NOT the dump` |
| H | END-TO-END GREEN control: the real tree | rc 0 |

⭐ **G AND H EXIST BECAUSE A CORRECT FUNCTION NOTHING CALLS IS `GATE-REACHABILITY`'s SUBJECT.** Arms
A–F import `verify_outcome_identity` and prove the predicate; only G and H prove the **wiring** —
that both lanes actually call it, before either reads a row.

⚠️ **HONEST BOUND, and it is why (b) is still owed**: this makes a stale dump **LOUD**, not
impossible. It answers *"is the dump I am reading the one the tracked report describes?"* and says
nothing about whether that report is itself stale against today's parser — which is
`CORPUS-CENSUS-CURRENCY`'s job and is now wired for both SV lanes (`.13j`(c), `.13m`). The two
compose: the census gate holds the report to the tree, and this holds the dump to the report.

⭐ **AND THE RE-MEASURE THIS SLICE HAD TO RUN IS ITSELF A NO-REGRESSION MEASUREMENT WORTH RECORDING.**
The full 16 336-file `sv` lane was re-run under the memory guard (81 s, peak 4 756 MB) to confirm the
new rows render: **every verdict reproduced** — `pass=9811 fail=6525 timeout=0 crash=0`, and
re-running the adjudicator over it left `adjudication_manifest.tsv`, both summaries, the v2005
manifest and the lane list **byte-identical** (`git status` clean on every tracked artifact).

⛔⛔ **LANDING THE STAMP CAUGHT A DEFECT IN THE READER, AND THE BANK IS WHAT CAUGHT IT.** The
end-to-end arm G built its fixture by **appending** a wrong-digest `results (output)` row after the

report grew a `results (output)` row of its own, the fixture carried **two** rows for one path, the

dump**. `OUTCOME-IDENTITY: 7/8`. Two corrections, both shipped here:

- **the reader REFUSES a self-disagreeing table** — two rows for one path with different digests is
  `SystemExit` (*"records TWO different digests … cannot vouch for anything"*), never a precedence
  question; an identical repeat is not a disagreement and does not refuse;
- **the fixture REPLACES or INSERTS, never appends** — a single-row mutation whatever the report
  carries.

Two new arms pin the property (**G1** self-disagreeing → REFUSED; **G2** identical repeat → OK), and
the bank reads **`OUTCOME-IDENTITY: 10/10 as declared`**.

###### `.13e.6` (b)+(c) — **(c) MEASURED OVER THE WHOLE HISTORY: the tracked report was stale at 11 of 35 scoreable grammar revisions, 7 of them describing a DIFFERENT LANGUAGE; (b) RULED: a grammar revision without a re-measure is already BLOCKED, not merely loud, and the natural experiment across the gate's wiring date reads 11-of-31 before, 0-of-4 after** (2026-09-02, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0335`; INSTRUMENT + RULING tier, ZERO Rust / grammar / codegen / generated bytes)

**(c) — HOW OFTEN IT HAPPENED, DERIVED FROM GIT OBJECTS AND NEVER FROM THE WORKING TREE.**
`docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/outcome_staleness_census/census.sh` walks every commit that
touched `grammars/systemverilog.ebnf` and, at each, compares the grammar blob's sha256 to the digest
the tracked `characterization.md` **at that same commit** recorded in its identity table:

```text
OUTCOME-STALENESS: grammar_revisions=312 scored=35 fresh=24 stale=11 stale_runs=7 no_report=230 no_identity=47 newest_stale=94ce18ff (2026-08-26)
```

230 revisions predate the report (first tracked 2026-06-17, `4dee0904`); 47 carry a report with no
identity table (the block was added mid-history) and are counted, never scored. Of the **35** that
can be judged, **11 were stale** — the published corpus numbers sat beside a grammar they did not
describe — in **7 runs**, the longest being **five consecutive semantic grammar revisions**
(`ac2aa012` 08-24 → `94ce18ff` 08-26) all measured against `3aba01ec`: that run is `.13e.5`'s
three-day episode, seen from history rather than by accident. In **0 of 11** stale commits was the
report touched (`git diff-tree`), which is the mechanism in one number — the grammar moved and
nothing asked the report to follow.

⭐⭐ **STALE BY BYTES IS NOT STALE BY MEANING, AND THE SPLIT IS THE FINDING `.13r` NEEDED.**
`classify.sh` recovers, for each stale row, the revision the report was actually measured against
(its recorded byte-sha looked up against every grammar blob in history — never guessed; a
non-matching sha would be `UNCLASSIFIED`, and there are 0) and compares the two grammars' **semantic
digests** — the frontend's own `raw_ast` envelope, the same recipe `check_sv_contract_currency.sh`
uses, so a comment cannot move it:

```text
OUTCOME-STALENESS-CLASS: stale=11 different_language=7 same_language=4 unclassified=0
```

| verdict | revisions | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| `DIFFERENT_LANGUAGE` | **7** — `94ce18ff`, `ea01160b`, `c46cac8c`, `2e492d08`, `ac2aa012`, `958fcc24`, `fdade1ce` | the published numbers described a grammar accepting a **different language** |
| `SAME_LANGUAGE` | **4** — `e28cc856`, `6ad18e48`, `59ec1f02`, `d1fadfaf` | stale by bytes only — comment / documentation edits (two of them literally titled *"comment-only"*) |

⇒ **7 of 35 scoreable grammar revisions (20 %) shipped corpus numbers about a language that was not
in the tree**, and **4 of 11 stale readings were false alarms a semantic digest would not have
raised** — which is exactly the price `.13r` was opened to measure, now measured over the whole
history rather than estimated: annotated onto `.13r` below.

⚠️ **HONEST BOUND, stated rather than implied.** The census measures how often the report was stale;
it does **not** measure how many verdicts each staleness hid — that would need the corpus re-run at
each of the 7 revisions under each revision's parser (7 × ~22 min rebuilds + 7 × 80 s), which is not
this slice's price. The one episode that WAS measured (`.13e.5`) hid one fix. So the honest sentence
is *"7 times the bar was about the wrong language; at least once it was numerically wrong"*, not
*"7 wrong bars"*.

**(b) — RULED: BLOCKED, NOT LOUD — and ruled on a measurement, not on the design.** The question was
*"must a grammar-revision commit re-run the lanes, or is the identity check enough to make the
staleness LOUD?"*. Since `.13j`(c) wired `systemverilog_raw_parse` (2026-08-31) and `.13m` wired
`systemverilog_v2005_raw_parse`, `CORPUS-CENSUS-CURRENCY` arm (3) re-hashes the grammar against both
tracked reports **on every commit, from `.githooks/pre-commit`**, and a mismatch is a **HARD
breach** — so a grammar edit without a re-measure cannot commit. Two independent legs:

- **the natural experiment the census hands over for free**: split at the wiring date, the
  scoreable revisions read **11 stale of 31 before 2026-08-31** and **0 stale of 4 after**, and all
  four post-gate grammar revisions (`a072e23e`, `1b482789`, `c4b2fe1b`, `03ca8d58`) touched the
  report **in the same commit** — the gate forcing the re-measure, visible in history;
- **the RED control**, `probe_b.sh` → `OUTCOME-STALENESS-BLOCKS: 5/5 as declared`: for BOTH SV lanes
  a copy of the real report with its grammar row zeroed drives the gate through the schema seam to
  **rc 1, `has MOVED since this census was measured`**, the untouched schema reads GREEN, and the
  gate is confirmed registered in `check_doctrines.sh` with the pre-commit hook running the registry.

⇒ **(b)'s answer is that nothing more is owed on the SV lanes**: the re-run is mandatory by gate, not

`var_qualifier_sv_only`, `declaration_lifetime_sv_only`, `extern_keyword_sv_only`,

`checker_rand_qualifier_sv_only`, `array_method_with_sv_only` — plus **one whole-rule** `@profiles`
gate on `streaming_concatenation`.

⭐⭐ **THE STREAMING CONCATENATION IS A FOURTH LENS, AND IT WAS FOUND WHILE FIXING THE FIRST THREE.**
`{ << { a } }` and `{ >> { a } }` PARSED under `verilog_2005`; "streaming" occurs **0 times** in the
IEEE 1364-2005 Annex A. ⛔ **No keyword-level census can ever see it, because `<<` and `>>` are
OPERATORS** — an IEEE-1800-only construct that introduces no keyword at all. Call it **L4,
PUNCTUATION-ONLY**, alongside (c)'s L1/L2/L3. It is gated here as a whole rule; **nothing enumerates
the rest of its class**, which is routed to `.13e.10`.

⛔⛔ **`lifetime` MUST NOT BE GATED, and the controls are what enforce that.** IEEE 1364-2005 A.2.6
`:254` and A.2.7 `:275` give `function` and `task` a legitimate `[ automatic ]`, and both parse
under `verilog_2005` today. The gate therefore sits on the `( lifetime )?` OPTIONAL at
`data_declaration_sv_2017`, `block_data_declaration_sv_2017`, `module_ansi_header:3679`,
`module_nonansi_header` and `module_declaration_sv_2017`'s wildcard alternative — the `.13e.4` idiom
— and `control_v2005_function_automatic.sv` / `control_v2005_task_automatic.sv` go RED if it is ever
widened.

⛔⛔ **THE FIRST INSERTION SILENTLY STOLE TWO PRE-EXISTING GATES, AND THE LINT CAUGHT IT.** Placing a
new rule immediately before its alphabetical anchor drops it BETWEEN that anchor's own
`@profiles:` annotation and the rule the annotation belongs to. Measured: `extern_tf_declaration`
and `immediate_assertion_statement` both lost `@profiles: ["sv_2017","sv_2023"]` and became
`verilog_2005` profile ORPHANS — `--lint-grammar` named both with a derived fix. The applier now
walks back over the anchor's contiguous comment/annotation header before inserting.
⇒ **an annotation binds to the next rule, so inserting a rule is an edit to whatever precedes it.**

**MEASURED — the grammar side, before a single byte was generated:**

| instrument | before → after |
|---|---|
| `--lint-grammar` | rules `1524 → 1537`; `profile_orphans` **0**, `unreachable_rules` **0**, `undefined_references` **0**, `non_terminating` **0**, `left_recursion_unhandled` **0** — all unchanged |
| `--dump-rule-profiles` | `sv_2017` **1388 → 1401**, `sv_2023` **1410 → 1423** (both **+13** = exactly the rules added), `verilog_2005` **1148 → 1147** |
| pre-existing rules whose satisfiable set moved | **exactly one** — `streaming_concatenation`, the deliberate whole-rule gate |

⭐ **THE INTERPRETER PAID FOR THE 40-MINUTE CYCLE ONCE.** A full before/after sweep over all **283**
pinned row × profile checks on `--interpret-parse` moved **exactly 17 verdicts, every one `ACCEPT →
reject` under `verilog_2005`, and ZERO under `sv_2017`/`sv_2023`** — the blast radius enumerated in
minutes instead of guessed. The interpreter was FALSIFIED first: it agreed with the shipped parser
on all 48 v2005 pinned rows at HEAD before the edit, and SV's `left_recursion_unhandled=0` clears
the one condition TOOLBOX 1.5b says voids it.

⛔⛔ **AND THE FIRST SWEEP WAS GARBAGE IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION.** Its baseline arm was pointed at
`systemverilog.ebnf.bak`; the frontend refuses that path (`Error: expected value at line 1 column
1`), and **a load failure is indistinguishable from a parse rejection at the exit code** — so it
reported **160** moved verdicts, all `reject → ACCEPT`, on rows the change cannot touch. The number
was too good and too uniform to be real, which is the only reason it was checked. The harness now
REFUSES unless each arm emits an `INTERPRET-PARSE:` verdict line, and asserts both arms accept a
smoke test before it measures anything.

`.13c.2m`'s row has existed since 2026-08-18 — and its carrier is `int y, m;`, which

incapable of reporting the `verilog_2005` leak, and only re-declaring the same text over an

explicit that the remedy stays `.13c.2m`'s (delete the bogus keyword in every profile); gating it
under `verilog_2005` would make the parser correct in one profile and leave it wrong in two.

⭐ **BOTH RED CONTROLS WERE OBSERVED, not assumed.** (1) filing `accepts_invalid_v2005_chandle.sv`

`data_declaration_sv_2017` and instead reach a `_v2005` sibling shaped like IEEE 1364-2005
A.2.1.3's actual `integer_declaration` / `time_declaration` / `real_declaration` /
`reg_declaration` / `event_declaration` set — or should each over-acceptance be gated where it
sits?

**RULING: gate per site with the named `_sv_only` idiom. The structural sibling is REFUSED.**
⛔ **And this is not a preference — (c)'s census turned it into arithmetic.** Every confirmed
over-acceptance's `verilog_2005`-LIVE referring rules were derived from the profile-filtered
graph (not read off the file), and the declaration-shaped subset was counted:

| construct | distinct v2005-live sites | reachable through a declaration rule? |
|---|---|---|
| `chandle` · `enum` · `virtual` | 2 each — `data_type`, `block_data_type` | ✅ |
| `string` | 3 — + `casting_type` | ✅ |
| `const` | 3 — `data_declaration_sv_2017`, `block_data_declaration_sv_2017`, `casting_type` | ✅ |
| `var` | 7 — + `for_variable_declaration`, `tf_port_declaration`, `tf_port_item_v2005`, `tf_port_item_v2005_continuation`, `var_data_type` | ✅ |
| `static` · `automatic` | 1 — `lifetime` | ❌ |
| `extern` | 2 — `module_declaration_sv_2017`, `udp_declaration_sv_2017` | ❌ |
| `iff` | 3 — `checker_or_generate_item_declaration`, `event_expression_primary`, `module_or_generate_item_declaration` | ❌ |
| `join_any` · `join_none` | 1 — `join_keyword` | ❌ |
| `rand` | 1 — `checker_or_generate_item_declaration` | ❌ |
| `with` | 2 — `array_manipulation_call`, `stream_expression` | ❌ |

**14 constructs · 19 distinct v2005-live grammar sites · a `data_declaration_v2005` sibling
reaches 6 of the 14.** The other eight are a lifetime keyword shared with the LEGAL
`function`/`task` sites, a module header, a UDP header, a `default disable iff` clause, an event
expression, two `fork`-join statements, a checker item and two array/stream method clauses. **None
of them passes through a declaration rule, so the structural rewrite would leave 8 of 14 defects
in place while paying for a cloned `data_type` subtree and a moved `verilog_2005` cert baseline.**

⭐ **THE SUPPORTING ARGUMENTS ALL POINT THE SAME WAY, and they are named as supporting so the
measurement stays the deciding one:** the fix hierarchy is declarative > grammar > engine and the

IDIOM (no inline sub-expression `@profiles` — the named rule costs ~0.0002 % of corpus entries and
buys visibility to four independent instruments); and a per-site gate moves the cert baseline by
one countable rule each, which is exactly how `.13e.4` proved `sv_2017 1387 → 1388` with
`verilog_2005` unmoved at 1148.

  module_parameter_port_list ] …`. `module_ansi_header:3679` carries the IEEE 1800 `( lifetime )?`

census re-found a known defect from a completely different direction is the cross-confirmation
that its reachability model is reading a real parser** — nothing in the census knows `.13c.2m`

###### `.13e.7` (c) — **DONE: the population is CLOSED, MEASURED at 14, and the census that produced it carries its own RED control** (2026-08-24, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0290`; INSTRUMENT tier, ZERO grammar / Rust / codegen / generated bytes)

**What (c) asked for, and why it was widened.** The written task was *"run the same shape census
against `block_data_type`, `net_declaration` and the port declarations"*. Those three rules are a
hand-picked sample chosen by the same reading that produced the nine — the very method
`SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.7`'s own blocker text calls out (*"checked only by a SAMPLE … never by a
closed population"*). Running it would have produced a fourth list nobody could bound. So the
sub-leaf answers the question the sample was a proxy for: **which IEEE-1800-only KEYWORDS can a
`verilog_2005` parse reach at all?** IEEE 1364-2005 Annex B is a closed normative list and PGEN
spells every keyword as its own `kw_*` rule, so that question has a finite, derivable answer over
*every* rule in the grammar, not three.

**The instrument** — `stimuli/sv/v2005_keyword_faithfulness_census.py`, 2.3 s, deterministic:

1. profile-filtered, **alternative-aware** reachability from the four declared entry roots, over
   the EBNF frontend's own `raw_ast` envelope (via `scripts/check_baseline_identity.sh --raw-ast`,
   the single owner of that definition — not a second frontend invocation);
2. intersect with the `kw_*` terminals → the keywords a `verilog_2005` parse can arrive at;
3. subtract IEEE 1364-2005 Annex B → the candidate population;
4. adjudicate every candidate on the **shipped release probe**, three legs (below).

**MEASURED** (`docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/v2005_keyword_faithfulness/census.md`):

```text
V2005-KEYWORD-FAITHFULNESS: reachable_rules=827 reachable_keywords=161 candidates=24
                            over_acceptances=14 gated=10 identifier_consumed=7
```

| | |
|---|---|
| rules in the source grammar | 1 493 |
| satisfiable under `verilog_2005` | 1 129 |
| REACHABLE under `verilog_2005` | **827** |
| keyword literals reachable | 161 — **122** are Annex B keywords, **15** are 1364-2005 symbol terminals (UDP tables, edge descriptors, `PATHPULSE$`), **24** are word-shaped candidates |
| **confirmed over-acceptances** | **14** — `chandle` `class_qualifier` `const` `enum` `extern` `iff` `join_any` `join_none` `rand` `static` `string` `var` `virtual` `with` |
| correctly gated (the control set) | 10 — `clocking` `dist` `inside` `interface` `local` `matches` `packed` `ref` `std` `unique` |
| refuted by leg 3 | 7 — `new` `null` `randomize` `super` `this` `tx_path_delay_expression` `type` |

⛔⛔ **LEG 3 IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN SKIPPED, AND IT MOVED THE HEADLINE BY SEVEN.** A row
is earned only when (1) the release probe ACCEPTS the witness under `verilog_2005`, (2) it ACCEPTS
under `sv_2017` — the control proving the witness is well-formed SV isolating a PROFILE
difference — **and (3) substituting the keyword for a fresh identifier makes it REJECT under
`verilog_2005`**. Legs 1+2 alone reported **21** over-acceptances. Seven were wrong: none of
`type`/`this`/`super`/`new`/`null`/`randomize`/`tx_path_delay_expression` is reserved by IEEE
1364-2005, so `type(y)` is a legal call to a function NAMED `type` — and
`--parse-dump-ast-pretty` puts the literal in a `plain_tf` **function-call** slot, not a keyword
slot. The parser was right and the witness was lying. This is `.13c.2q`'s lesson (*"THE SLOT IS
NAMED, NOT INFERRED"*) arriving as a mechanical third leg rather than as per-row discipline.

⭐ **THE CENSUS CARRIES ITS OWN RED CONTROL, IN THE BASELINE RUN.** The same code, same grammar,
same oracle, under `sv_2017` — where these keywords are native — reaches **136** word-shaped
IEEE-1800-only keywords. So `verilog_2005` **GATES 112 and LEAKS 24**. A census blind to the
profile would print one number twice; the report prints the pair, and the run REFUSES the
degenerate self-comparison (`--profile sv_2017`) by name rather than reporting a flattering
"leaks 0".

⭐ **THE FIRST MODEL WAS WRONG AND THE PROBE CAUGHT IT.** A rule-level reference graph keeps an
edge alive when a MANDATORY SIBLING in the same alternative has been profile-filtered away. It
reported `rand`, `randc`, `packed`, `dist`, `inside`, `local`, `matches`, `std` and `type`
reachable through `data_type`'s struct alternative — whose *first element*, `struct_union`, is
gated to `sv_2017`/`sv_2023`, so `struct { reg a; } s;` cannot open under `verilog_2005` at all
(`furthest_position=16`, exactly at the `{`). Alternative-awareness dropped seven of the nine and
the probe legs refuted the rest. What remains is a deliberate over-approximation (a path gated
only by a `@predicate` or a lookahead still counts as reachable) — false POSITIVES, which the
probe removes; never false negatives, which nothing would.

⛔ **AND ONE PUBLISHED NUMBER HAD TO BE RECONCILED BEFORE IT COULD BE QUOTED.**
`--dump-rule-profiles` runs on the POST-elimination grammar (1 524 rules) and `raw_ast` is the
SOURCE grammar (1 493); the 31 extras are `_lr_*` rules the indirect-left-recursion eliminator
SYNTHESISES, **19 of them `verilog_2005`-satisfiable**. A reachable-vs-satisfiable gap quoted
against the raw `1 148` would have silently folded those 19 in. The report publishes the
intersection (**1 129**) and names the residue, and `1 129 + 19 = 1 148` reconciles to the cert
contract's `expected_total` exactly.

**Refusals proven** — `docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/v2005_keyword_faithfulness/probe.sh`,
**13/13**, including a GREEN control on the real tree so the refusals are not vacuous: the
profile-sensitivity pair, the degenerate self-comparison, `--write` refused under either control
knob (a control run can never become the baseline), a manifest row removed for a reachable
keyword, a manifest naming an absent witness, a witness that cannot run leg 3, a reachable
keyword whose `sv_2017` control fails (an unmeasured HOLE is refused, never counted as clean),
gate-mode DRIFT on a stale artifact, and byte-identical determinism across two writes.
⭐ The missing-witness refusal **fired on its own first real run**, on `with` — a reachable
IEEE-1800-only keyword absent from every hand list this leaf had produced.

##### ⛔⛔ `.13e.8` — **RETRACTED: the finding was FALSE. The engine already crosses profile-filtered reachability with the whole rule set, and has since `VERILOG-2005-PROFILE.6.7`** (opened 2026-08-24 by `.13e.7`(c); **RETRACTED 2026-08-25, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0294`, under director challenge**)

**WHAT I PUBLISHED, AND IT IS WRONG.** This leaf claimed that *"the `verilog_2005` certificate
denominator counts 302 rules no `verilog_2005` input can reach, because BOTH instruments that could
notice are bottom-up … Nothing crosses them"*, and that
`PGEN_CERT_RESIDUAL_CLASSIFICATION`'s `profile_entry_unreachable` class *"is applied to the RESIDUAL
and never to the DENOMINATOR"*. **Both halves are false.**

**WHAT REFUTED IT** — a test this leaf never ran, and the director's challenge is what prompted it.
The contradiction was sitting in my own evidence and I explained it away instead of closing it: the
cert pass reported **1 144 certified rules** under `verilog_2005` while my model said only **827**
were reachable. I wrote that off as *"the witness passes re-route through an alternative parent
carrier"* and never checked. Intersecting the two sets settles it in one command:

```text
proof-covered = 356 · my 'unreachable' set = 323 · overlap = 323 of 323
```

**Every single rule my model calls unreachable is in the certificate pass's `proof` category — an
exact set match, not a correlation.** `gather_verified_profile_proof_covered_rules`
(`rust/src/ast_pipeline/grammar_wellformedness.rs:3017`, wired on the cert path at
`rust/src/main.rs:3409`) classifies the **WHOLE active rule set** — its own comment says so, and it
passes `rule_order` as the candidate universe — and issues every `profile_entry_unreachable` rule a
`ProfileEntryUnreachable` certificate that is **independently RE-VERIFIED**, with a re-verify
failure reported as *a LINTER BUG, never silently covered*. The pre-fix numbers corroborate:
302 unreachable against 334 proof, 323 against 356 — the same ~32-rule remainder both times.

⭐ **AND COUNTING THEM AS CERTIFIED IS SOUND, not a loophole.** The engine's own justification is
correct: a rule not positively reachable from any declared entry *can never be exercised by an
accepted parse*, so the transactional witness primitive correctly never records it — demanding a
witness would be impossible by construction. There is no defect here to fix.

⛔⛔ **THE SHAPE OF MY ERROR IS THE ONE `-0289` HAD CORRECTED ME ON ONE COMMIT EARLIER.** That
retraction was of the claim *"`verilog_2005` faithfulness is checked by NOTHING"*, and its lesson
was recorded as: **an "X is checked by nothing" claim is a CENSUS claim, and must not be published
without running the census.** I then opened this leaf with *"nothing crosses the two"* — the
identical form — on the identical subject, having read two `grammar_wellformedness.rs` functions and
not looked for a third. ⇒ **reading two implementations is not a census of implementations.** The
cheap check I skipped is `grep -n "fn .*profile.*proof\|fn .*proof.*profile"`, which names the
function in one line.

⚠️ **A SECOND OVERCLAIM IN THE SAME LEAF, ALSO REFUTED.** It said the census's reachability model
was cross-confirmed by cert-coverage's own reach computation. Measured: cert-coverage's
`NO reach path from the entry` list is **11 rules and my model calls all 11 REACHABLE — agreement
on 0 of 11.** Neither is wrong; they answer different questions (mine unions the four declared entry
roots, that warning was produced under a single `--entry-rule systemverilog_file`). But *"the two
instruments agree"* was asserted and never checked, which is the same failure one level down.

**WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS WORTH KEEPING:**

- **`--dump-rule-profiles`' `satisfiable_under` is bottom-up and does NOT mean reachable.** The

after** `.13e.7` (`git show ac2aa012^:grammars/systemverilog.ebnf`, `grep -cF` = 1 on both sides for
each of the four):

| when | commit | what happened |
|---|---|---|
| **2026-04-22** | `cd8770cd` *"SV stimuli: promote header seeds to rule-level"* | `@sample: "module m(input logic a);"` written. Only SV profiles existed — **the sample was CORRECT.** |

⭐⭐⭐ **THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON, AND IT IS ENGINE-UNIVERSAL RATHER THAN SV:**
**adding a profile retroactively invalidates every profile-blind annotation already in the grammar,
and nothing re-checks them.** A profile NARROWS the accepted language, so every literal already
written against the wider language becomes a candidate defect the moment the narrower profile
exists. This binds any PGEN grammar that ever gains a profile. ⚠️ Two of the ten cleared residuals
(`data_type_or_void`, `function_statement`) were UNKNOWN **before** `.13e.7` — i.e. the defect was
already costing certificate coverage for 54 days, in a number the project publishes.

## ⛔ THE REGISTER HAD NO HONEST SLOT FOR THIS CHANGE, AND THAT WAS ITS OWN DEFECT

`PGEN_SV_GRAMMAR_REVISION_REGISTER.tsv` defined two dispositions: `RELEASE` (contract section + bug
ledger row) and `NEUTRAL` (comment-only; **digest EQUALS its predecessor's**). A `@sample` repair
fits NEITHER — annotations are in the `raw_ast` and comments are not, so the digest MOVES
(`470d4998… → 6cffb405…`) and `NEUTRAL` refutes itself, while `RELEASE` would buy its currency check
with a bug-ledger row describing a defect **no released parser has**. ⇒ a third disposition,
`GENERATOR-ONLY`, whose claim is STRONGER than `NEUTRAL`'s and cheaper to check than tier D: *the
digest moved and the generated parser did not*. New **tier E** re-hashes
`generated/systemverilog_parser.rs` against the row's `parser_sha256=`; on a clone with no
`generated/` it reports **NOT EVALUATED, loudly, never a pass**. ⚠️ HONEST BOUND, stated before the
tier is trusted: tier E compares the row against the parser PRESENT in `generated/`; that this is
the parser HEAD's grammar produces is `GENERATED-REPRODUCIBILITY`'s job. The two compose; neither
alone is the argument.

⛔ **A green enforcer proves nothing until its refusals fire.** All five drove RED, and the register
was restored byte-identical (`cmp`) with a GREEN control re-run on the real tree afterwards:

| control | verdict |
|---|---|
| `parser_sha256` wrong | ✗ tier E refuses, naming both hashes |
| `parser_sha256` absent | ✗ tier C refuses |
| `GENERATOR-ONLY` + a release number | ✗ tier C refuses |
| digest EQUALS predecessor's (i.e. really `NEUTRAL`) | ✗ tier C refuses — **verified to be the INTENDED arm**, `grep -c` = 1, not merely a neighbouring tier reacting to the same edit |
| disposition `MAYBE` | ✗ refuses; "only RELEASE, NEUTRAL and GENERATOR-ONLY are defined" |

  **L4 — PUNCTUATION-ONLY**.

###### `.13e.10` (a)+(b) — **DONE: the population is CLOSED, DERIVED and MEASURED at 19, and the oracle had to be rebuilt twice before it could be trusted** (2026-08-25, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0298`; INSTRUMENT tier)

**WHAT LANDED.** `stimuli/sv/v2005_punctuation_faithfulness_census.py` — read-only, changes no byte
of grammar, parser or any tracked artifact. It REUSES `.13e.7`(c)'s reachability rather than
re-implementing it, so L1 and L4 are commensurable by construction and one fix to the reach model
fixes both.

| | measured |
|---|---|
| rules reachable under `verilog_2005` | **805** (source-satisfiable 1128; 19 eliminator-synthesised rules excluded as unadjudicable) |
| terminal rules in the SOURCE grammar | 383 — string-literal **73**, regex **310** |
| non-keyword string-literal terminals | **72**, of which **68** are REACHABLE under `verilog_2005` |
| oracle: IEEE 1364-2005 Annex A | **386** productions over 851 BNF lines ⇒ punctuation alphabet **60** tokens |
| **VERDICT** | 49 reachable punctuation terminals appear in that alphabet; **19 DO NOT** |

**THE 19 CANDIDATES.** `<<<=` `>>>=` `!=?` `<->` `<<=` `==?` `>>=` `%=` `&=` `*=` `++` `+=` `--`
`-=` `.*` `/=` `^=` `|=` and `'`.

⛔⛔ **THE ORACLE'S FIRST CUT WAS A SUBSTRING COUNT AND IT FAILED IN THE SILENT DIRECTION.**
`annex_a.count("--")` reported the decrement operator **present, twice**. Both occurrences are the
**YAML front-matter delimiter `---`** on lines 1 and 9 of the tracked file. IEEE 1364-2005 has no
decrement operator, so the count produced a **false negative on a real member of the population** —
and substring counting can only err in that direction, which makes its zeros sound and its
non-zeros worthless. Replaced by a set-vs-set comparison over a tokenized BNF, which recovers `--`
and `'`. ⇒ **an instrument's census is only as good as its own tokenizer** — the operator-level twin
of [[a-heading-census-is-only-as-good-as-the-heading-grammar]].

⛔⛔ **AND THE TERMINAL EXTRACTOR WAS BLIND ON EXACTLY THE MEMBERS THIS LENS CARES ABOUT.** A
terminal is `name := trivia <literal> -> {…}`, so the obvious extractor splits the body on the
return-annotation arrow `->`. A terminal whose LITERAL CONTAINS THAT ARROW is truncated:
`iff_arrow := trivia "<->"` read as `"<`, `implies := trivia "->"` read as `"`. Both are operators,
which is the whole subject of L4 — the extractor was silent precisely where it mattered, and the
population read **66** instead of **68**. Parse the literal ANCHORED first, then require the
remainder to be empty or an annotation. ⇒ **when your delimiter is also legal content, anchor the
parse; do not split.**

⛔ **FOUR REFUSAL ARMS, ALL OBSERVED FIRING at the published refusal code `2`**, plus a GREEN control
on the real tree in the same run:

| control | verdict |
|---|---|
| oracle (Annex A) missing | ✗ `rc=2` REFUSED — "the oracle is absent, so this instrument has nothing to compare against" |
| oracle truncated to 20 productions | ✗ `rc=2` REFUSED — "a shrunken alphabet reports phantom candidates in the FLATTERING direction" |
| front matter opens and never closes | ✗ `rc=2` REFUSED — guessing where it ends is how the `--` false negative was produced |
| grammar with no literal terminals | ✗ `rc=2` REFUSED — "a census that reads nothing must refuse rather than report an empty candidate set" |
| the real tree | ✓ `rc=0`, **19 candidates** |

⛔ **AND THE FIRST RUN OF THOSE CONTROLS FOUND A DEFECT IN MY OWN REFUSAL PATH.** The missing-oracle
arm died with a `ValueError` **traceback and exit 1** instead of the published refusal code `2`,
because the message formatted its path with `Path.relative_to`, which RAISES on a path outside the
repo root. The only call site was inside a refusal message — the least-exercised branch in the file.
⇒ **a check that tracebacks is indistinguishable from a check that is broken**, so the FORMATTING of
a refusal must not be able to fail. Routed through a helper that cannot raise.

⚠️ **HONEST BOUNDS, stated before the number is quoted:**
1. The Annex A alphabet includes BNF **metasyntax** (`{` `}` `[` `]` `|`), which is indistinguishable
   from Verilog's own braces and brackets in that document. This can only make a candidate look
   ACCOUNTED-FOR, never manufacture one — and none of the 19 is metasyntax.

|---|---|---|
| `rule_entry_counts[R]` | **INVOCATIONS of `R`'s generated rule method** — one monotone `fetch_add`, never rolled back, delta'd past a pre-parse baseline. ⚠️ a memo **HIT** still invokes the method, so a hit counts. | `ast_based_generator.rs:4285` + `:7122` (`inlined_frame_call`) |
| `rule_committed_counts[R]` | **OCCURRENCES of `R` in the FULLY EXPANDED derivation tree of the accepted parse.** ⛔ **not a counter at all** — a post-parse FOLD over `coverage_stack` + `coverage_deltas`. | fold `:1973`; push `:4295`/`:7125`; truncate-on-fail `:9318`; body `split_off` + `REPLAY\|d` marker `:9776`; memo-hit marker `:9586` |
| `rule_memo_hit_counts[R]` | `record_memo_hit` inside `memoized_call`, same coverage opt-in. | `:9586` region |

⇒ **A MEMO HIT ON AN *ANCESTOR* OF `R` ADDS AN OCCURRENCE OF `R` WITHOUT INVOKING `R` AT ALL.**
That is the whole mechanism, and it is the point of `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.22`(e): the memoized
body's slots are moved into a side table and replaced by ONE marker, which the fold expands *with
its multiplicity*. The DAG is counted, not materialised — so the count is the TREE's, while the
entry counter is the DAG's.

**(b) — RULED: a DOCUMENTED, HANDLED CONSEQUENCE, not a defect.** Three independent supports:

1. **RE-DERIVED by command.** `dot_star` **entered 1 / committed 3**; the enclosing
   `list_of_port_connections` is invoked **3×** — **1 memo miss + 2 memo hits** — and its body delta
   contains `dot_star` once. Rule id `571` resolved against the generated `RULE_NAMES` table rather
   than inferred from the trace frame.
2. **FALSIFIED against an oracle I did not build, and the control MOVES.** `--trace-rules
   list_of_port_connections` independently reports `Memo hit for rule 571` **×2** — the trace and
   the counter maps agree on the *derivation*, not merely on the verdict. The **multiplicity law**
   is the falsifier: two `.*` sites must give committed **6** and memo hits **4**, and they do. A
   miscounting counter has no reason to land on exactly 2×.
3. **THE PRIMARY CONSUMER ALREADY HANDLED IT — this was never unknown to the engine, only to
   TOOLBOX.** `--fusibility-outcome-counts` carries a named `committed_overshoot` field, accumulates
   it with `saturating_sub` so a per-rule discard can never go silently negative
   (`fusibility_census.rs:2493`), and prints a loud `WARNING: committed_overshoot=…` (`:5528`). Its
   own doc-comment names both contributors.

⭐ **AND THE `35 vs 298` HALF OF THE ROUTING NOTE DISSOLVES ENTIRELY.** The maps are **NESTED, not
disjoint**: 298 rules had their method invoked, 35 survive into the accepted tree, and
**committed-not-entered = 0** (measured, exact set containment). The 263-rule gap is ordinary
truncated speculation. Only **5** rules overshoot, and all five sit inside the memo-shared subtree
above.

truncates coverage only on its **Err** arm, so a **positive lookahead that SUCCEEDS** keeps its
inner pushes while its position is restored by hand (`generate_lookahead_logic`). Measured over
comment-stripped `grammars/systemverilog.ebnf`: **7** positive-lookahead sites, every one a
*peek-the-token-the-next-element-consumes* shape, so today it inflates a multiplicity rather than
manufacturing a phantom. ⛔ **That is a property of THIS GRAMMAR, not of the instrument** — a
`&( X )` whose body is not subsequently consumed would put `X`'s rules in `committed` without them
appearing in the accepted tree. Stated as a standing caveat rather than a clean bill of health.

  the measurement that a blocker firing on legacy teaches bypass. That ruling does NOT apply here,
  and the reason is arithmetic rather than taste: `.13e.9`'s fix already drove the population to
  **0 defects over 115 checks**, so a FULL-population blocker fires on nothing on day one.
  ⇒ **a guard is safe to make blocking over its whole population exactly when the fix precedes it.**
- ⛔⛔ **PREMISE UPDATE 2026-08-25 (`.13e.10`(c4) / `-0305`) — THIS LEAF'S FOUNDING ARITHMETIC IS NO
  LONGER TRUE, AND THE COMMIT THAT BROKE IT IS THE ONE THAT WROTE THIS PARAGRAPH.** The routing
  evidence above rests on *"`.13e.9`'s fix already drove the population to **0** defects over 115
  checks, so a FULL-population blocker fires on nothing on day one."* Gating the sixteen IEEE-1800-only
  punctuation terminals moved it to **1**. MEASURED, not reasoned — and the first draft of this note
  said **2**, which the measurement refuted:

  | `@sample` site | owning rule's `@profiles` | verdict |
  |---|---|---|
  | `module_declaration_sv_2017:3866` `"module m(.*); endmodule"` | ⛔ `["sv_2017", "verilog_2005"]` | `sv_2017`=ACCEPT, **`verilog_2005`=REJECT** — the offender |
  | `module_declaration_sv_2023:3878` (same text, `dot star` spelling) | `["sv_2023"]` | ACCEPT ✅ |
  | `program_declaration_sv_2017:4985` `"program p(.*); endprogram"` | `["sv_2017"]` | ACCEPT ✅ |
  | `program_declaration_sv_2023:4997` | `["sv_2023"]` | ACCEPT ✅ |

  ⭐ **The discriminator is the OWNING RULE's profile list, not the sample's text** — three of the four
  samples spell an SV-only `.*` and are perfectly correct, because their rule is never live under
  `verilog_2005`. A guard keying on the text would report 4 false positives out of 4; keying on the
  rule reports exactly 1. That is this leaf's real design constraint, now with a live example.
- ⭐ **AND THE OFFENDER HAS A MEASURED COST, so it is not a hygiene item:** it is why the
  `verilog_2005` certificate baseline moved `witness 774 -> 757 / UNKNOWN 17 -> 18` in `-0305`. The
  one rule that fell to UNKNOWN, `kw_macromodule_df04b866`, still PARSES (`macromodule m; endmodule`
  accepts under all three profiles; `--dump-rule-outcome-counts-json` reports it `committed=1` under
  `verilog_2005`) — the certificate pass simply lost its ROUTE to a sample when that alternative
  became unsatisfiable. Same class as `.13e.7`'s UNKNOWN +7, which `.13e.9` paid back in full.
  ⇒ **fixing this one sample is expected to return `kw_macromodule_df04b866` to `witness`**, and that
  is this leaf's first acceptance arm rather than a hoped-for side effect.
- ⚠️ **The honest residual, stated before the leaf is scoped:** 7 of the 115 checks reject and are
  CORRECT (a branch dead under `verilog_2005` whose sample is honest). A naive guard would fire on
  all 7. The join is the culprit — `satisfiable_under` is RULE-level while 43 of 52 samples are
  BRANCH-level — so the leaf owes either branch-level profile satisfiability or an explicit,
  justified allow-list. **Building the guard on the rule-level join would ship a 7/11 false-positive
  rate**, which is the `.6`/`.12` shape that was refused.
- **Owed:** (a) derive branch-level profile satisfiability, or price the allow-list; (b) wire the
  check as a gate arm with a RED control proven firing; (c) decide whether it is an SV gate arm or a
  registered doctrine — it is grammar-agnostic, so the second is the honest home, and every PGEN
  grammar with both `@profiles` and `@sample` is in its population, not just SystemVerilog.

###### `.13e.11` (a) — **DONE: branch-level profile satisfiability is DERIVED IN THE ENGINE, the census reads 0 defects over 101 checks — and running it REFUTED this leaf's own founding arm** (2026-08-26, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0307`; ENGINE/ANALYSIS + INSTRUMENT tier, ZERO grammar-semantic / codegen / generated bytes)

⛔⛔ **THE FOUNDING ARM IS REFUTED, AND THE TOOLBOX REFUTED IT ON THE FIRST COMMAND.** The premise
update written into this leaf by `-0305` — and asserted a second time in a TRACKED CONTRACT
(`rust/test_data/grammar_quality/verilog_2005_conformance_contract_v0.json`, `cert.baseline_note`) —
says *"fixing this one sample is expected to return `kw_macromodule_df04b866` to `witness`, and that
is this leaf's first acceptance arm rather than a hoped-for side effect."* **It is not, in either
half.** The `@sample` is not a defect, and repairing its text could not have moved the certificate.

⭐ **HALF ONE — THE SAMPLE IS HONEST, AND THE ENGINE NOW SAYS SO BY DERIVATION RATHER THAN BY HAND.**
`module_declaration_sv_2017` branch 2 spells `.*` and its branch is DEAD under `verilog_2005` once
`-0305` gated `dot_star`. That is verbatim the class `.13e.9` had already adjudicated for branches
**3 and 4 of the same rule** (`extern module m(a);`, `extern module m;`) and recorded as *"branch
DEAD under v2005 — sample honest"*. `-0305` placed the new sibling in a different class than the two
it sits beside, because it joined on the sample's OWNING RULE rather than on the sample's own BRANCH:

```
$ ast_pipeline grammars/systemverilog.ebnf --dump-rule-profiles rp.json
  module_declaration_sv_2017:
    declared_profiles         ["sv_2017", "verilog_2005"]
    satisfiable_under         ["sv_2017", "verilog_2005"]     <- the rule-level view: BLIND
    branch_satisfiable_under  [["sv_2017","verilog_2005"],    <- 0  module m; endmodule
                               ["sv_2017","verilog_2005"],    <- 1  module m(a); endmodule
                               ["sv_2017"],                   <- 2  module m(.*); endmodule   ⭐
                               ["sv_2017"],                   <- 3  extern module m(a);
                               ["sv_2017"]]                   <- 4  extern module m;
```

⇒ **the `@sample` defect population is `0`, not `1`**, and the honest-reject set `.13e.9` closed at
7 is now **8**. The leaf's routing evidence (*"the population is 0 today so a blocking guard is
free"*) is therefore RESTORED rather than broken — but it was restored by measurement, not by luck,
and the arithmetic it rested on was wrong for a day.

⛔⛔ **HALF TWO — `kw_macromodule_df04b866` IS A REACH-PLANNER DEFECT, NOT A SAMPLE DEFECT. THE
PROBE CLASS SETTLES IT IN ONE LINE.** TOOLBOX 4.3's reading is that `parsed=false` = malformed forced
sample (the `.13e.9` class) and `parsed=true witnessed_target=false` = a reach/routing gap. Measured
under `verilog_2005` at the contract's own parameters:

```
$ PGEN_CERT_COVERAGE_DEBUG_PROBES=1 ast_pipeline grammars/systemverilog.ebnf \
    --report-certificate-coverage --grammar-profile verilog_2005 --entry-rule systemverilog_file \
    --count 40 --seed 0 --cert-union-config …
  [plannable-probe] rule='kw_macromodule_df04b866' parsed=true witnessed_target=false
      sample="primitive\foo (output o, input i);table 0:0;endtable endprimitive"
```

`parsed=true` — so the probe input was never malformed, and no `@sample` text was the blocker. The
generator simply ended up somewhere else entirely (a UDP primitive, which contains no module
keyword at all). TOOLBOX 4.4 says to dump the PLAN before blaming the planner, because a probe
sample shows where generation *ended up* and the hop chain shows what it was *instructed to do*:

```
$ PGEN_REACH_PATH_DUMP=1 ast_pipeline … --grammar-profile verilog_2005 …
  [reach-path] target='kw_macromodule_df04b866' hops=[…, ("module_declaration", "root/o0"),
      ("module_declaration_sv_2017", "root/o2/s1"), ("module_keyword", "root/o1")]
```

⭐⭐ **`root/o2/s1` IS THE DEAD BRANCH.** The plan routes through alternative **2** — the one whose
mandatory `dot_star` the profile filter removed — so the renderer cannot execute it and generation
falls back silently. **`root/o2` is exactly the `branch_satisfiable_under` entry that reads
`["sv_2017"]` above**: the planner picked a branch its own grammar analysis can already prove dead.

⭐ **AND THE TARGET IS REACHABLE UNDER `verilog_2005` THE WHOLE TIME, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS A
DEFECT RATHER THAN A LIMIT.** Two sibling alternatives reach `module_keyword` through live routes,
and both accept — so a correct plan exists and the planner declined it:

| input | `verilog_2005` | `sv_2017` | route |
|---|---|---|---|
| `macromodule m; endmodule` | ✅ accept | ✅ accept | `root/o0` → `module_ansi_header` → `module_keyword` |
| `macromodule m(a,b); endmodule` | ✅ accept | ✅ accept | `root/o1` → `module_nonansi_header` → `module_keyword` |

**ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE), named in the source rather than inferred.**
`reach_hops_pass` (`rust/src/ast_pipeline/stimuli_generator.rs:9661`) validates a hop by asking only
whether the rule *referenced at that site* survives the profile filter:

```rust
for site in sites {
    if !self.grammar_tree.contains_key(site.referenced_rule.as_str()) { continue; }
```

It never asks whether the ALTERNATIVE CONTAINING that site is renderable. `module_keyword` is live,
so the edge is taken; `dot_star`, a MANDATORY SIBLING in the same sequence, is not, so the branch is
not. ⛔ **The engine already states the correct rule 500 lines below, and states it as a mirror of
this very function** — `mandatory_node_gated`'s doc-comment (`:10166`): *"A reference to a rule
MISSING from the active (profile-pruned) tree is treated as gated — it cannot be rendered, so it is
no escape (mirrors `reach_hops_pass` skipping that edge)."* That predicate is **Sequence-aware**
(gated iff ANY element is); `reach_hops_pass` is not. **The mirror is asymmetric, and the asymmetry
is the bug.** ⇒ routed as **`ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.51`**, which owns the repair. This leaf does
NOT fix it: the reach planner drives every profiled grammar's certificate numbers and the repair is
priced there, not smuggled in behind a `@sample` census.

## WHAT (a) BUILT: THE PREDICATE IS DERIVED IN THE ENGINE, NOT RE-MODELLED IN THE INSTRUMENT

`derive_branch_profiles` (`rust/src/ast_pipeline/grammar_wellformedness.rs`) — for each rule, one
profile set per TOP-LEVEL ALTERNATIVE, in body order. ⭐ **It reuses `compute_sat_by_profile` and
`node_satisfiable` — the exact fixpoint the profile-orphan lint already gates on** — so there is no
second model of the grammar to drift. Surfaced additively as `branch_satisfiable_under` +
`branch_count` on `--dump-rule-profiles` (no gate or script consumed that dump; census below).

⭐⭐ **THE CROSS-CHECK IS AN INVARIANT, NOT A CONVENTION, AND IT IS MEASURED OVER THE WHOLE GRAMMAR.**
`node_satisfiable` on an `Or` is exactly *"some alternative is satisfiable"*, so the UNION of a
rule's per-branch sets must equal its `satisfiable_under`. Over all **1 537** SV rules:
**0 violations.** A consumer can assert it; `derive_branch_profiles_unions_to_the_rule_level_set`
pins it; and it is what proves the new field is a REFINEMENT of the old one rather than a rival.

⚠️ **HONEST BOUND, stated before the field is trusted.** This is BOTTOM-UP satisfiability — *can this
branch derive a string under P* — and is NOT reachability, inheriting TOOLBOX 5.11's standing trap
verbatim (`kw_void` is satisfiable under `verilog_2005` and `function void f;` rejects). It is the
right predicate for a `@sample` join, because a sample is parsed AT its owning rule as the entry, so
the question genuinely is bottom-up. It would be the WRONG predicate for an entry-relative claim.

## THE CENSUS, AND THE COST OF THE JOIN — MEASURED, NOT ARGUED

`docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/sample_profile_parity/sample_profile_parity.py` (grammar-agnostic;
`--join` selects the join so the design decision is a measurement). The `@sample` population is read
from the NORMALIZED gen-AST, never by grepping the `.ebnf` — an annotation binds to the NEXT rule,
and a regex census over annotation text is the instrument `-0293` was burned by:

| join | checks | reported | TRUE defects | false positives |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ⛔ rule-level (the wrong one) | 115 | 8 | **0** | **8 — 100 % of its own reject set** |
| ⭐ branch-level (this leaf's) | **101** | **0** | **0** | **0** |

⭐⭐ **THE 8 ARE EXACTLY THE 7 `.13e.9` ADJUDICATED BY HAND, PLUS THE 1 `-0305` CREATED** —
`block_data_type` 3/4, `data_type` 3/4, `case_statement` 1, `module_declaration_sv_2017` 3/4, and
now `module_declaration_sv_2017` 2. That is leg 2 of the three-way check: a DERIVED predicate
falsified against an oracle this slice did not build — `.13e.9`'s parse-by-parse adjudication — and
they agree on **7 of 7**, with the derivation supplying the 8th the hand pass never saw.
⇒ **the leaf's predicted "7/11 false-positive rate" for the rule-level join was right in kind and
understated in degree: every single row it reports is a false positive.**

⛔ **THE POPULATION IS CLOSED ACROSS EVERY TRACKED GRAMMAR, because the guard is grammar-agnostic and
"it only matters for SV" is a census claim:**

| grammar | `@profiles` | `@sample` | checks | defects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `systemverilog` | 3 | 52 | 101 | **0** |
| `regex` | 1 | 1 | 1 | **0** |
| `systemverilog_preprocessor` | 0 | 2 | 0 | NOT EVALUATED (no profile universe) |
| `json`, `vhdl`, `ebnf`, `rtl_*`, the annotation pair, the LRM extractions | 0 | 0 | 0 | NOT EVALUATED |
| `systemverilog_lrm_profiled_generated` | 184 | 0 | — | REFUSES: an include fragment, no `@entry` |

⇒ the LIVE population is **two grammars**, and both are clean. ⭐ A grammar with no `@profiles`
reports **NOT EVALUATED, loudly — never a pass** (the `CORPUS-KEY-INTEGRITY` A1 shape: a reader that
treats what it cannot evaluate as *no findings* fails in the PASSING direction).

⭐ **AND THE `.13e.9` GREP TRAP REPRODUCED ON A SECOND GRAMMAR, which is why the gen-AST is the
source.** `systemverilog_preprocessor.ebnf` has **6** `grep -c '@sample:'` hits and exactly **2**
real annotations — four sit in prose comments. Same 54 → 52 shape SV showed, independently.

⛔ **THE INSTRUMENT REFUSES RATHER THAN GUESSES, on two axes that would each fail silently.**
(i) A rule whose branch-annotation vector no longer indexes its body is reported `unjoinable`, never
joined on a guessed index — left-recursion elimination rewrites a top-level `Or`, and the engine's
own `pre_lr_elim_branch_return_annotations` is the evidence it does. Measured on SV: **2** such rules
(`block_event_expression`, `select_expression`), **neither carrying a `@sample`**, so the join is
total today and guarded for when it is not. (ii) A check is scored only from the interpreter's own
`INTERPRET-PARSE:` verdict line — never from the exit code, because a LOAD failure and a PARSE
rejection are indistinguishable at `rc=1`, which is how `-0293`'s sweep read 160 phantom moves in
the flattering direction.

⛔ **A GREEN INSTRUMENT PROVES NOTHING UNTIL ITS REFUSALS FIRE.** `--self-test` runs a synthetic
pinning BOTH directions in one grammar — a branch honestly dead under the strict profile (which MUST
NOT be reported: the false-positive class) beside a genuinely broken sample on a live branch (which
MUST be reported, once per live profile). **`arms=2/2`, 2 defects observed, both on the intended
branch.**

###### `.13e.11` (b) SLICE 1 — **THE CENSUS MOVES INTO THE ENGINE: 101 processes become 1, 2 m 43 s become 33 s, and every number agrees with the Python oracle it replaces** (2026-08-26, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0308`; ENGINE/INSTRUMENT tier, additive CLI surface, ZERO grammar / codegen / generated bytes)

⛔ **WHY THIS SLICE EXISTS AT ALL — the cadence question decided the design, and it was MEASURED
before it was decided.** (b) owes *"wire the check as a gate arm with a RED control proven firing"*.
Wiring the `(a)` driver as-is would have put **2 m 43 s** into a pre-commit hook that currently runs
in seconds, and a three-minute hook is a hook that gets bypassed — the exact failure
`DOCTRINE-GAP-OWNERSHIP.15` names. So the first question was not *"which gate"* but *"why does one
check cost 1.6 s"*, and the answer is that **it is nearly all grammar load**: a single
`--interpret-parse` on `systemverilog` is 1.46 s and the whole `--lint-grammar` pass is 4.8 s, so
101 separate processes pay 101 grammar loads to do 101 parses.

⭐ **AND THERE WAS A SECOND REASON, WHICH IS (a)'s OWN PRINCIPLE.** (a) shipped
`derive_branch_profiles` *in the engine* precisely so *"there is no second model of the grammar to
drift"* — and then the driver re-implemented the sample/branch join in Python against two JSON
dumps. That is the second model, one layer up. Moving the census into the engine retires it.

**WHAT SHIPPED** — `--report-sample-parity` (`rust/src/main.rs`), with
`--sample-parity-json <FILE>` and the contrast mode `--sample-parity-rule-join`. It runs on the
UNFILTERED bundle for the same reason `--interpret-parse` does (profile selection is a RUNTIME guard
the interpreter applies itself), and calls the same `interpret_parse_gen_ast` entry point — so each
check is byte-for-byte the check a separate `--interpret-parse --interpret-entry-rule R
--grammar-profile P` invocation makes. Two new pure functions sit beside `derive_branch_profiles` in
`grammar_wellformedness.rs`: `collect_profile_samples` (the population, refusing a mis-indexed branch
vector rather than guessing an index) and `profiles_requiring_sample` (the join).

⭐⭐ **THE EQUIVALENCE IS MEASURED AGAINST AN ORACLE THIS SLICE DID NOT BUILD — leg 2 of the
three-way check — AND IT AGREES ON EVERY NUMBER, IN BOTH JOINS:**

| arm | Python driver (`(a)`) | engine (`(b)` slice 1) |
|---|---|---|
| `systemverilog`, branch join | `profiles=3 samples=52 checks=101 defects=0 unjoinable=0` | ⭐ **identical** |
| `systemverilog`, RULE join (the wrong one) | `checks=115 defects=8` | ⭐ **identical** |
| `regex` | `checks=1 defects=0` | ⭐ **identical** |
| `json` (no `@profiles`) | NOT EVALUATED | ⭐ **identical** |
| `systemverilog_preprocessor` | NOT EVALUATED, `samples=2` (6 grep hits, 4 in prose) | ⭐ **identical** |

⇒ agreement on a **rule-join contrast that reports 8 defects** matters as much as agreement on the
clean run: a port that only reproduced the green number could be green for the wrong reason.

⛔ **THE RED CONTROL IS PROVEN AT THE CLI, WITH A GREEN CONTROL ON THE SAME PATH SO IT IS NOT AN
ARTEFACT OF THE COPY.** One `@sample` on a branch live under all three profiles
(`assignment_pattern` branch 0, `'{0, 1}`) was corrupted to `'{0, 1` in a COPY of the grammar:

```
$ ast_pipeline tmp/…/sv_red.ebnf --report-sample-parity ; echo rc=$?
  SAMPLE-PROFILE-PARITY: DEFECT — rule='assignment_pattern' branch=0 profile='sv_2017'      … furthest_position=6
  SAMPLE-PROFILE-PARITY: DEFECT — rule='assignment_pattern' branch=0 profile='sv_2023'      … furthest_position=6
  SAMPLE-PROFILE-PARITY: DEFECT — rule='assignment_pattern' branch=0 profile='verilog_2005' … furthest_position=6
  SAMPLE-PROFILE-PARITY: grammar='sv_red' … defects=3 unjoinable=0
  rc=1
$ ast_pipeline tmp/…/sv_green.ebnf --report-sample-parity ; echo rc=$?   # an UNCORRUPTED copy
  SAMPLE-PROFILE-PARITY: grammar='sv_green' … checks=101 defects=0 unjoinable=0
  rc=0
```

⭐ **One broken sample produces THREE defects — one per profile its branch is live in** — which is
the census reporting per-check rather than per-sample, and is what makes a partial breakage
(a sample that parses under `sv_2017` and not `verilog_2005`) visible as such.

⛔ **A GRAMMAR WITH NO PROFILE UNIVERSE REPORTS `NOT EVALUATED`, LOUDLY — NEVER A PASS.** The
`CORPUS-KEY-INTEGRITY` A1 shape: a reader that treats what it cannot evaluate as *no findings* fails
in the PASSING direction. `systemverilog_preprocessor` is the live example — **2** real `@sample`
annotations and **0** profiles, so there is nothing to check and the tool says so with the sample
count attached rather than printing a clean line.

**STILL OWED, and the leaf stays `in progress`:** (b) slice 2 = the gate arm itself, and (c) = the
SV-arm-vs-registered-doctrine ruling. ⭐ Slice 1 changes what slice 2 can afford: at 33 s the census
is cheap enough to be **staged-scope-aware and run the real check** — inert when no staged file is a
grammar declaring `@profiles`, full census when one is — instead of needing a tracked baseline plus
an identity block as a currency PROXY for a check too slow to run. ⛔ That is the difference between
gating the truth and gating *"was it re-run"*, and `.53` had just re-learned what a proxy costs.

###### `.13e.11` (b) SLICE 2 + (c) — **THE 28th REGISTERED DOCTRINE, AND THE CLOSED-POPULATION SWEEP CAUGHT A FALSE-POSITIVE BLOCKER IN THE GATE'S OWN FIRST CUT** (2026-08-26, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0309`; OPS/ENFORCER tier, ZERO grammar / codegen / generated bytes)

**(c) THE RULING: A REGISTERED DOCTRINE, NOT AN SV GATE ARM.** The leaf already reasoned that the
check is grammar-agnostic and therefore *"the second is the honest home"*; slice 2 confirms it by
measurement rather than by repeating the argument. The `--all` sweep classifies the **closed**
population of all **18** tracked `grammars/**.ebnf` — 3 censused, 15 NOT EVALUATED — and the defect
class is created by ANY grammar declaring a dialect, not by SystemVerilog. An SV-only arm would have
left `regex` (which already has a profile and a sample) unguarded and would need re-inventing the
first time a second family gets a dialect. `SAMPLE-PROFILE-PARITY` is registry entry **28**.

**(b) THE GATE — `scripts/check_sample_profile_parity.sh`, ORACLE archetype.** It RE-EXECUTES the
census, so it gates whether the samples PARSE — never whether the census was re-run. ⛔ The
alternative was considered and refused **in writing**: a tracked baseline plus an identity block,
tier 1 hashing inputs and tier 2 on demand, gates *"was it re-run since the grammar moved"* — a
currency PROXY, and `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.53` had measured in the same week what a proxy costs
when the question moves out from under it. Slice 1's 4.9× is what made the proxy unnecessary.

**STAGED-DIFF-SCOPED, and the cadence is measured on both sides:**

| situation | cost |
|---|---|
| no `grammars/**.ebnf` staged (the common case) | **0.026 s** — inert |
| a grammar staged | one census: **33 s** for `systemverilog`, ~2 s for `regex` |
| `--all`, the closed population | **41.8 s** for 18 grammars |

⭐ The generator is proven CURRENT rather than merely present — `cargo build --features
"generated_parsers ebnf_dual_run" --bin ast_pipeline`, the `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.32` pattern
(~0.8 s when current, a rebuild when not, which is exactly when you want one). A tree that cannot
build the analyser is reported **NOT EVALUATED, loudly, and is not blocked**: that is a BUILD
finding, larger than this gate measures.

⛔⛔ **AND THE CLOSED-POPULATION SWEEP CAUGHT A DEFECT IN THIS GATE'S OWN FIRST CUT — one that would
have BLOCKED A LEGITIMATE COMMIT ON 4 OF 18 GRAMMARS.** The first cut treated *"no
`SAMPLE-PROFILE-PARITY:` headline"* as a single refusal that fails. Running `--all` over the whole
population instead of over the two grammars I already knew about produced:

```
SAMPLE-PROFILE-PARITY: REFUSING to score 'grammars/verilog_2005_lrm_extracted.ebnf' …
SAMPLE-PROFILE-PARITY: REFUSING to score 'grammars/systemverilog_2017_lrm_extracted.ebnf' …
SAMPLE-PROFILE-PARITY: REFUSING to score 'grammars/systemverilog_2023_lrm_extracted.ebnf' …
SAMPLE-PROFILE-PARITY: REFUSING to score 'grammars/systemverilog_lrm_profiled_generated.ebnf' …
```

Reading the logs rather than the count names the cause: three carry raw LRM text the loader rejects
(`Error: unterminated regex literal in expression '+ | - | * | / …'`) and the fourth is an include
fragment with **no `@entry`**. ⭐ **The two nonzero causes need OPPOSITE dispositions**: a grammar
whose samples do not parse is a DEFECT; a grammar that cannot be LOADED is an extraction finding this
doctrine does not measure, and converting one into the other is the `-0293` failure in the *blocking*
direction. The headline separates them — it is printed only after the grammar loaded — so the check
now returns **NOT EVALUATED** for a load failure and reserves the block for a **clean exit with no
verdict line**, which is the one case that reads to any consumer as *"checked everything, found
nothing"*. ⇒ **the population sweep earned its place by refuting the gate that ran it.**

⛔ **AND THE PASS LINE NO LONGER OVERCLAIMS.** With every target NOT EVALUATED the old wording —
*"every staged grammar's `@sample` set parses"* — is true and useless, and reads as coverage that did
not happen. It now says which: `OK — 3 grammar(s) censused … (15 NOT EVALUATED)`.

**5/5 REFUSAL ARMS OBSERVED FIRING (`--self-test`)**, including a GREEN control so the RED arms are
not red for the copy:

| arm | what it proves |
|---|---|
| 1 | a clean copy PASSES — without it, arms 2-5 could be red for the copy rather than the edit |
| 2 | a broken sample on a LIVE branch is REPORTED with a nonzero exit |
| 3 | a grammar with no `@profiles` is NOT EVALUATED, never a pass |
| 4 | a grammar that does not LOAD is NOT EVALUATED — never scored clean, **never a block** |
| 5 | a SILENT clean exit (a stub binary printing nothing) is REFUSED and BLOCKS |

⭐⭐ **THE RED CONTROL IS PROVEN THROUGH THE DRIVER, NOT ONLY THROUGH THE ENFORCER** — the
`CORPUS-KEY-INTEGRITY` standard. `grammars/regex.ebnf`'s own `@sample: "é"` was corrupted to
`"é["`, STAGED, and `bash scripts/check_doctrines.sh` run:

```
SAMPLE-PROFILE-PARITY: DEFECT — rule='unicode_char' branch=rule-level profile='relaxed' sample="é[" furthest_position=0
  ✗ FAIL  SAMPLE-PROFILE-PARITY — …
doctrines: ✗ one or more doctrines FAILED — commit/merge blocked. Fix above, do not bypass.     (rc 1)
```

and after restoring the grammar, `ALL 28 enforced doctrines PASS`. ⇒ the block is observed at the
level that actually stops a commit.

⛔ **THE REGISTRY DESCRIPTION CARRIES NO BACKTICKS, DELIBERATELY.** `DOCTRINE-GAP-OWNERSHIP.16` is
open precisely because `check_doctrines.sh:76` has four UNESCAPED backticks inside a double-quoted
bash string, so the driver EXECUTES them and the published description silently loses those words —
`bash -n` clean, driver exit 0. Rather than escape and hope, this entry avoids the character
entirely. ⚠️ That does not close `.16`, which owns the four live sites and the guard.

**⛔ THE FOUNDING TABLE HOLDS, AND THE NARROWER READING IS THE SHARPER FINDING.** `.13j`(e) opened
this leaf on a walk over `.sv`/`.svh`/`.v`. The reading most favourable to the filesystem source is

|---|---|---|---|
| `ispras-sv-tests` | 356 | **360** | 1 266 |
| `iverilog` | 1 909 | **3 799** | 3 799 |
| `sv2v` | 341 | **341** | 953 |

⇒ **2 of 3 suites breach on the narrow reading and 3 of 3 on the wide one.** ⭐⭐ And the row that
agrees is the one worth reading: on `sv2v` the two populations are **set-identical**, not merely
equal in count (`diff` of the sorted lane paths against the sorted `find` output = 0 lines over 341
