coincidence as confirmation**, which is the same shape as `.13j`(c)'s symlink arm being green "by
accident of what those corpora happen to contain".

**⛔ `lane_list` IS A RE-DERIVATION, NEVER A SKIP** — `.13m`(b)'s own condition, and the reason is
stated in the gate: an arm that opts out is `GATE-REACHABILITY` wearing a census. Four legs: the
per-suite count is held equal to the row that publishes it; the comparison is **two-sided** (a suite
in the list and not the report is a breach, and so is the reverse); the total is held equal to the
totals row; and every listed path must be a **regular file** — `stat.S_ISREG(os.lstat(...))`, the
same definition `count_sources` uses, because the producer reads that list verbatim and a row naming
a file that is gone is a denominator it can no longer reproduce. An unimplemented source **REFUSES**
rather than falling through to the walk, and a declared list that is **absent** is a BREACH.

**⭐ THE HEADER ROW IS SKIPPED BY POSITION, THE WAY THE PRODUCER SKIPS IT.**
`stimuli/run_external_corpus.sh:405` is `tail -n +2`. A reader that dropped rows whose first field
reads `suite` would also drop a real suite called `suite`; a reader that dropped none would count
the header as a file. The self-test pins it with a list whose every row names suite `suite` and
requires 100, not 99.

**THE BANK — `docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/v2005_lane_denominator/probe.sh`, 9 arms, ~2 s,
`V2005-LANE-DENOMINATOR: 9/9 as declared`.** Every arm drives the real gate through its
`PGEN_FAMILY_STATUS_SCHEMA` seam against **copies** of the lane list under `rust/target/`, so **no
tracked file is mutated at any point** — the `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.87` rule that a deliberate
mutation must never outlive the tool call that applied it, satisfied by never applying one.

|---|---|---|

| 1 | the shipped declaration on the tracked tree | GREEN, tuple `2606/2300/306/0/0` |

⛔⛔ **AND THE GATE COULD NOT HAVE RUN GREEN ON SYSTEMVERILOG WITHOUT TWO CORRECTIONS. Driven
before anything was edited, it returned `rc 1` with two breaches and one NOT EVALUATED:**

```
✗ friscv    publishes  441 files but stimuli/sv/subs/friscv    holds  446 …
```

- ⛔ **DEFECT 1 — ARM (4) RE-IMPLEMENTED THE PRODUCER'S POPULATION AND GOT IT WRONG.** The producer

  The gap is **37 rows**, and two independent oracles agree on every one: `find -type l` on the

**(c) — THE RULING, and it did not need a new judgement: the tree had already made it.**
`adjudicate_external_corpus.py`'s own taxonomy defines `must_reject` as *"the text has no derivation
in the LRM's grammar (Annex A / the clause-5 lexical rules). Covers BOTH the suite's own intentional
invalidity AND **text a vendor tolerates that the standard cannot derive** — the pin tables below
carry ~30 of the latter, **where the spec outranks the upstream tool**."* That is these rows exactly.
`divergence:explained_*` is NOT the answer: its whole vocabulary is svpp and timeout CAUSES
(`_include`, `_macro_use`, `_conditional`, `_protected_envelope`, `_timeout`), and nothing about
preprocessing or a deadline explains a token the edition does not have. ⭐ `.13k`'s own worry —
*"a GOLDEN file that is genuinely not 1364-2005 is a CORPUS COMPOSITION fact, not a parser verdict"*
— is answered by the same sentence: the composition fact is recorded IN the pin's basis, and
`must_reject` is what turns a correct reject from a defect-column row into a claim WITH A CITE.
⇒ [[feedback_answer_your_own_technical_questions]]: the tree had decided this, in the file being
edited, ~30 rows earlier.

**(a) — THE BASIS, RE-DERIVED IN-REPO FOUR WAYS AND NEVER FROM WHAT PGEN DOES:**

1. **IEEE 1364-2005 Annex A has NO compound assignment operator at all.** `grep -cE '(\+=|-=|\*=|/=|%=|&=|\|=|\^=|<<=|>>=)'` = **0** over `docs/verilog/2005/txt/section-Annex_A-…txt`
   (48 062 B), over `docs/verilog/2005/grammar_clean.ebnf` and over
   `grammars/verilog_2005_lrm_extracted.ebnf` — three extracts, three zeros. The only assignment
   forms are `blocking_assignment ::= variable_lvalue = [ delay_or_event_control ] expression`
   (`:518`) and `variable_assignment ::= variable_lvalue = expression` (`:527`); the for-STEP **is**
   a `variable_assignment` (`loop_statement`, `:617-622`), so `i -= 1` in a header falls to the same
   clause as `i |= 1` in a body.
2. **The PROSE agrees**: 0 hits across all 37 `docs/verilog/2005/md` sections. ⭐ The only `+=` /
   `-=` bytes in the entire standard are the clause-14 specify-path POLARITY operators `+=>` / `-=>`
   (`section-14-specify-blocks.md:638`, `:652`) — a different token in a different role, and the
   residual reconciles EXACTLY.
3. **IEEE 1800 DOES define them, which is what makes this an EDITION contrast rather than a gap**:
   `operator_assignment ::= variable_lvalue assignment_operator expression` and `assignment_operator
   ::= = | += | -= | *= | /= | %= | &= | |= | ^= | <<= | >>= | <<<= | >>>=` — 1800-2017 §10.4.1
   (`docs/systemverilog/2017/txt/section-10-assignment-statements.txt:288-290`) and §11.4.1
   (`section-11-operators-and-expressions.txt:100-102`, tagged *"from A.6.2"*); 1800-2023 in

⛔ **ROUTED 2026-09-06 by `.3.43` (`PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0371`): the wrapper `scripts/check_lrm_clause_citation.sh` is SILENT on the verdict it exists to explain.** `out="$(python3 "$CENSUS" 2>&1)"; rc=$?` runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so a `disagree > 0` exit aborts the script before `printf '%s\n' "$out"` — the doctrine runner prints *✗ FAIL LRM-CLAUSE-CITATION* with the doctrine's description and none of the rows, and the author must run `stimuli/sv/lrm_clause_citation_census.py` by hand to learn which citation is wrong (measured: `bash scripts/check_lrm_clause_citation.sh` → rc 1, zero bytes on stdout and stderr, while the census printed `disagree=2` with both rows). Not worked here: the SV lane lock; it does not block (the census is runnable directly).

⛔ **THE QUESTION `.13q` LEFT OPEN WAS THE RIGHT ONE TO REFUSE TO ANSWER CHEAPLY.** `-0325` shipped
the census with a `REVIEWED_NOT_A_DEFECT` table of seven hand-written exceptions keyed by
`(citing file, clause, LRM file, LRM line)` — a key whose LAST COMPONENT MOVES whenever the LRM
corpus is re-extracted, in a repository that has re-extracted it before. **A gate whose green
depends on a hand-maintained exception list is not a gate, it is a promise.** So the registration
question was answered by first asking whether the list was necessary at all. It was not.

**BOTH SHAPES ARE STRUCTURAL, and the rules are decidable rather than heuristic:**

1. ⭐ **BRACKET SCOPE** kills the *defined-here / absent-there* shape (5 of 7 rows). In
   *"`interface_class_declaration` is defined (§8.26.1 / A.1.2) but NOT referenced as an alternative
   in `class_item` (`section-8-classes.md:95`)"* the clause and the line are DELIBERATELY different
   places — and the signal is not semantic: **the clause's own bracket group CLOSES before the ref's
   group opens.** A relative depth going negative between them is that departure (`in_clause_scope`).
2. ⭐⭐ **ADDRESSABILITY** kills the PDF-split shape (2 of 7) — and it turned out to be
   **load-bearing for correctness, not merely for exemptions.** ⛔⛔ **THE FORM SHIPPED HERE WAS
   WRONG AND ITS NUMBER IS WITHDRAWN BY `.13u` — read that leaf before quoting anything below.**
   It tested a FILE against its own FILENAME via the modal heading major; the correct question is
   per-(file, CITED CLAUSE), and *"17 of 124"* counts correctly-named SPANNING files as defects. A section file's NAME is a claim
   about which clause it holds; the census resolves a file FROM a clause number for the
   clause-adjacent forms, so a false name MANUFACTURES a disagreement. **MEASURED: the claim is
   false for 17 of 124 vendored section files** — 14 of 55 in 1800-2017, 3 of 41 in 1800-2023, 0 of
   28 in 1364-2005. The test is the file's **modal heading major** versus its filename —
   parameter-free on purpose, and the separation is not close: `section-0-…` scores **1 of 39**,
   `section-28-…` scores **34 of 40**. Routed to **`.13t`** as a corpus-integrity defect.

⭐ **AND A THIRD RULE THE QUESTION DID NOT ASK FOR, found by building the first two.** A heading
whose major disagrees with its file's own modal major is **PDF-split noise** and must be skipped
when resolving the enclosing clause: `docs/verilog/2005/md/section-7-…md` carries four stray
`## 2 delays` / `## 3 delays` headings which are **fragments of §7.14's own delay-cardinality
prose** — the very sentence this whole thread began with — and reading one as the enclosing clause
reports every citation past it as wrong. Line `2328` resolves to clause `3` unfiltered and **§7.14**
filtered.

⇒ [[an-x-is-checked-by-nothing-claim-is-a-census-claim]] again, and specifically the **SET**
failure: *when you publish N findings, verify the GROUPING — that N is the whole population and the
shared cause holds member by member.* I checked `section-0` and `section-28`, saw a clean

**THE INSTRUMENT FIX — both questions are per-(file, CITED CLAUSE), never per-file:**

1. **`addressable_for(path, major)`** — does this file carry ANY heading of that clause's major?
   That is what *"can a citation of clause X be checked here"* actually means. It needs no filename
   claim and no threshold.
2. **`enclosing(path, line, major)`** now filters by the **cited** major, not the file's modal
   major. ⛔ The modal form was **latently wrong** for a spanning file: in `section-15-…md` (modal
   16) it would have skipped all **26** clause-15 headings and judged a §15.x citation against 16.x.
   It was masked only because the file-level test bucketed that file out first — **a mask, not a
   defence.**
3. ⛔ **`section_mismatch` IS DELETED — the filename's number is now read NOWHERE.** It was the same
   filename-trusting mistake in a third guise, and it fired on **two CORRECT citations**: §11.4.12
   into `section-0-…md`, a file carrying **35 of its 39** headings in clause 11.

§5.14). For every `§X.Y` in a tracked file it binds the LRM line references it can bind
STRUCTURALLY — an explicit `section-….md:N` path, a `§X.Y:N` glued form, or a `` `:N` `` continuing
one of those inside a bounded span — resolves the edition (an explicit path's directory outranks
prose), and reports whether the innermost heading enclosing that line is the cited clause or a

including this leaf's own known-bad `§28.16 → :396`) and a miss exits **7** rather than reporting a
clean tree.

⛔ **THE FIRST CUT OF THAT INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG IN THE LOUD DIRECTION AND ITS OUTPUT WAS NEVER
PUBLISHED.** Resolving the file from the clause's own major number and sweeping every `:N` between
one `§` and the next reported **160** disagreements; read row by row, most were the tool attributing
a `furthest_position=`, a source-line reference or a neighbouring citation's line to the wrong
clause — a ledger row is one physical line thousands of characters long, so *"the next `§`"* is not
a boundary. **160 was never a defect count**, and the shape of that error is exactly the one this
leaf is about: a number lifted out of a frame nobody measured. ⚠️ **It is RECORDED, NOT REPLAYABLE**
— the first cut was never committed, so 160 is an observation this session made and cannot
re-derive; it appears only beside its own refutation, never as a finding (`-0132`'s discipline: say
so rather than let a number imply a replay). Tightening to structural binding
gives **31** judged rows, and reading all 31 gives **24 REAL** (every one this leaf's delay class,
zero elsewhere in the repo) and **7 FALSE POSITIVES OF TWO NAMED SHAPES**, carried in the tool's
`REVIEWED_NOT_A_DEFECT` table with their reasons rather than suppressed by path:

- **the *defined-here / absent-there* shape** (5 rows) — *"`interface_class_declaration` is defined
  (§8.26.1 / A.1.2) but NOT referenced in `class_item` (`section-8-classes.md:95`)"*. Correct prose;
  the clause and the line are deliberately different places, so the enclosure premise does not hold.
- **the PDF-split artifact** (2 rows) — the §11.4.12 notation sentence lives in
  `section-0-defined-as-false-…md:520`, a file whose name carries no clause number because the
  PDF→md split mis-titled it. The citation is right; the corpus filename is what cannot be checked.

⇒ **the enclosure premise is a property of a citation SHAPE, not of citations** — the instrument is
a lead generator whose rows are READ, and it is honest only because both shapes are named.

⭐⭐ **AND THE INSTRUMENT IMMEDIATELY AUDITED MY OWN CORRECTION, WHICH IS THE POINT OF BUILDING IT
BEFORE FIXING RATHER THAN AFTER.** Splitting one clause into two (`§28.4 (`:396`) / §28.5 (`:454`)`)
left the SECOND half unbindable, because the first cut bound only `§X.Y:N` and an explicit path —
not this repo's dominant shape, ``§X.Y (`:N`)``. Judged rows had quietly fallen **35 → 17** while
`no_line_ref` rose by 27: **the fix was making the tree less checkable and the census was reporting
it as clean.** Binding the clause-adjacent form took judged rows to **35** and promptly failed
**three rows of my own newly written text** — a `§28.6` whose nearest edition token was
`1364-2005` (so it resolved to `section-28-protected-envelopes.md`, a real 1364 clause 28 that is
not the one meant), and two bare `` `:N` `` refs chaining to the wrong neighbour, one of them an
Annex A line attributed to §7.4. All three are now spelled with their edition and their file.
⇒ **a correction is a claim like any other, and the reach of the instrument that checks it is part
of the claim** — a census that gets cleaner because it stopped looking is the failure mode that
looks most like success.

  1. **BY DESIGN** — a standalone parse of a design file is not testimony about the design, so a
     deferred row's improvement genuinely should not move a confidence bar. Then the obligation is to
     say so where the bar is published, because a bar that silently UNDER-reports progress is
     misleading in the direction that looks like slow progress.
  2. **A DEFECT** — the bar should distinguish *"no verdict, and the file does not even parse"* from
     *"no verdict, but it now parses standalone"*, because those are different states and collapsing
     them discards measured information.
⭐ Whichever is chosen, `.13`'s stratification already has the shape to carry it: this is a bucket
split, not a new instrument. ⛔ And it must be decided from the DENOMINATOR's point of view rather
than from this slice's — the question is not "did my fix get credit", it is "does the bar report what
it claims to report".

1. **A bar counts DIVERGENCES, and a divergence needs an EXPECTATION.** A `deferred:chained_only`

   number report progress from an event that is not evidence, which is `.13`'s own

the deciding evidence is usually already on disk.*

### `.3.30` → `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.91` — the lint accepts case-colliding rule names; the generator emits one constant twice

1. **Does it reproduce OUTSIDE the family it is routed to? — by construction, yes, and the mechanism was read
   in the emitted artifact, not inferred:** `generated/systemverilog_parser.rs:654-665` (first cut of `.3.30`)
   carries `const RULE_UDP_SYM_X: RuleId = 549u16;` and `… = 550u16;` back to back, for `udp_sym_x` and
   `udp_sym_X`; the constant is the uppercased rule name, and nothing about that is SystemVerilog. The grammar's
   hash-suffixed keyword pairs (`kw_x_11f6ad8e` / `kw_X_c032adc1`) are the standing workaround, present since
   the extractor first met case-differing keywords. ⚠️ Honest bound: a synthetic two-rule grammar was NOT
   compiled for this routing; `.91`'s own RED control is where that is done.
2. **What was MEASURED to place it there?** `--lint-grammar` rc **0** on the colliding grammar (`1561 rules …
   unreachable_rules=0`), the interpreter accepting every pin (the interpreter keys rules by name, not by
   constant), and `cargo build --features "generated_parsers ebnf_dual_run" --bin ast_pipeline` rc **101** with
   six `E0592` errors — one per case pair. Renaming the six upper-case twins `udp_sym_<c>_upper` (no other
   change) removed all six; that is the two-sided attribution.

### `.3.39` → `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.98` — the stimuli generator's lexical-boundary tracking fuses a backtick-led token to the next word, and the `/` separator to a following `//` comment

1. **Does it reproduce OUTSIDE the family it is routed to? — yes, measured on a three-rule scratch grammar
   with no SystemVerilog in it:** `rust/target/s339/scratch/fuse.ebnf` (`s := t w`, `t := /`abc\b/`,
   `w := /def\b/`) through `ast_pipeline --generate-stimuli --count 3 --seed 0` renders `` `abcdef `` three
   times; the identical grammar with `t := /abc\b/` renders `abc def`. The class is the token's FIRST
   character — punctuation-led tokens get no boundary on their right — and every grammar whose tokens begin
   with punctuation and end in `\b` (VHDL's `'attribute`, the annotation grammars' `@name`, `$` system names)
   is in it; the `.98` leaf carries the census command. The sibling class (the literal `/` before a `//`
   comment sample, `100 fs ///x`) was measured on the SV certificate's own seed-0 and seed-42 sample-parse
   failures and its mechanism read from the same renderer; ⚠️ honest bound: its scratch reproducer was NOT
   run for this routing — `.98`'s RED control is where that is done.
2. **What was MEASURED to place it there?** Protocol A on the 1.0.217 candidate: `[plannable-probe]
   rule='in_scope_compiler_directive' parsed=false witnessed_target=false sample="module m(input wire
   a);`celldefineendmodule"`, `rule='pragma_expression' parsed=true witnessed_target=false sample="`pragmawj
   dm"` (the fused name fails the typed arm and falls into the opaque residue), and under `verilog_2005`

### `.3.35` → `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.93` — the generated layout skipper accepts an unterminated block comment

### `.3.31` → `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.92` — a caller split loses the twin's memo replays; the memo is keyed by rule, not by what the rule derives

   `(rule id, position)`; `hierarchical_bit_select` and `constant_bit_select` are two rule ids whose
   bodies derive the same text on every iteration a constant index can take, and nothing in the memo
   relates them. That is a property of every grammar that splits a rule to widen one caller.

### `.3.29` → `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.89` — the existence predicates are store-wide

   whose own doc comment says *"across the whole store … in any scope_depth"* — no grammar name, no
   profile, no SystemVerilog rule in the path. MEASURED on a six-rule synthetic with no SystemVerilog in
   it, banked as `docs/tasks/artifacts/engine_universal_services/eus89_store_wide_has_fact/probe.sh`:
   `{x}T` (fact emitted into a `region` scope that then closed, then gated) → `accepted=true`; the RED
   control (same gate, no region) → `accepted=false`; `eus89 probe: 2/2 as declared (fail=0)`.
   The regex grammar not only reproduces it, it RELIES on it
   (`grammars/regex.ebnf:572`, a `phase: final` `has_fact` over groups defined inside closed lookaround
   scopes), which is why the routed leaf prices an opt-in query rather than a change to `has_fact`.
2. **What was MEASURED to place it there?** The interpreter trace on the SV pin — `🔓 @open_scope`,
   two `📥 @emit_fact … scope_id=ScopeId(1)`, `🔒 @close_scope OK`, then `🔍 has_fact(… CrossQueueType) → true`
   from `ScopeId(0)` — read against the source of `any_with_name` and of the depth-keyed
   `any_with_name_at_scope`. The scope machinery (open, emit-into, close, rollback) behaved exactly as
   the book describes; only the existence query is scope-blind. `.3.29` therefore shipped CONTAINMENT
   (`in_scope_kind(cross)`, the regex `not_in_scope_kind(lookaround)` idiom) and left the engine gap owned.

### `.12c.1` → `EBNF-FRONTEND-SILENT-TRUNCATION.5` — the four GRAMMAR readers

1. **Does it reproduce OUTSIDE the family it is routed to? — the honest answer is NOT TODAY, and
   that is measured, not assumed.** Censused every `.ebnf` under `grammars/`, `docs/` and
   `rust/test_data/`: **42 files scanned, 0 non-UTF-8**. So the defect is real in the code
   (`ebnf_frontend.rs:16`, `:563`, `ebnf_dual_run_diff.rs:288`, `parser_registry.rs:3805` all call
   `read_to_string`) but has **no in-repo instance** — it is a user-facing limitation on
   third-party grammars, not a live failure. ⛔ Stating that plainly is the point: routing it as if
   it were breaking something today would misprice it, and routing it *without* the census would
   have been a guess in either direction.
2. **What was MEASURED to place it there, not what makes it plausible?** The categorised census of
   all 46 text readers in `rust/src/`
   (`docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/source_text_readers/enumeration.md`). It is the census —
   not the fix — that separates grammar text (4 sites) from user source (7) and from PGEN's own
   artifacts (35), and the separation is what makes this a *different* leaf rather than four more
   lines in `.12c.1`.
3. **Why not just fix it here, since the decoder already exists?** Two reasons, both structural:
   the standing **SV lane lock** binds work to the SV release, and a grammar file has a different
   risk profile from user source — the grammars in this repo are PGEN-owned artifacts, so
   encoding tolerance there sits closer to category C than to category A. That judgement deserves
   its own leaf, not a footnote in this one.
4. ⚠️ **Naming honesty, recorded on both sides.** The receiving tree is titled *silent* truncation
   and this defect is **loud**. It is filed there because that tree is the repo's home for EBNF
   frontend input-handling integrity, and the sibling relationship is real (*the frontend not
   reading what the file says*) — but the mismatch is written into the receiving leaf rather than
   glossed over.

### `.11c` — the memo is part of the acceptance semantics on cyclic rules

1. **Does it reproduce OUTSIDE the family it is routed to? — YES, MEASURED, and that is precisely
   why it is routed to the ENGINE rather than to any grammar family.** Three independent
   measurements, none of them SystemVerilog:
   - the isolating case `recursion_guarded_memo_isolation` reproduces the whole mechanism on a
     **6-rule SYNTHETIC grammar** with no SV in it, through the compile-and-run oracle AND the
     interpreter (`parse_harness_combinator_gate`, 28/28);
   - the code changed is `ast_based_generator.rs` + `ast_based_generator/cascade.rs` +
     `RecursionGuard` in `mod.rs` — **shared codegen and shared runtime**, compiled into every
     generated parser, so no grammar can opt out;
   - the **VHDL** corpus was re-run for exactly this reason (13 720 files, **0 transitions**), and
     the equivalence gate re-certified **all 11** grammars, confirming the behaviour is uniform
     rather than SV-shaped.
2. **What was MEASURED to place it there, not what makes it plausible?** That refusing to replay a
   recursion-tainted SUCCESS costs **4 corpus files pass→fail** — i.e. the replay is load-bearing for
   acceptance, not merely a cache hit. That is an observation about the ENGINE's acceptance
   semantics on cyclic rules; it was obtained by A/B-ing two engine builds over the same 16 336-file
   corpus, not inferred from the SV grammar.
3. **What would have to be true for the routing to be WRONG, and was it checked?** It would be wrong
   if the behaviour were an artifact of `systemverilog.ebnf`'s particular cycle (`cast → casting_type
   → constant_primary → constant_function_call → call_primary`) rather than of the engine. Checked
   and refuted: the synthetic grammar has none of those rules and exhibits the identical
   order-dependence, and the interpreter — a second implementation with **no cycle guard at all**,
   only a depth ceiling — shows the same class through its own mechanism. ⚠️ **Honest limit:** the
   *quantitative* claim ("how much acceptance depends on evaluation order") is measured only on SV
   and on the synthetic case. No other family's cyclic surface has been swept for order-dependent
   acceptance, and `.11c` should start by doing that rather than by assuming SV is representative.

### `.11d` — the memo taint test is a global over-approximation

1. **Does it reproduce OUTSIDE the family it is routed to? — the MECHANISM yes, by construction;
   the PATHOLOGY not yet, and the negative result is recorded rather than smoothed over.** The taint
   snapshot/compare/stamp and the epoch-eviction are emitted from the **shared codegen**
   `memoized_call` template, so they are compiled identically into all ten generated parsers — no
   grammar can opt out. But the pathology needs BOTH legs, and only SV currently has them.
   Measured, same instrument, one parse each:

   | grammar | `predicate_evaluations` | `facts_emitted` / `rolled_back` | stale-tainted evictions |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `systemverilog` (`.11a` chain, n=6) | **1467** | 1128 / 1119 | **1860** |
   | `regex` (named groups + backref + bounded quants) | **3** | 5 / 0 | **0** |

   ⇒ regex is CLEAN, and that is informative rather than disappointing: it shows the degradation is
   not "predicates are present" but "predicates are evaluated **and** the store is written between
   an insert and its next lookup". `regex` is the ONLY other grammar in the repo declaring
   `@predicate` (18; vhdl/json/rtl_frontend/svpp declare none), so SV vs regex is the whole
   available cross-family surface today — which is exactly why `.11d` must start by BUILDING the
   cross-family taint census rather than by generalising from one chain.
2. **What was MEASURED to place it in the ENGINE, not in `systemverilog.ebnf`?** That the eviction
   fires on rules whose taint is **inherited, not intrinsic**: `statement_or_null`,
   `statement`, `statement_item` and `statement_item_sv_2017` declare no predicate of their own, yet
   all four are stamped tainted and evicted at the same rate (114 each at n=6), because
   `predicate_evaluations()` is a whole-parse counter and any predicate anywhere in their subtree
   moves it. A grammar edit cannot fix a test that never looked at the grammar. The identical
   per-rule numbers under the `ident` and `lit` variants — chains that differ in whether their
   conditions reference an identifier at all — is the second half of that: the taint does not track
   what the rule actually read.
3. **What would have to be true for the routing to be WRONG, and was it checked?** It would be wrong
   if the evictions were driven by `systemverilog.ebnf`'s own predicate placement — i.e. if moving or
   deleting SV's predicates removed the degradation, making it a grammar-shaped defect. Partially
   checked and NOT fully closed: the `lit` variant removes every identifier-driven fact LOOKUP from
   the chain's conditions and changes nothing (same inserts, same 114 evictions, `facts_emitted`
   1128 in both), which rules out the chain's OWN predicates as the driver. ⚠️ **Honest limit:** it
   does not rule out SV's predicate surface as a whole, because the SV stdlib preload and the
   statement surface still emit facts throughout. A grammar with predicates but no mid-parse store
   writes has not been constructed, and that synthetic control — not another corpus run — is the
   cheapest thing `.11d` can do to make this routing airtight. The `parse_harness_semantic_suite`
   (TOOLBOX 1.8) already owns the isolating-grammar machinery for exactly that.

### `.11a` / `.11b` (routed by `.10`, evidence recorded here for completeness)

- **`.11a`** (four opentitan crossbars over a 60 s budget) is routed INSIDE this tree, not out — it
  is an SV-corpus performance row with a tool-pinned locus (`--dump-rule-call-counts` on
  `xbar_peri.sv`). It was **re-measured under `.3.12`**: still exactly 4 timeout rows, the same
  files, unchanged by the memo fix — so it is not a memo-caching defect wearing a performance mask,
  which is the reading that would have made this routing wrong.
- **`.11b`** (`cluster_rejects_valid.py` rebuilding `uvm-core` paths under `subs/`) is a
  repo-script path-convention defect, also routed inside this tree. It reproduces outside SV **by
  construction** — the same normalizer defect class was already measured in
  `adjudicate_external_corpus.py` (`.10`) and `corpus_rule_coverage.py` (`.7c`) — which is why it is
  filed as a convention defect with three known consumers rather than as an SV-corpus bug.

- Stressed well today: LRM-clause breadth (sv-tests), 30 years of real-world
  regression mess (verilator).
- Measured gaps: (1) no verification-class (UVM-scale) code in the bulk run
  (uvm-core vendored but outside `subs/`); (2) parse-level `must_reject`
  population ≈50 rows, accepts-invalid candidates just 6 — the negative axis

  — the biggest untapped stress reserve is already on disk; (4) slang/verible

## Acceptance Criteria (tree)

1. Fresh characterization at HEAD vintage + a complete adjudication manifest:
   every vendored case classified with a metadata/spec-derived expected verdict.
2. The parser matches ALL expected verdicts; exclusions named + justified in the
   tracked manifest; **zero unexplained divergences** ("flying colors", earned).
3. The graduation gate is standing, deterministic (pinned corpus commits), and
   wired into the SV family-status `Done` computation.
4. Full lockstep (books/LIVE/contract) and every landing leaf through the
   TOOLBOX acceptance checklist.
5. **(Amended 2026-07-22)** The corpus itself is proven **top of class**:
   the `.7` instrument reports **100% measured coverage of the parseable
   grammar surface per profile** (uncovered rules/clauses = 0 or
   N/A-with-cause), with keyed negatives present wherever the LRM defines
   parse-level illegality — the ADD-v1 suites vendored and adjudicated.

## ⭐ DIRECTOR DIRECTIVE (2026-07-25, session #206) — a STRICTNESS AXIS for the SV parser

Raised by the director while reviewing `.3.11`: *"I want the SV parser to be
flexible, strict-LRM compliance would mean hardcode, let's give us the possibility
to accept strictness and dialect-tolerance, so I would go for a switch."*

**⭐ SETTLED SAME SESSION, after the `.3.11` measurement was shown to the director:**
*"So, we will stick to strict-LRM compliance then, good I prefer that."* ⇒ the SV
parser is **STRICT-LRM BY DEFAULT** and the switch is **DEFERRED, not rejected**.
Banked as decision record
`docs/decisions/feedback_sv_strict_lrm_compliance_default.md` (layer C), which
carries the policy, the ⚠️ scope limit, the re-open trigger and the mechanism
constraints. The three constraints below stand as the design brief IF it re-opens.

**ACCEPTED as a direction, with three engineering constraints recorded so the
design does not start on the wrong foot.** No leaf opened yet — the design leaf
belongs to `LRM-GRAMMAR-FIDELITY` (which already owns cross-family fidelity
infrastructure) rather than to this corpus-graduation tree.

1. **⛔ Do NOT bootstrap the design from `.3.11`.** That case was measured to have
   **zero** real-world conflict (0 of 16,336 files write a spaced time literal;
   273 write it tight), so it needs no switch — it is a plain accepts-invalid bug.
   A general mechanism designed around a single non-contentious instance will be
   the wrong mechanism.
2. **⭐ The evidence base already exists and is measured: the accepts-invalid
   population — 21 rows (`sv_2017` lane) + 14 rows (`verilog_2005` lane) = 35.**
   Those are, by construction, every place PGEN currently accepts what the standard
   forbids. Sorting those 35 into *(a) genuine dialect tolerance the ecosystem
   relies on* vs *(b) plain over-acceptance bugs* is the real input to a strictness
   policy: bucket (a) is what a switch is FOR, bucket (b) should simply be fixed.
   That triage is a read-only leaf and should come first.
3. **⛔ TWO HARD CONSTRAINTS ON THE MECHANISM:**
   - **It must be EBNF-NATIVE.** `EBNF-SOURCE-OF-TRUTH` is a *mechanically
     enforced* doctrine (`scripts/check_doctrines.sh`: "no new out-of-band
     acceptance validator wired outside the EBNF"). A strictness switch bolted on
     as a runtime parser flag would fail that gate on the pre-commit hook. The
     existing `@profiles` annotation is the proof that an EBNF-native switch is
     achievable.
   - **It must be ORTHOGONAL to `@profiles`, not folded into it.** Profiles answer
     *which standard* (`sv_2017` / `sv_2023` / `verilog_2005`); strictness answers
     *how pedantically to enforce it*. Folding the second into the first gives a
     combinatorial explosion (`sv_2017_strict`, `sv_2017_lax`, … ×3) and would
     muddle a mechanism that is currently clean, gate-verified
     (`profile_orphans=0`) and load-bearing for two cert contracts.

**Recommended sequencing:** triage the 35 accepts-invalid rows into
dialect-tolerance vs bug (read-only) → design the orthogonal EBNF-native strictness
annotation against bucket (a) → implement → wire a gate that proves both settings
behave as declared. Fix `.3.11` strictly in the meantime; it is independent of all
of the above.

### `.13c.2x.10` — ✅ **CLOSED: the `fully_certified` claim is now VERIFIED AT HEAD** (was: the gate that proved it had never seen the parser in the tree) (**`done`**, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0278`, 2026-08-23; opened by a director question — *"is the SV parser fully certified now?"*)

- **WHAT THE LAST GREEN RUN SAID, and it is a real result**: `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate`,

  1. `systemverilog_recognized_cert_union_contract.json` pins
     `generated/systemverilog_parser.rs = cc874b60…`. The parser on disk is **`e53cb4a2…`**.
  2. Two more declared inputs moved: `grammar_wellformedness.rs` (`b6ed770f…` → `420ed130…`) and
     `stimuli_generator.rs` (`f5d12713…` → `9b5c9a70…`).
  3. **The gate has not been RUN since.** `rust/target/sv_cert_recognized_union_gate/summary.json`

     **2026-08-23 12:16**. The proof predates its own subject by over a day.
- ⭐ **THE GRAMMAR IS INNOCENT — this is codegen drift, not a language change.**
  `git log 767a1b37..HEAD -- grammars/systemverilog.ebnf` is **0 commits**. The parser moved because
  the engine-universal codegen moved under it on 2026-08-23 (`-0177` per-terminal layout guard,
  `-0178` comment-skip prefix guard, `-0179` the shared `RegexAtomEmitter` kernel). ⚠️ `-0177`
  explicitly measured `systemverilog` as regenerating BYTE-IDENTICALLY, so the mover is `-0178` or
  `-0179` and **which one is not yet attributed** — that attribution is part of this leaf.
- ⛔ **WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT, and this is the transferable part.** `BASELINE-IDENTITY` DID see the
  drift — it printed it — but by design staleness inside a derived commit budget is a **NOTE, not a
  failure**, so `check_doctrines.sh` reports ALL 25 PASS with the SV certificate claim resting on a
  parser that no longer exists. That is correct behaviour for a pre-commit enforcer (`.13c.2x.4`:
  a moved input must not block every commit) and it means **the freshness of a SIGNOFF claim needs a
  different tier from the freshness of a commit**. A release claim cannot rest on a NOTE.
- **WHAT THIS LEAF OWES**: re-run `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate` (~2 min/seed × 3 seeds × 4 union
  configs) against the parser actually in the tree, then either re-stamp on green or attribute the
  divergence on red; attribute which codegen commit moved the parser; and price a tier that re-runs
  the certificate proof whenever a pinned generated parser digest moves, so a signoff claim can never
  again be a day older than its subject.

#### (i) ATTRIBUTION — **`-0178` (`d1bfd17a`) MOVED THE PARSER**, read from the artifact, not inferred

- **THE QUESTION THIS LEAF OPENED**: `-0177` measured `systemverilog` as regenerating
  BYTE-IDENTICALLY, so the mover is `-0178` or `-0179` and *"which one is not yet attributed"*.
- ⛔ **ELIMINATION FROM THE COMMIT RECORDS WAS AVAILABLE AND IS NOT WHAT I USED.** `-0179`'s own
  subject says *"ZERO generated bytes"* and its body *"generated_reproducibility 11/11
  byte-identical, no parser moved"*; with `-0177` measured byte-identical that leaves `-0178` by
  elimination. ⚠️ But a recorded claim is exactly the evidence class this session has repeatedly
  found false, so it is used as CORROBORATION, never as the finding.
- ⭐⭐ **THE POSITIVE SIGNATURE, TWO-SIDED, READ OUT OF THE SHIPPED ARTIFACT.** `-0178` rewrote
  `allow_comment_skip` from an equality test over six spellings to a PREFIX test, and that
  expression is **EMITTED INTO the generated parser** — the generator's own unit test asserts it
  (`assert!(rendered_all.contains("allow_comment_skip"))`), so the artifact carries the vintage:

  | form | introduced / removed by | occurrences in `generated/systemverilog_parser.rs` |
  |---|---|---|
  | `expected != "/" && !expected.starts_with('#') && !expected.starts_with("//") && !expected.starts_with("/*")` | **ADDED** by `-0178` | **1** — line 1 435 762 |
  | `expected != "#" && expected != "//" && expected != "/*" && expected != "/**" && expected != "///" && expected != "/"` | **REMOVED** by `-0178` | **0** |

  ⇒ the post-`-0178` shape is PRESENT and the pre-`-0178` shape is ABSENT. The parser in the tree
  was emitted by a generator at or after `d1bfd17a`. ⭐ Two-sided on purpose: presence alone would
  not discriminate if both forms could coexist, and absence alone would not date the artifact.
- ⭐ **AND IT IS THE RIGHT KIND OF EVIDENCE FOR THIS QUESTION.** No regeneration was needed, no
  worktree, no 130 MB rebuild — the artifact was asked what vintage it is, rather than the commit
  log being asked what it should be. That is the same correction `.1a` made one tree over: **ask the
  instrument, never the record.**
- ⭐⭐ **AND THE SIGNATURE PROVES MOVEMENT, NOT MERELY VINTAGE — because the GATING was checked too.**
  `-0178`'s entire diff to `ast_based_generator.rs` is the expression text and nothing else: no

- ⭐⭐ **`-0179` IS EXCLUDED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY ITS OWN COMMIT MESSAGE.** It *does* touch

- ⚠️ **HONEST BOUND**: `-0177`'s byte-identity for `systemverilog` is still taken from its own

#### (iv) THE SIGNOFF TIER, PRICED (what this leaf owed, discharged as a DESIGN with numbers)

- **THE GAP, restated precisely**: `BASELINE-IDENTITY` treats a moved pinned input as a printed
  **NOTE** inside a derived commit budget. That is *correct* for a pre-commit enforcer — `.13c.2x.4`
  measured the alternative, where one comment line in the SV grammar blocked every commit in the
  repository. But it means **all 25 doctrines reported PASS while the SV certificate claim rested on
  a parser that no longer existed**. ⇒ *the freshness of a SIGNOFF claim needs a different tier from
  the freshness of a commit.*
- **THE DESIGN**: mark a baseline `signoff: true` and give the shared verifier a `--signoff` mode in
  which **any** moved pinned input on such a baseline is a HARD failure (exit 1), with no budget.
  It is invoked by the RELEASE lane, never by `.githooks/pre-commit`, so the pre-commit posture
  `.13c.2x.4` established is untouched.
- **PRICE, from this run's own numbers**: the check is a re-hash of 5 declared inputs — **~1 s**,
  the cost `BASELINE-IDENTITY` already pays every commit. The expensive part is only the REMEDY when
  it fires: **448 s** for this gate. ⇒ the tier costs essentially nothing until it has something to
  say, which is the property that makes a per-commit budget unnecessary at release time.

### ✅✅ `.13w` DISCHARGED — **46 of the 247 `unexplained_rejects_valid` rows are the parser's SOUND STORE GATE doing what the director-confirmed boundary demands, PROVEN PER ROW BY PARSING, and they leave the bar as `divergence:explained_store_gate` with their minimal prelude published; the bar falls 268 → 222 with ZERO parse verdicts moved; the same search REFUSED two rows and thereby found a grammar defect (`.3.29`); ADJUDICATOR tier, ZERO Rust / grammar / codegen / generated bytes** (2026-09-03, `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0346`)

**The question.** `SV-PARSE-STRICT.2` shipped the boundary the director confirmed on 2026-06-09: the parser
REJECTS a provably-undeclared type/nettype identifier at parse time and ACCEPTS when it cannot prove (an
unresolved wildcard import in scope). Every answer key in the corpus is derived from Annex A or from a tool's
verdict, and neither can express that boundary — the BNF has no notion of "declared" — so a single-file suite
test that uses a type it never declares is keyed `must_accept`, refused by design, and was being counted as a
defect. The `.13c.2`-era clustering of the 247 rows (163 signatures, largest cluster 7) had already shown the
population has no construct family to fix; `probe_fact_gates` on 8 suspect rows returned demanded-and-missing
`type_name` facts (`typedef_missing.sv → {'T'}`, `t_inst_paren_bad.v → {'sub'}`), which is the gate's signature.

**The discipline: nothing is relabelled by argument.** A row leaves the bar only when its OWN bytes, with a
minimal prelude of declarations prepended and nothing else changed, PARSE — through the dark-worklist search
(`adjudicate_dark_worklist.drive`/`minimize`, imported by path, never copied): harvest the names the parser
DEMANDED AND LACKED from its trace, declare them, iterate to a fixed point, minimise, publish the winning prelude
in the basis. Three soundness conditions keep a row in the bar even when that parse succeeds, each decided
mechanically and each with a RED arm: an **unresolved wildcard import** (the boundary says ACCEPT there, so a
rejection would be the gate being unsound — a `SV-PARSE-STRICT` defect, never an explanation), a package
**`export`**, and a name the **LRM predefines**.

- ⭐ **HOW IT WAS FOUND, AGAIN.** The local `sota-exit-gate` aggregate on `50a97d00c` (2026-09-30) refused `sv_parser_family_status_gate` on the SV formal-exhaustive-closure surface: the external-corpus triage read `parse_pass_total 10 / parse_fail_total 4` against the tracked `14 / 0`, the two UVM cases in both profiles rejected at `package uvm_pkg;` with `furthest_position=1016474` = `uvm_transaction.svh:443`. The one-line repro `class P #(type T=int); endclass typedef P #(int) T1; class C; const local T1 events = new("events"); endclass` fails on the shipped parser and the interpreter while `const T1 …` and `local T1 …` pass; the interpreter bisect over the 50 grammar commits since the gate's last green run (2026-08-24) lands on `e0a324964` (the Annex B reserved-word fix, 2026-09-04: with `new` reserved, `new("events")` no longer slips through `constant_expression` as a function call). All of it was already on file as `SVPP-EXPANSION.5`(d) — the director call of 2026-09-09, bisect and fix shape included — with the push lane as its fifth waiting surface (`-0028`).
- ⛔⛔ **WHY + WHERE, and the ruling.** Annex A A.1.9 gives the `const`-first class property only `const { class_item_qualifier } data_type const_identifier [ = constant_expression ] ;`, and `new(…)` is no `constant_expression`; the `local const …` order IS derivable through `data_declaration`'s `class_new` initializer — an asymmetry the standard carries and every simulator smooths over, while §8.19's prose reads "global constant class properties include an initial value as part of their declaration". The director's 2026-08-10 bounding ruling (`feedback_sv_strict_lrm_compliance_default`) puts the operative test FIRST — *does the change make the SV parser reject input the ecosystem actually writes?* — and this rejection took the whole UVM library and everything built on it. On 2026-10-01 the director, asked for the ruling a third time ("looks like you are stuck"), left the standing ruling to decide it: option (a).
- ✅ **FIX — GRAMMAR tier, one arm.** `class_property`'s const alternative reads `( assign ( class_new | constant_expression ) )?`, `class_new` first (`new` can never begin a `constant_expression` now, and a `constant_expression` can never begin with `new`); the typed shape keeps `{kind: "const", qualifiers, data_type, name, init}` with `init` the `class_new` object. Recorded as a named deviation in the SV book (`preprocess-parse-pipeline.md`'s UVM paragraph, the changelog) and in the contract's current-state note.

Its stop under the 2017 pipeline is `parameter int Q[$] = '{1, 2};` (`t_display_p_elab.v:37:20`) — an unsized (queue) dimension on a parameter, which 1800-2017 A.2.4 `param_assignment ::= parameter_identifier { unpacked_dimension } …` does not derive and 1800-2023's `{ variable_dimension }` does — and it PASSES under the `sv_2023` reading with no identity define (`.38`'s census row; the 2023 key already rules it `must_accept`).
- **The ask.** Re-read the row on the 2017 key as an EDITION CONTRAST (`.14b.1`'s shape: `must_reject` on the 2017 lane with both editions' productions cited, a `invalid_…_sv2017` / `control_…_sv2023` pin pair), drop the stale disposition, and re-derive the manifests, the re-adjudication and the tuple — each moved number named.
- ⛔ **RETRACTED (2026-10-02).** The file's own lines 35-37 read `` `ifndef VERILATOR `` / `// Generally not supported by others` / `parameter int Q[$] = '{1, 2};`: the stop sits INSIDE the branch the file selects on Verilator's identity macro, which is exactly what the disposition says (*"the portable branch the lane parses is … a non-standard construct"*). That the construct is 1800-2023's and parses under `sv_2023` is a second true fact about the same line, not a contradiction of the first; the 2017 key's `must_accept` is the driver's expectation WITH `VERILATOR` defined, where the line is skipped. Nothing to re-key. What went wrong: `.38`'s census printed the stop line and I read the line without opening the file around it.

##### ✅✅ `.43` — **`done`** 2026-10-03 (`PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0428`; GRAMMAR + FAMILY-COMPONENT + PINS + LANE + CEREMONY tier — release **`1.0.249`** / contract `1.0.249`, ledger **`SV-0134`**, schema 34 unchanged; opened 2026-10-02 by DIRECTOR DECISION, [[project_sv_opt_in_tolerance_profile]]) — **THE OPT-IN TOLERANCE PROFILE `sv_2023_tolerant`: `sv_2023` plus the four spellings `.41` ruled, and nothing else; the strict profiles unchanged — measured so on every lane, every AST and every parse-cost counter**
- **The order** (director, 2026-10-02, verbatim in the decision record): *"looks like we should carry an opt-in tolerance profile, so, let's go for it."* Scope fixed by the order: opt-in; the four spellings.
- **Design, chosen in execution** (each stated in the record as revisable):
  - **One profile, `sv_2023_tolerant`.** Its language is `sv_2023`'s plus four arms. Carried by the EXISTING `@profiles` directive: every list that names `sv_2023` gains `sv_2023_tolerant` (393 directives today: 263 `["sv_2017", "sv_2023"]` + 130 `["sv_2023"]`), a mechanical, script-made edit; the four arms live in rules gated `@profiles: ["sv_2023_tolerant"]` alone. ZERO engine bytes is the target — the first rung of the neutrality ladder; a `@profile_extends` directive is the named alternative, not built.
  - **The invariant, enforced:** for every `@profiles` list, `sv_2023 ∈ list ⇒ sv_2023_tolerant ∈ list` (a check wired to a gate that runs), and measured on the corpus as `sv_2023_only_pass = 0` against the tolerant reading.
  - **The four arms.** (e) `foreach ( array ( [ expression ] )+ [ loop_variables ] )` — selects before the loop-variable bracket; (f) `solve … before …;` admitted inside a braced `constraint_set`; (c) a `hierarchical_identifier` as a `cross_item`; (a) an optional `lifetime` in `task_prototype` / `function_prototype`. Each AST shape named and documented; each a new `kind`, so a consumer can tell a tolerated spelling from a standard one.
  - **The pins, two-sided:** the seven `.41` pins keep `REJECT` on `sv_2017,sv_2023`; four new rows pin `ACCEPT` on `sv_2023_tolerant` (the same text), and the controls gain the tolerant profile.
- **Plan.** `.43a` the grammar on a scratch copy, through the interpreter on the pins and on OpenTitan's seven packages' stops (no generated byte); `.43b` the release ceremony (lint, sample parity, certificate — the union gains the tolerant config so the new rules are witnessed —, closure, the three raw lanes unmoved by construction and measured, reproducibility, parse cost, umbrellas); `.43c` the tolerant READING of the pipeline lane and its census against `sv_2023` (`2023_only_pass` must be 0; the seven packages and their members are the expected gain — a prediction, to be replaced by the run's count); `.43d` the books and the contract (the profile list, the four spellings with the standard's rewrite, the AST kinds, "the default is strict").
- **Not in scope, stated.** No fifth spelling; no change to `sv_2017` / `sv_2023`; no redefinition of the primary reading or of the verdict-coverage tuple.

And the boundary: `binsof(cfg.a)` — a TWO-part name — parses under the tolerant profile (`bo1.sv`), because it is syntactically `cover_point_identifier . bin_identifier`; the syntax cannot tell a variable path from a bin reference, so the tolerance begins at the THIRD part.
  - **§19.6.1, both editions, prose and production.** 1800-2017 Syntax 19-4 `bins_expression ::= variable_identifier | cover_point_identifier [ . bin_identifier ]` (`docs/systemverilog/2017/txt/section-19-functional-coverage.txt:924-926`) and *"The binsof construct yields the bins of its expression, which can be either a coverage point (explicitly defined or implicitly defined for a single variable) or a coverage point bin"* (`:1048-1049`); 1800-2023 A.2.11 (`docs/systemverilog/2023/txt/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax.txt:1069-1071`) and the same sentence (`docs/systemverilog/2023/txt/section-19-functional-coverage.txt:1356-1357`). A hierarchical name is neither: no production derives the third part, and the clause names the two things the operator takes. The standard's own rewrite is the one `.41`(c) already gives: declare a coverpoint for the variable and name the coverpoint (OpenTitan's `cfg.vif.bat_disable` is the variable its cross covered implicitly; `cp_bat_disable_val: coverpoint cfg.vif.bat_disable;` and `binsof(cp_bat_disable_val)` is the LRM form).
